text: I have trouble sleeping, especially with waking up at 3 or 4 am and not being able to get back to sleep. There are things I don't like about it - it's so hard to open. When it's 3 am and you're trying not to wake up any more, wrestling with this plastic wrapped package is very irritating. I also hate the taste of stevia, so I really have to choke it down. However, very few sleep aids work for me. Sominex, Nyquil, etc make me very agitated instead of sedated, and my heart feels like it might pound my way out of my chest. Valerian is just as bad if not worse, kava doesn't do much for me. L-thianine (Suntheanine brand) works well to make me drowsy for bedtime, but I still wake up later. Dream water at first gave be really vivid dreams and my husband said I thrashed around a lot. That seems to have faded. It makes me fall asleep within 10 minutes or so, so it's really worth having around. If it's late, like 3 or 4 am and I need to wake up at 7, I drink 1/2 of a bottle. Nothing else shuts off my brain, and I'm still able to get up in am without feeling too drugged (not that I wouldn't like to roll over again and keep sleeping). Once I'm vertical, I'm just fine. The more I use it the less it seems to work, but as long as I don't use it every day, it's good.

title: Great hot water treatment for general soreness
text:
I’ve been experiencing more and more leg soreness after long runs, particularly in my quads. I’ve tried different hot and cold therapies, but true to my Asian roots, decided that it was finally time to try using a rubber water bag. Here are some thoughts:

• Size/Design: The water bag is appropriately-sized to cover a large area of the body. I have a fairly large hot water kettle that I use for this bag (about one kettle fills one water bag). The exterior cloth is both comfortable and aesthetically pleasing. I also appreciate the buttons, as it allows me to peel the cloth bag to avoid getting the cloth wet when pouring the hot water into or out of the bag.

• Ease of Use and Effectiveness: As noted, this holds a good amount of water. The rubber design is nice and flexible, allowing for good contortion to the body. I actually don’t think you have to fill the water all the way, as it helps to “slosh” the water a bit to get a bit more heat. Be careful at first, however, as I found that the water bag was a bit too hot in the first few minutes of use. It may be good to take some breaks here and there, as I had some noticeable red marks on my quads afterwards. Overall, I found that the bag stayed well-heated for over an hour (if not closer to one and half hours).

• Leakage: This is well-made with a screwable top that prevents water from leaking out.

In summary, I’m happy with rubber water bag and will continue to use this to treat general soreness. My only concern is that this water bag can get a tad hot in the beginning and may leave some redness, but as long as you are cognizant of these factors then I think this is a great addition to the home. Recommend!

This one is TERRIFIC. Seals tight so no leakage. The cover is super soft and comes off so it can be washed and placed back on easily. text:
We've got plenty of heating pads, but I think a hot-water-bottle has its place in a home.
I was attracted to the pretty cover and it is pretty and soft. Fits the bottle well, has a snapped section to hold it in place near the neck.
Basic red hot water bottle with screw cap. (I shook it full of water upside down... squeezed it... no leaking)

I suspect, also because of the pretty cover, the hot tap water I used did not provide the kind of "warmth" I was seeking. Next, I will microwave the water and I suspect, that will be sufficient to really warm it to "feels good soothing".

While I am happy to have a working hot-water-bottle for home, it won't be my first choice above one of our heating pads (unless the power goes out). Once filled with water, it is heavy - doesn't lay flat and using it on my my belly felt heavy and I didn't get as good coverage as the heating pad.

IF you're in the market for one, I DO recommend this one.

title: Essential Companion!  Excellent kit!
text:
UPDATE 4/4/17: This Key Chain has been hanging on the outside of my purse/bag every day since I purchased it back in August 2015! (It currently holds 7-2ml and 2-1ml bottles. See pics of well-loved pouch.) I still absolutely love it. It has held up well, no busted seams or over-stretched elastic.

I see where some reviewers are not happy. I wonder if this is due to a product change or purchased from a different seller than I did. Mine came from Everything Essential [[ASIN:B013GKMF7G Stylish Essential Oil Key Chain with 8 5/8 Dram (2 ml) Vials and Blank Labels - Fits Easily in a Purse or Makeup Bag - Carry Your Favorite Essential Oils Everywhere You Go! (Black/White Windsor)]]

Of note, my order contained only the case and eight 2ml brown bottles. No pipettes, labels, or removal tool... AND YET! I would buy it again for the current $12.95 price. I am in no way related to the seller - I just love this product.

ORIGINAL: Dang, I love this thing!
It comes with eight amber 2ml (5/8ths) dram glass bottles with black lids. Each with a small white lid label that can be applied.

Outside:
The outside is made of cloth and has a soft canvas feel. I received the blue/white windsor colored case. It is a very dark blue, nearly black.
A smooth-gliding black zipper wraps around three sides. It is attached to an approx 2" silver carabiner hook. The set up feels very sturdy.

Inside:
The inside has a dark blue background with white polka dots. Very cute! This is where there is eight black elastic loops for securing oil vials. Each 3/4" width elastic loop easily holds from 1ml (1/4 dram, 7/8") bottles *up to* 5ml (1.5"), too!
(Dram = 3.7ml, but a dram bottle is often called a 5ml.)
Further, the vials are protected from the zipper with a piece of soft piping that runs the full zipper length! This is a really nice extra feature!

I currently have this stocked with my favorite go-to oils and have it clipped to my bag. It is lightweight and much easier to haul around than a baggie or small satchel. I love that my bottles are secured, but still easy to access.

***Note: One trick I have found is to slide the bottles into the case elastic lid first. This prevents the elastic from hanging on the bottle lid.***

It is made in China.

title: Fantastic Product, Great for Stretching Out The Back!!
text:
Awesome traction pillow. I have been using this a lot for the last couple days and I have felt a lot different in the back of neck and upper back. I have chronic neck and back pain for the last 10 years. I am so sick of the pain. It was recommended to me to try this.

Where the pain in back originates from there is a lot of stretch feelings. It feels like that support in my neck from the pillow has help with the pain. Also in my upper neck where my neck kind of sits forward all the time. It created my spine to slightly curve in my neck. So I am wishing over time that it will help significantly with the long term pain.

The pillow is a good quality and very durable. It inflates and deflated easily. The pump is like the blood pressure arm bands at the hospital. There is a ball on the end with a twist relief valve. Twisting it all the way down allows it to pump up and twisting it up releases the air. Great product. Very well done.

I received this item at a significant discount. My opinion expressed is provided at my own discretion and is a direct reflection of my personal experience.

title: Neck felt better after using the very first time
text: I received the Cervical Neck Traction Device by NONPAREIL recently and am very pleased with the device. I like that it is easy to use. I had never used one of these contraptions before so I was very glad that it comes with printed directions. However I do wish the directions were printed in a larger font as I had to use a magnifying glass to read them. Once I did read the directions it was easy to proceed.  It feels a bit strange at first as it inflates until you get used to it but it is in no way unpleasant. Once it’s fully inflated it is Wow!” It relieves the tension I carry in my neck and I feel it is very much helping my posture to change (for the better). The fabric is soft and comfortable. The cervical neck traction device is adjustable and so relaxing as I am wearing it. It’s also amazing when I finish using the device and take it off that my neck just feels fantastic and I walk taller with a definite improvement in posture, which for me is huge. It makes my neck feel good and because it causes my neck and spine to align pain is greatly diminished and I am looking forward to greater results as I continue using it regularly. As they say practice makes perfect. The only concern I do have is that the little blue adjust valve is made of plastic and seems somewhat flimsy. I am hopeful it will stand up to continued use. I'm blessed to be able to share the Cervical Neck Traction Device by NONPAREIL has worked for me.

text: Though I have not yet inserted this particular filter, I have used them in the past and am very pleased with them.  Easy to change with the upgraded slide bars.

title: Photo misleading
text:
AS others said the photo of the filter is misleading. It shows the filter inside the shell, this is not the case. The shipping was fast and I received two filters (I have a split AC system so I needed two) nicely packaged. However it is not "just slide in" you need to place the filter in the shell of your previous filter. For me this is much better than dealing with an accordion style filter where you have to use four combs and have enough dexterity to figure it all out in the dark tight space of the attic. I was surprised to learn about this style of filters as I am a new home owner who is used to 3M filters from your local Target store.
This does the trick and it is rated for a year so I'll deal with it again next year. So far so good.

title: Seems to work great
text: Product delivered didn't look anything like the picture but fit inside the old Spacegard shell with no problem. The filter is a rigid, freestanding unit shaped like a box fan that fits perfectly inside the existing Spacegard shell after the old filter and pleat combs are removed. Be sure to check your airflow direction arrows before buttoning up the system.  Very handy not having to sit down and fit each pleat spacer any more.  Seems to have good fit inside the duct without needing additional insulation like the original filters.  I didn't think $30 each was bad considering I was buying the original filters for $40 from an HVAC company and installing them myself.  The original filters also had a problem with spreading fine white dust throughout the house...see if the new filters have the same problem.

title: NOT a replacement filter -review update

I had previously bought the Honeywell RP2200, which was a COMPLETE replacement filter, and threw out the combs & case. without the case it is too small and just flops around in the opening.
Not worth shipping back, I'll just have to bite the bullet and order the honeywell RP2200's

"Hello Tim this product is made to be used with the original space guard
enclosure not a Honeywell. These are two totally different enclosures and

title: Small but festive
text: These Halloween decorations are okay, but they are smaller than I expected. It's enough to decorate an entry way or one wall or snacks table but that's about all. The shaped Mylar balloons in particular were quite little.  I got a spider (8" tall x 14" from leg tip to leg tip when deflated), a ghost with  pumpkin (a total of 11" x 13" with a 8" x 8" pumpkin and a 5" x " ghost), and 3 16" circular balloons (2 that are orange and say "Happy Halloween" with cute Halloween pictures, one black with a bloody skeleton that says "spooky"). So I got more than the 3 Mylar balloons promised in the product description, but they were much smaller than the product description indicated. I got 16 latex balloons, 4 each of white with a ghost face, orange with a scary jack o lantern face, black with a red scary face and clear with orange and black confetti. They look good but smell very strongly of turpentine. I got 6 tissue paper pom poms (some assembly required) with an 8" diameter. 2 each in orange black and white. There were also kits to make 12" long black and orange tissue paper tassels. Lastly there is a set of cardstock cutouts with images that spell out "Happy Halloween" and some black ribbon to string them on. Overall the decorations look cute, but honestly I was hoping for something better at this price.

title: Some Crafting Skills Required.
text: This kit comes with a lot of stuff for the money - and the balloons are fabulous - I would get this for them alone. Helium was used for the full effect seen here (not included with the kit but worth it.)  The other things in the listing (garlands, pom-poms, and banner) do take a little work.  The pom-poms ARE manageable but they take A LOT of time and care to spread them all out and it is tricky to do without ripping them. If you get them please note the instructions DO NOT say to leave the ribbon on. YOU NEED TO LEAVE THE RIBBON ON or it will never work.  Even after figuring this out (which took longer than I’d care to admit) I'll be honest after ripping one beyond salvage and the time spent on the second one I gave up with those.  The same goes for the garlands- I have zero crafting skills and didn't even attempt them (but that's on me).  The banner comes as separate letters and one very useful extra was the plastic needle to help thread them.  Made life much easier.  I put them on one long string (provided) - but did have to take them off and rearrange them - because I had the words backwards the first try. (Totally my fault and didn't even realize until the hubby pointed it out).  Overall I would say if you are crafty you will get a fabulous effect for the money.  For me - as I said the balloons alone were well worth the cost (even after adding in the cost for the helium tank).

title: A lot of work to put things together, only OK in the end
text:
I got these small decoration to put around an apartment. There's quite a bit of assembly required. The Happy Halloween banner has to have a cord threaded through each letter (two holes each), the pom-poms are very thin tissue paper that needs to be very carefully separated and rolled and tied, and the white orange and black decorations that need to be carefully teased into balls. It takes a lot of work to do all of this; it has to be slow because the paper's so thin.

The balloons are generally nice. There's one with confetti where the confetti is quite dull and the balloon somewhat milky, so the effect is pretty poor. In any case the confetti just sinks to the bottom of the balloon. One popped and made a mess.

The Mylar balloons are fine. There was no straw or anything to blow them up with it, so that was frustrating. I suppose getting some helium would have made this all easier as it's hard to mount a balloon when it wants to fall down. The smaller ones have long bits sticking out the bottom that look a little random.

Overall it took a few hours to make some mediocre decorations and I didn't really find this worth it.

title: @8 grams per serving. Bovine, Marine, Chicken, Eggshell provides types 1, 2, 3, 5, & 10
text:
It's fine. I have my preferences over this. This is a nice blend of various collagen sources (bovine, marine, poultry, eggshell) and therefore a wider degree of collagen types (1, 2, 3, 5, 10). Hence the elevated price tag (I don't rate on price, but I will comment that it should be compared to others of this ilk. It is with similar price range). Some sources are more expensive. Some sources don't require as much to be effective. Ie, bovine is cheapest, but needs more, marine is usually most expensive yet needs a lot less. This has a good amount, well fair amount, per serving at about 8 grams of collagen peptides (hydrolyzed- meaning it is broken down to readily absorbable, easily digestible form, and it mixes in hot or cold without gelling).

Multi forms can impart a slight smell and flavor. I think the ones that use eggshell tend to have a little extra aroma. May disappear depending on what it is being used in. Or might be noticeable. Not a big fan of it in my plain black unsweetened coffee, but is totally fine in a smoothie, or when I have a coffee that I doctor up with cream and flavor syrup. I dont fault the brand, as it is merely a facet of the composition. I will always used collagen, often single source, but will pepper in multi source as I see fit.

This is a perfectly fine product. Though I recommend that they actually include a picture of the nutritional information. We dont need to see half a dozen pictures of people drinking it. Let us know what is in it. Had I been shopping around for it, I would have passed this over for a listing that tells me all that I am getting.

Though I am pleased to see this:
"If you’re not 100% satisfied with your purchase, we’ll issue you a refund."

title: Cute & Nice Controls, Just Didn’t Make Much of a Difference on My Lashes
text:
This comes in an outer product box - There’s a cardboard sleeve, and a box slides out from the sleeve. It is made in China. It comes with a little information pamphlet, which I always appreciate since things like that since it seems like so often they aren’t included in things!

It says that it has a temperature display, ceramic heating, four-gear temperature is optional, intelligent temperature control, and dynamic curling.

The charging cord is underneath the plastic shelf in the box holding the eyelash curler.

It has a nice look to it. It is lightweight. The cap is on good. It isn’t going to fall off easily.

The on/off button is the long gold button (see photos). To turn it on, you hold the on/off button down for a few seconds. Then you will see a temperature on the LCD screen. There’s 4 different temperatures you can set it to - 60C, 70C, 80C, and 90C (which is 140F, 158F, 176F, and 194F). To set the temperature you want you just hit the on/off button until it changes to the temperature you want. To turn it off you just hold down the on/off button for a couple seconds. I noticed when I turned it off on a certain temperature, when I would turn it back on it would still be at that temperature. So it’s nice you don’t have to keep setting it to the temperature you want.

The battery display is to the right of the temperature. It’s nice that you can see how much battery you have left. Out of the box I was able to use it without charging it first. It had 2 bars.

The pamphlet says that the curler will shut down automatically after 10 minutes of use. That’s nice in case you forget to turn it off yourself.

This is NOT waterproof so you can NOT use water to clean it. The pamphlet says, “If it is necessary to clean the brush head, please clean with cleaning brush and then wipe with flannel cloth. Do not wash with water.” It also says that you can “NOT wash it with water, alcohol, detergent, mercury, alkaline, or acidic products.”

Even on the lowest heat setting, 60 C (140 F), it feels pretty darn hot. I wasn’t too sure how comfortable I felt holding something so hot against my eye like that. I used it how it described but I didn’t notice a huge difference. They did get a little curl, but it wasn’t much. It just kind of pushed them up a little and they stayed there. tried it quite a few more times and just never noticed it doing too much. Unfortunately, it wasn’t enough of a difference for me to want to go through the process of using it.

Overall, this isn’t for me. I’m not sure if it’s me not doing something right, my lashes, or something else, but the little lift that this gave wasn’t enough of a difference to make it worth the hassle of using it. Maybe I needed to use a higher heat setting, but 60C felt pretty darn hot to me, and I didn’t feel comfortable going any hotter and having to hold it so close to my eye. So, it’s just a no for me. I give it 3 stars for the curler itself - it’s nice, looks nice, feels durable - and the controls - I like how it has an LCD screen, I like that it shows battery display, and I like that it turns off automatically after 10 minutes of use. I just didn’t like the results I got, so I took off 2 stars for that. So I give it 3 stars.

Random Info in Case Anyone Wants to Know:
Battery Capacity: 400 mAH
Maximum Power: <2.5W
Charging Time: 1.5H
Product Size: 133*19mm
Charging Voltage: DC/5V
Working Voltage: DC/3.7V
Working Current: 100-600 mA
Net Weight: 29g

text:
No need for too many words here, just look at the before and after pictures and see!

Sorry for sharing my dirty laundry with you but this is the best way to show you how impress I am with this product. Granted that you still have to do some work depending on the stain and how stubborn they are. Note also that this product will not make your old things look brand new again, but it did cut down my cleaning time by almost 75 percent of time. The city I live in have very, very hard water as you can see from my shower door and glass. I do not have a water softener and I am having to clean out my showers at least once every 2 weeks (I know, I should do it more often). It used to take me at least 20 minutes each time but now with the help of this GreenFist product, I am down to about 5 minutes scrubbing and cleaning. Depending how stubborn the stains are, for me I just spray this all purpose cleaner on the glass door and showers for about 5 minutes, then just scrub a few times with a wet sponge as I wipe and the result is shown in the after pictures above. For the grouts I spray and left it there for about 30 minutes, it's a lot better but may need to re-apply again at least one more time to get the stain out completely. Also may need to scrub more with the grouts than with glass door but not as much as I used to.

Of course, there are other stronger products out there to do the job but I just did not feel using Chemicals is worth the trouble. This product is Eco-friendly and biodegradable, a lot safer to use than other products using Chemicals. Also, the orange smell from this product is a lot easier to work with in a closed or small environment like your shower or bathroom. I used to get a headache from using other stronger product within minutes but not with this product.

Overall, I am very impress with this product. Tremendously cut down my shower cleaning time and safer to use. The orange smell from this product is very pleasant. It may not get all the stain out completely the first try but the result did impressed me, I believe by using this product a few more times, the lime scale will not be as stubborn as it used to be so I will be using this product more often from now on. Great and Eco-friendly product!

title: Works for me...
text:
I find cleaning products, in general, a gigantic, dollar-sucking hassle. If we we all go along with a custom cleaning product for everything we clean around our homes - we’d need to make serious room for grout cleaner, toilet cleaner, surface cleaner, etc., etc., There’s a “best” in class cleaning product for just about everything - if that’s what we choose to believe. I gravitate to products like this hydrogen peroxide to take care of my cleaning needs.

HP is a known chemical that comes with no surprises. It cleans and disinfects quite well given the chance. I read through a few reviews and found some to be a little harsh on the price. It doesn’t surprise me that it’s $25. for the gallon (where’d the $40. price come from?). Buying ANY liquid online and having it shipped is going to cost extra. It’s heavy and it could leak, so packaging is important. It’s pretty cheap when buying it in person, but through the web - there’s ALWAYS a markup. It’s a given.

The GreenFist product has worked well for me in the applications I’ve tried it on. But my favorite “before and after” was on the cream colored grout in my guest bathroom. I had a couple of nieces living with me for a few years and they managed to make some sections of the grout go a yucky brown. My niece took a crack at it with grout cleaner. No improvement. I tried the same cleaner with a serious scrub brush and a lot more shoulder into it. No progress. I used this hydrogen peroxide with a wash cloth and not much muscle and the brown was gone in a minute (with an extra few minutes of drying time). There was no “film” on the floor from the grout cleaner I had to deal with the first go arounds. It worked.

This is the type of cleaning solution that works great for me - it’s versatile and has no scary chemistry in it. The HP emits a nice orange scent as I use it, not the smell of serious chemicals. It’s perfect for me. Recommend!

title: I Shampooed A Dirty Nubuck Leather Boot Using This & It Delivered
text: Knowing that peroxide is akin to bleach I decided to take a chance and generously spray a light tan colored nubuck western boot with this.  The boot had some dirt and water stains and I was curious if this would do something better than Lincoln Easy Cleaner for suede and nubuck leathers.  Importantly I did not leave it on longer than five minutes and then doused it again and used a brass brush (the right abrasiveness because brass is softer than steel and has finer tines).  Brushing with the brass brush quite aggressively seemed to get results but I wouldn't know until the leather dried and lightened up (anything wet makes nubuck darker).  I am glad to say it did a good job removing dirt and water spotting.  I rinsed the boot thoroughly to wash away both the dirt and the peroxide.  Then I dried overnight on the famous PEET BOOT DRYER.  Come morning it looked good but a little dry.  I was please because it looked clean and even if a bit dry.  To finish it I gave it a good finishing treatment of delicate cream which is something that replinishes moisture but when it dries to the touch the leather comes back lighter as  in this  case the original color.  After I was sure it was dry it looked perfect and I sealed it with Scotchgard for suede.  This delivered for me in this use.  You just need to remember this can change the color of some leathers just like bleach on fabric.  I wouldn't advise leaving it on to dry.  Nope, apply it, agitate according to the leather,  wash off, and dry very slowly.  Treat leather with appropriate conditioning then seal the deal with invisible Scotchgard.

title: Works ok when plugged in.  Definitely not "rechargeable" though.
text:
These work ok. They put out a decent amount of heat, but not so much as to be uncomfortably hot, which is important since there is no way to adjust the heat setting (aside from unplugging them). Together the pair consumes ~8.5 watts of power total at 5 volts. (See the photo of the USB power meter that I uploaded.)

I also uploaded a photo from a thermal camera showing exactly where the heating element is within the insole. The heat is produced in a thin band/loop and is not as evenly distributed as the seller's photos imply. But in practice you can't really tell just how localized the heat is -- it feels more spread-out when it's worn inside a shoe.

Lastly, I don't know why the seller calls them "rechargeable", as it's a completely untrue/misleading label (although this seems to be a common claim among sellers of similar heated insoles on Amazon, no matter how untrue). They have to be plugged into a USB port to produce heat, and after they're unplugged the heat doesn't last for any significant amount of time. So if you want to use these while on-the-go and not be tethered to a wall power adapter, a simple approach is to have a USB battery power bank in your pocket and then run the wires up your pant legs to plug into the power bank. Voila.

In the title it says "Winter hunting skiing fishing hiking". I "charged" them and by the time I walked from the bedroom to the kitchen (the kitchen is in the same small house, not in another town) not only were they no longer warm they felt cold. Maybe the author of the description goes fishing in a tank next to the computer indoors but most people take the item description to mean they will keep your feet warm while you hunt and fish etc. outdoors. I don't hike or ski. Do you guys carry USB battery packs or maybe a generator on the slopes? All of that being said I can put them in bedroom slippers and sit at the computer with them plugged into the computer and have warm feet but I won't be walking around with wires coming out of my shoes plugged into a battery in my pocket. I would not have purchased them had I known. If you want warm feet outside warming your shoes and socks with a blow dryer before you put them on would likely work as well.

I can easily reach into my pocket to turn the power to the liners on and off as needed for heat. The Y-shaped cord that comes with the liners is easily long enough to reach from my pocket into my pants and down my legs to plug into the short cord attached to the liners. I stitched a small loop of waistband elastic to the inside of my boots in a location where the cord would not bother me. It holds the end of the cord attached to the liners to keep the plug in place and make it easier to unplug the long cord from the liners to take my boots off. I can slip the plug out of the elastic if needed. I was so happy with them that bought a second pair of liners for my big snow boots because they are so affordable and so I don't risk damaging them regularly transferring them from one set of boots to another. It's nice to be able to power them with something I can use for other devices, too.

title: Good Monitor
text:
The pads work as expected.

Kerr Medical shipped fully assembled. All I had to do was add three C batteries to the alarm and program the alarm to recognize the pads.

Programming was just pressing a pin into the back of the alarm until two LED lights lit up in the alarm, then sit on - and get off of the pads, then press the pin into the back one time to finish.

The plastic pads make a little stiff plastic "crinkle" noise if they are not under a mattress or couch cushion. This draws attention of my senior Mom and can lead to repetitive questions, or removal if I'm not watching.

The alarm is made for wall mounting or setting on something. My preference is slipping it into a front pants pocket. The alarm is larger and heavier than a wallet but it works ok for me and I wear loose fit jeans. If it goes off, I just reach into the pocket and reset the chime.

When Mom is on the couch I may be at the computer in front of her on the floor. When the couch (chair pad) alarm goes off, she is typically already on her feet and stepping away.

Left on her own she would go onto the porch in summer heat, so this is just adequate warning. With her fall risk I don't know if another product would alert me faster or physically impede her (which I really don't want to do).

The directions (mention) imply that this also works with "Cordless Floor Mat", "Cordless Nurse" call button and "Cordless motion sensor".

The "Low volume" is not disruptive, about as loud as a typical cell phone ring.

This may be like the [[ASIN:B0043RFKME Bed Alarm and Bed Pad (Cord Free)]] if it uses the 433-EC alarm, but this includes a chair pad (see their reviews for more feedback). One of those reviews mentions a power plug adapter - but I did not receive one for this product.

title: Excellent product, does the job. Gives me reassurance and freedom. Could be improved.
text:
Purchased this for use in the home with my mother who is at risk of falling. I use the bed alarm and it functions well. If you are in a similar situation this product will allow you to go to sleep or go about your day confident that your loved one will not get up without you knowing.

I place the sensor pad on the bed beneath her shoulders so I know when she's sitting up. This gives me plenty of time to get to her before she tries to get up on her own. I place it underneath the bed sheet and bed pad used for toileting. Check the position of the pad each time you make the bed to make sure it hasn't slipped. It is very effective and has not failed me as long as the sensor pad is positioned correctly. I am running through the batteries, so will purchase the AC adaptor for use at night.

If I were to improve this product:
1) Make more volume levels. The lowest is still loud enough to travel through walls. It is important, for the person's dignity, for them not to feel so monitored. To keep from bolting out of bed at night I have put a piece of duct tape over the speaker, and sometimes put it under the covers with me.
2) Make the alarm unit lighter and smaller so it can be worn or easily carried in a pocket.
3) Make a variety of alert sounds that don't sound like alarms. Even the chime sounds alarmy.
4) Make it rechargeable.
5) Make the resetting of the alarm unit more obvious.

Note: I do not use the chair pad for a variety of reasons. For the person's dignity, the pad should be camouflaged. That is difficult when she's sitting on a couch. She moves around from couches to chairs several times during the day and its not practical to try to position the sensor on every one or to run around putting it down before she sits (re: dignity). I keep the chair pad in case we get to the point where she is in a wheelchair during the day. Right now she's using a walker.

Note: I purchased this on my husband's amazon account therefore this review will not show up as a verified purchase, but this is the unit I purchased here on Amazon.

On the hood I noticed that the little bit of bird droppings on the vehicle just weren’t breaking down as well as with other products. Additionally after the wash there were two big streaks of dust that had become more tacky and clung to the clear coat. I used on another vehicle that is garaged and not a daily driver that gets a weekly wash and the soap did well but the car didn’t really have anything on it so it is hard to mess that up. Because of the results I had and the price of this soap I do not think it is a very good deal for the price. title: great product especially for tall people
text: We are using the changing bathing table combo for 5 weeks now. We really like it. We were not really convinced when it arrived and we put it together. However, after 5 weeks of intensive use with our newborn, we both think it is great. The working height is very convenient. I am 5-8 and my husband is taller. Maybe for very short people the table is too high. We really like that you can have anything you might need for changing and bathing easily accessible on the open shelves and in the different compartments. The changing table surface is soft enough and easy to clean for those little accidents that happen during changing. The tub is great also. However we bought a little insert to rest the baby on while it is bathed, that is more comfy and adjusts to the babies body. The insert looks like a miniature sun bathing chair. The water drainage works great. The tub is easy to clean. I also like that the system is highly mobile. So you can change its location easily. Just roll it around. My sister used it for her two year old today. And the changing table even worked for the bigger infant. She even fell asleep on it, so I assume it was comfy for her. I would totally recommend this product for a friend.

The piece was impossible to assemble. The Apple Health connection was important to me, though, so at first I bought a different scale (the Easy Home bluetooth body fat scale), but I did not like that one for several reasons. So, I returned that scale and took a chance with this Yunmai scale and could not be happier! It DOES sync with the Apple health kit and my weight uploads automatically to Myfitnesspal!! The app that goes with the scale is great too. I love that you can use this scale without the app (i.e. a guest could use your scale to get his/her weight just by stepping on the scale). This differs from the Easy Home scale; for that scale you need to use the app and have a profile created to get any measurements. Also (and I know that this applies to very few people!), I was delighted to find that I can not only weigh my cat on this scale, but could set up a profile for her on the app to keep track of her weight over time! I have to carefully monitor my cat's weight due to a medical condition, and I was disappointed to discover that the Easy Home scale would not work to weigh her. Finally, the shipping was super fast and the packaging that the scale came in was superb! Buy this scale - you will love it! :)

In answer to the complaint that the scale was only reporting weight: either (1) you don't have your phone app open, (2) your scale batteries are already needing changing, (3) your smartphone maybe has an old version of Bluetooth? In answer to the complaint about the feet for carpet not helping: Maybe "carpet" in China means a thin throw rug as opposed to a heavy rug stapled over a piece of foam? All of the features worked for me. But consider the sparse instructions in non-native English (but not too bad). The provided batteries were weak in approximately 4 weeks. It was easy to not install the batteries firmly aligned and in-place. The good news is that if you use your common sense, the scale works well and is a good value compared to more expensive alternatives.

title: Genuinely Fantastic; coming from me, that says a lot.
text:
We all have smelled them - those horribly stinky
, nasty air freshening [sic - as in sick smelling] agents that do far more vile olfactory offense than any odor they could’ve possibly been trying to cover up. This is not one of those. Quite the opposite.
I had forgotten actually that we had put one of these in our car, a car that routinely hauls our two big, outdoors loving dogs with all the - um - scents as evidence of the trouble they’ve been up to that day. Throw in a smoking husband, and, well... ..so I get in the car and drive the 20 miles to the nearest grocery store and just before I get out of the car I notice it. Cologne, just a hint of it. Smells good. I wonder to myself what new cologne he has bought, wanting some myself. Kid you not. Did my shopping, got back in the car and smelled it more clearly this time, unmistakably masculine, clean. It had to be cologne; it was that same light tinge of change in smell that you would get from something clean and fresh. Think rubbing alcohol - you catch a whiff and it carries with you for the moment but is light and clean enough that it does t smell sticky or nasty. Just what is this cologne I wonder again to myself. Right about then I realized I should plug my phone in and look down to grab my lightning cord, and then I see it. The new Glade car air freshener, plugged in to the car’s lighter assembly.
Needless to say I am a now a big fan. And you will be too, as soon as you listen to me and go click on this scent - the New Car smell - and nab the device that diffuses the smell. Ordered us a cigarette lighter adapter that gives you two USB ports and replicates the lighter port for use with the diffuser, about $9-10 here on Amazon. Recommend one of those if you charge your phone in the car (who doesn’t) and can’t afford to lose your charger.

First, I would spray a light coat over the bread and then lightly butter the bread before popping it into the oven.  Voila!  Full flavor with minimum work.  I also used a lot of it up simply pouring it into soups, stews, chili - basically anywhere that garlic worked for me.  I sprayed it on roasts and chicken before slow-roasting them and poured it into my ground beef when I was browning it for spaghetti sauce or Mexican dishes. title: Cuts close without irritation
text:
I know this is technically a men's razor, but I'm a woman and I use it on my legs. I've tried a few different electric razors and I've noticed that men's razors tend to work better and cost less.

I'm not going to try to claim that it works as well as using a regular straight razor, but this one might actually provide the closest shave out of any electric razor I have tried, including more well known name brand razors for both men or women. It also does not irritate my skin at all, which is a big deal because I have very sensitive skin that gets razor burn from everything.

Two bonuses that aren't necessary, but are very nice to have: 1) The meter that tells you how much battery life is left and 2) a cord that actually comes with an outlet adapter. Many of them only come with a USB cord, no adapter.

And I really appreciate that it came with a replacement blade.

I can't help you if you're looking for info on how it cuts beard hair, but it's had pretty solid results for me.

title: (Almost) Exactly What I Needed
text:
I don't know about you guys, but finding a comfortable chair at a coffee shop to sit on for a couple of hours is more difficult than it appears. Especially for someone like me who...ahem...doesn't have much built-in cushion.

I've heard of the Purple brand before and saw commercials for them. As usual, I read into the comments here on Amazon to see what other people said about the product. I am one of those consumers that are willing to spend more for a quality product.

The product itself is as advertised as far as the comfort. Almost any surface you place this cushion becomes 10x more comfortable. I have not had the cushion collapse and not bounce back into shape. For reference, I'm 5'2" and 140lbs.

I also appreciate that it comes with a washable 'pillow-case' so I can sanitize it as needed. One side of the cloth case also has a rubber-like texture which helps anchor the cushion to whatever surface you place it on. No slip and sliding for this!

My only one-star deduction is that it's not the MOST portable. Though the exterior sleeve does have handles on two sides, the cushion tends to flop around when holding one. It doesn't seem to be advisable to fold it in half to make it smaller. I have to transport in in a large tote bag or backpack. I think this is the main reason I've also misplaced and lost it at least once. I've yet to figure out how best to bring this cushion around.

title: Worth getting addicted to...especially if you like really Dark Chocolate
text:
I saw the words "Dark Chocolate" and I lit up. For years now we have been enjoying the lower sugar and positive effects of dark chocolate, braving all the way up to a smooth and cool 90% cocoa -- That's right up there with baking chocolate. I didn't let myself expect much from a commercially made probiotic, and maybe that has to do with my happy surprise. But let me start with the fact that the chocolate is 64% cocoa! Not bad, not bad at all for dark chocolate lovers.

They are the size of a rounded quarter and have a firmness that allows them to be savored - they melt just like a piece of chocolate would. If you are a dark chocolate lover you will appreciate the slight tang and less syrupy sweetness that accompanies milk chocolate. These are really pleasing and they tout that their flora survives our stomach acid 100X better! It took me 4 days, to notice the shift. My roommate took 10 but we both commented on the absence of feeling bloated after dinner and the regularity that ensued (Okay I have to confess that I would often take one at lunch AND dinner)!

These are NOT laxatives but candy bites that are packed with Probiotics or "good bacteria" the stomach needs to help digest our food and maintain a healthy balance of energy and fuel. So rather than feeling that your food takes hours to digest there is really a sense that things are more efficiently being broken down in the intestines. It's not an uncomfortable feeling at all (but could be if you over do them).

They don't taste like they smell, so don't dig your nose in and take a big whiff anticipating a nice rich chocolate smell...You won't. What matters is the flavor and the results both of which you will get.

title: But these so called First Aid kits are mostly for things like a cut or a splinter or mild sprain
text:
This kit contains no pain medicine. If you get injured chances are you are in pain from mild to severe. Pain is one of the first things you need to deal with other than bleeding. Pain confuses the mind and leads to hysteria. One cannot deal with other problems if the patient is is in a state of panic. That is what sedatives and painkillers are for. To allow you to treat the patient. But these so called First Aid kits are mostly for things like a cut or a splinter or mild sprain. Really they are close to useless. And they don't supply the medications necessary to really treat a moderate to severe injury.
If you are going camping or hiking and need a real first aid kit you have to pay a doctor and hope he gives you the prescriptions for the proper kit. These are not First Aid kits they are just bandages at a high price.

title: Neighborhood Cat Pee
text:
I purchased Naked Jungle’s Natural Odor Eliminator Spray to help get rid of the cat pee that I smell around my deck and in certain areas around the outside of my home. I don’t think it’s supposed to be used outdoors, but I was desperate. I couldn’t sit out on my deck without be overpowered by the cat urine odor which is HORRIBLE.

I don’t know whether the previous owners of our home had cats or the neighborhood cats smell the ones we used to have on my outside wicker furniture, but they keep coming over to my house and mark their territory. I’ve been using a vinegar based concoction on the places where they do pee but the urine scent is still present.

All of that to say….I sprayed some of the Naked Jungle around my deck and on my wicker furniture and it does help to get rid of the cat urine odor. I do smell the Naked Jungle so it is not odorless, but the scent is very much less obtrusive to the smell than it is to smell cat pee. I will continue to use this product around the outside of my home and I will stock up on it if I need to reapply due to it being used outdoors. It’s worth it!

title: The flexibility of the head makes it very easy to get the back of the back molars! 6 Stars
text:
*** update 8/5/2020 I just realized that the way it bends that it makes it very easy to brush the BACK of the farthest molars. I hadnt thought about brushing that surface until my dentist removed a molar because of it.
So remember to get the back of your back molars always. This makes that Very easy (6 stars)
It takes a bit of getting used to and I originally thought the bristles were too short. But with how soft the bristles are if they were longer the ends of the bristles would not move against your teeth. The bristles in this case grips the stuff between your teeth and pulls it out instead of scraping it out of your teeth.
It takes a bit more work it seems to do a thorough job like all soft bristles.
Another advantage with this one is that because there are such gaps between the bristles its easy to clean after every brushing. I mean a FULL clean. Just your thumb and running water is all it takes. Give it a little buzz to shake off that water and makes it easy to dry.
So I would give it more of a 4.25 because of how much more work it takes to get all the gunk off your teeth. Other than that it would definitely be good for teething children or anyone with sensitive gums.

text: I got this for my sister, whose kid is attending dental school.  she insisted that she needed an electric toothbrush. I guess no one wants to brush that long.  the bottom glows green when its on, and it doesn't make so much noise that its annoying.  once she cranked it up to 5, it did get a little loud and she said that after a while her hand started to feel weird.  strike 3.  we put it in a cup of water to watch the bristle action.  only the top moves, the bottom stays frozen.  strike 4.  she said her teeth felt clean after though.  the instructions that come with this machine are very lacking as well as confusing.  its as if they were translated to English.  the punctuation is all wrong and the words are just incorrect.  so if u r looking for assistance with using it... ur on ur own, but its a toothbrush... haven't we been using them our whole lives... title: Soft Silicone E-Brush
text:

The bristles DO NOT ROTATE while usage. They are extrememyl gentle on my gums, and teeth, but the bristles do not do much. The toothbrush is an electronic one, but all it does is vibrate against your teeth. text:

I originally had a maternity support belt, but it didn't help much to begin with and I outgrew it a few weeks before the pain started. The only thing that has helped is warmth (warm baths, showers, and pools)--I have been miserable.

At my doula's continued suggestion, I purchased this maternity harness earlier this week, and I wish I had done it sooner. It isn't perfect, but it definitely alleviates the back pain. It does nothing for the hip or round lagament pain, but I didn't expect that.

The things I don't like about this product are:
- It is difficult to conceal under shirts because of the neckline.
- The straps are difficult to adjust while it is being worn.
- I wish the belly portion had more adjustability--they only give 3 options to fit it under the belly. I find that I need a set of hooks in between the smallest and medium setting. Had I purchased this sooner, I would have likely taking it to a seamstress to have a couple more hook rows added.
- They don't include instructions for putting the item on.

But overall I am glad I made this purchase because it takes away some of my discomfort. And at this point I am not going to purchase more maternity clothes, so I have accepted that part of the "V" portion of the shoulder straps is going to show. And I do wish I had purchased this sooner.

Oh, and shipping was incredibly fast through Amazon, and I don't have Prime. So I was so thankful for it to arrie when it did.

title: THE BEST "STUFF" ON THE MARKET!
text:
Readers; This retired woodworker, old house owner and 'lover' and historian has a review of a good wood finish product for ALL woods. In the case of the wooden top shown in the image: these are the two lids to a 1925 Victor Talking Machine and its radio set. When I brought it home, all the mahogany finish was 'ugly, black, dirty and 100% filthy and uncared for a 100yrs"
I set to work with the related product-"Skidmores Restoration Cream" and 000 grade steel wool-- to get the 'ugly off". The rags were so dirty, that even after a wash, they were stained black. Much labor and some Time, and the 'ugly' was gone. Next step- The'' Skidmores Finish" compound. This is far and away better than ANY petro-chemical wood finish--petro-chemical finishes are NOT good for wood or wood finishes.
I put this on with a short bristle paint brush, being sure to cover ALL the surface of the wood. Then let it sit half of one day and all of the following night. In the AM, I got a whole sack of micro fiber rags out, and went to work on the cabinet. First, rags to take off the excess product. Then, a clean, new one, in fine, it was one rag for all 06 sides. This buffs out the finish. When done, you can toss a dime on top and watch it glide off the other side. Now, you can judge from the Photo, how it looks. And note too- this photo is done with a cheap flip phone camera. The reflection you see is from an East facing window-the photo taken a circa Noon.
If you want a wood finish that works, is good for the wood, and good for your hands{no gloves nor HAZMAT suit needed for this product} and smells fabulous - this is the ONLY one to buy- as I have been for several years, and for all my antique furniture.

title: What a sonic brush should be. Excellent design. Excellent sonic power.
text:
This is one of the better powered facial brushes that I've used, including sonic, rotary or vibrating varieties. It has a nice sleek, minimalist design appearance. There's only one button, for very easy operation. The massage heads merely push on, and pull off, but they don't fall off when in operation. Perhaps the only design flaw is the piece of silicone that holds the cover for the charging port will sometimes interfere with standing it up on a counter. It's generally possible, but I feel it's not very stable. It's a minor issue, though.
Operation is a simple press of the power button, which lights up the ring around the button. Also, the top button lights up, indicating the first power level. Another press advances to the next power level, indicated by the bottom light coming on. Next press activates the third power level, with both lights alight. The next press will power it off.
I was actually surprised by the robust sonic cleansing effect of this brush. You actually feel the brush impacting the face. In fact, I had to take off the brush head to confirm that it wasn't rotating the brush. Prior to this device, I always felt that rotary brushes performed much better at cleansing the face, because I actually felt the brush moving on the face. I got this effect from this sonic cleansing brush.
There is no information regarding the battery capacity, other than the product details stating that it takes 3 hours to charge it, and it lasts 2 months (with the title explicitly stating "continuous use for 2 months"). I think the battery capacity and some semblance of operating time estimate should be provided, especially in the user manual. This absence dings the rating.
Additionally, they state that the device is 'waterproof', without disclosing the waterproof rating. I consider IPX7 to be waterproof, with lower ratings to be water-resistant. This information is also lacking in both the product details and user manual.
The user manual is very brief, with sparse information/specifications. This is the negative aspect of the product.
Overall, I do like this sonic cleansing brush, a lot. Attached are photos to show real world images of the sonic cleansing brush, with a ruler for size reference. Various angles, accessories and close ups are provided for a comprehensive overview of the product.
The missing information/specifications lowers the rating of an otherwise excellent product. It receives a 4.5+ star rating, with a high level recommendation.

title: Excellent sonic cleansing performance. Attractive design. Good value.
text:
I like the overall appearance of this sonic cleansing brush. It has a stylish minimal aesthetic, with easy handling and operation. Of note, it affords an exemplary sonic performance. When powered, even at the lowest setting, your skin can feel the brush head actually vibrating. This is perhaps the best sonic technology cleansing brush that I've encountered.
It comes with three different brush heads, which easily push on/pull off. Two of the brushes have fine nylon bristles, designated as soft and deep cleaning, with the third being a silicone bristle brush head. The brush heads are well made.
The device has three modes. According to the user manual: Level one is Daily Cleaning, Level two is Deep Cleaning, with the third level cycling between the two modes. The user manual does not give specifications for each level. (The product details mentions the two levels as being 9600rpm and 7200rpm.)
The user manual is very brief, with sparse details, specifications. Besides the lack of details regarding the power levels, there is no information on the battery capacity. It does note that it takes 3 hours to charge the battery. And, that it can be used for two months. That's a very vague, ambiguous specification for operating time.
Also, no definitive detail on the waterproof rating. They claim it's waterproof, but clearly mention not to 'soak' the device under water. So, I doubt that it's rated IPX7, which would be true waterproofing. At best, it's IPX6, which means that it's safe to wash/clean under a faucet. But, again, this lack of detail/specification is missing.
The regular price of $50 seems like a decent cost for the quality of the product. The current cost of $25, including the $25 savings coupon, makes this a very good value. Attached are photos to show real world images, with a ruler for size reference. Various angles and close ups of key features, aspects are provided for a comprehensive overview.
The quantity and value of the missing data counters the excellent design and performance of the product. It does exhibit excellent performance, elegant appearance, and good value, resulting in a 4.5+ star rating, with a high level recommendation.

text:

The Drs pointed out that the DIY spinning bristle brushes harbor bacteria and can possibly scratch and roughen delicate skin especially if used more than once monthly. Their preference is for sonic tools with silicone brush heads as they are easier on skin, don't harbor bacteria and with the more gentle vibrations of the sonic tools, clear out pores better. That advice convinced me to change from a rotary bristle brush to a sonic silicone [vibrating] brush.

This one was a good choice. It's well balanced and easy to hold while you move it around your face and neck. Everything about this brush is simple, from the snap on heads to the one button speed selection. I've used it for a week and so far it shows no sign of needing a charge. text:
This is one of the better powered face brushes I've tried, including those with sonic, rotary, or vibrating motors. It has a good sleek, minimalist look about it. There is simply one button for simple operation. When in use, the massage heads simply press on and draw off, yet they do not fall off. Perhaps the only design problem is that the piece of silicone that secures the charging port lid will occasionally interfere with standing it up on a counter. It's generally doable, but I don't think it's particularly stable. It's a little annoyance, though. This brush does not rotate, but rather vibrates in the manner of a sonic toothbrush head. When I tried it on myself, I really enjoyed it. The speeds are comfortable, with options of 7,200, 9,600, or a combination of 7,200 and 9,600 RPM. More significantly, the brushes are gentle and efficient, causing little harm to the skin's surface while providing a refreshing sensation. The silicone head is said to be the gentlest, but it feels the toughest on my face; nonetheless, the rounded tips are probably less abrasive than the bristles on the brushes. The brushes, on the other hand, are both quite soft.
The operation is as easy as pressing the power button, which illuminates the ring surrounding the button. In addition, the top button illuminates, showing the initial power level. Another press advance is made.

text: I've been using the Boie brush for about 10 days now. There were several things I really liked about this brush when I first got it: The dense bristles did a terrific job with gum massage as well as scouring between teeth and in tight places. It took a little time getting accustomed to the new feel rubbery "fingers" instead of fiber bristles. The bristle area is larger than my old brush, so the way it fit in my mouth felt different. I'm usually on autopilot when I am brushing my teeth, but with this, I had to concentrate on what I was doing to get a good cleaning. Still, even with that, I thought the brush did a good job of cleaning my teeth. It rinsed out nicely with no residue on the brush, and after 10 days' use, there is no bristle deformation. The reason I am giving it one star is that it has a design flaw that makes me uncomfortable to use it. The brush is in two pieces: a stiff plastic handle and a the head which is a sleeve with the soft rubber-like "bristles". The head slips onto the handle like a tight sleeve. The trouble is that the bristle head does not seal on to the handle and after a few days of use, moisture, saliva, and toothpaste gunk seeps into that area between the handle and the head, and makes the whole thing a funky mess. text:
I love this scent! Perfumey and potent, I barely use any of these in the wash and they do the trick. The scent is strong so you don't need much. It don't really know what to compare the smell to, other than it smells like a feminine perfume... floral but with a bright citrus note too. On clothing, it's very mild, but if you are washing a picky male's laundry you might want to try something more herbal. My husband doesn't care one way or the other so this is fine for us.

I know fabric softeners/scent boosters/added stuff are not that great for fabrics but I like my laundry to smell clean. I respond to scent and I have found that I enjoy doing laundry much more if I have nicely scented things to use.

I was using Purex Crystals but the packaging is deceptive, it's only about 3/4 of the way full. I also have to use more in order to get the benefit of the scent. The Downy packaging is a bit better and I do the tiniest sprinkle. One bottle lasts a long time.

They open easily (I guess so people can try the scent before purchasing) and people can steal right from the bottle. I have found half-empty bottles on the shelf before. A friend of mine works in a department store and she says people will dump the entire contents into a ziploc bag and walk out with it! So be sure to check your bottles when you make a purchase! It's easy to just grab a bottle thinking it's full and get home to find that some is missing, especially if you're a distracted mom and are in a hurry to get home before your child has an in-store meltdown!

I now make my own laundry detergent and I use these in one of my batches (I make a softener/added stuff free batch too, for towels) and I am very happy with it. Only one step and no measuring when its time to wash. The recipe I use is from a blog called Aprons 'n Pearls and the post is called Homemade Laundry Soap (if you want to Google it, I found it on Pinterest). It uses washing soda, borax, Fels Naptha, and other ingredients plus these. You only need a couple-few tablespoons per laundry load so one batch lasts a looong time. It takes about 20-30 mins to make it.

I purchased this through Prime Pantry and it was $6.99 with a $2.00 coupon, which is still a little bit more than what I'd pay in my grocery store. But I needed a new bottle before I would have a chance to run to the store. I paid extra for the delivery but in store this is much less expensive, especially if you can find a coupon.

title: One of the better protein options for the money
text:
This protein from EAS can be significantly less expensive per pound than what you'd pay for some of the premium stuff at GNC (if you catch a good sale at Amazon or if you have a membership to Costco/Sams). Some of the reviews focus on the fact that 23g of Protein in 2 scoops is a little skimpy. While this may be true, I'm not sure you'd want/need much more than 23g in one serving and if they used any less than 2 scoops for that same amount of protein you'd definitely sacrifice some of the taste. I've found that this EAS Protein tastes better than most other protein powders out there. The chocolate blends very well with skim milk and I usually throw a banana into the blender as well and it comes out great everytime. It has been a tough winter. We have barely seen the sun for weeks at a time. That has a tendency to make a person cranky and feeling more tired than normal. I have been trying to get more fresh, raw, and green into my body to help counteract this winter problem. Let's take a look at this..

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This is a pretty large foil sealed bag of barley juice powder. Notice it says JUICE. That is essential when you are taking barely green. Some people think that buying ground up barlely greens is just as good- it isn't. This is very bright green and smells VERY fresh.

HOW DO I USE THIS?
I do not put this into things, but I prefer to get some refrigerator cold water, put it in my tiny cordless blender, and put a teaspoon of this powder in. I run it for one cycle which is barely a minute, and then I have the most luscious fresh green drink you can get without fresh greens. There is a lovely layer of foam on it and it tastes heavenly.

DOES IT REALLY TASTE THAT GOOD?
I must preface this by saying that I have had varieties of green powders, fresh green drinks including fresh wheatgrass and kale smoothies. This has a sweetness that is not quite as intense as wheatgrass juice is. It is easier to drink in my opinion than wheatgrass.

I will say that using barley juice powder helps a lot to add energy to my day, helps me to sleep better and it does tend to detox. I would recommend you start with a half teaspoon at first if you are not used to this kind of product. Work up to a teaspoon. It also does keep me regular and not feeling quite so wiped out in times of stress.

DID I GET A DETOX REACTION?
I eat really healthy, do I did not get a detox reaction, but I also made sure to start with half a teaspoon and work up to a teaspoon. It is important to go slowly with this as it can be a bit much if you are not used to it.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This has given me energy, a more positive outlook, helped me feel supplemented, and definitely is helping me through winter very well compared to not having it This tastes fresh and makes a wonderful drink.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I will be buying this again. I stopped getting barley juice powder because I just could not find a really good quality one.. until now. (grins).

title: Appears to be high quality, and definitely inexpensive
text:
This is the second manufacturer I have purchased Barley Grass Juice Powder from; TerraSoul (TS from this point forward) was the first. The issue I had with TS was the taste was significantly stronger than what I was used to (prior to that, I started drinking Barley Grass from a Japanese brand Barley Grass Powder), AND it was extremely difficult to get it to mix/dissolve in water.
After reading many reviews on ZNaturals (ZN), I decided to give this one a try; especially since it specifically mentions it dissolves "easily in water". Well, once I received it, I immediately put it in the refrigerator, which it recommends (interestingly, no other Barley Grass Juice Powder product that I saw recommends this), and finished the last of my TS.
About a week later, I tried the ZN for the first time. First impressions, it mixed better than the TS in water; not perfectly, not 100%, but better than the TS. I still don't understand this as from everything I read, one of the advantages to Juice Powder over just Barley Grass Powder, is the removal of the cellulose, which is not digestible AND is supposedly what makes the Powder clump and NOT mix in water. So, if any Barley Grass product is a Juice Powder, its cellulose has been removed, and it should be completely dis-solvable/mixable in water, right? I even asked ZN before I bought their product about this, and they responded "mix vigorously" in water and it should completely dissolve/mix. While it did not 100% mix, it was definitely better than the TS; there was a little undissolved juice powder floating on top, and the longer I let it sit, more would settle to the top (again, not a huge amount, but not 100% dissolved either).
The second thing I want to mention is the taste. As with the TS product, and apparently ANY Barley Grass Juice Powder, the taste is much, much stronger than just Barley Grass Powder (at least the Japanese brand I was drinking). It is much more like wet grass; whereas the Powder was more like a strong green tea flavor. In my opinion, the ZN was very, very slightly sweeter (natural sweet, not a sugar sweet) than the TS. I actually don't mind it, but several others I've given it to could not drink it straight, they had to add something (juice, almond milk, something...) in order to drink it. I drink it straight, just a scoop of the Juice Powder and approximately 8 ozs of water, every morning.
The only other thing I will say, since there were several reviews that mentioned this, is that on some mornings, I can detect a very, very light saltiness to it; however, it is EXTREMELY light, and I really have to smack, smack, smack my lips/mouth and really try to search for it. I did not find it "overwhelmingly salty" or that it had a "strong salt flavor" to it. I DO NOT add salt to any food (on a very low sodium diet), I don't cook with salt, and I very rarely eat extremely salty foods (guilty pleasure 1 or 2 times per year). My point is, that I am usually very sensitive to salt, to the point where I have even stopped ordering steaks at many restaurants, and have pretty much stopped eating out at all, because everything seems overly salty to me now. So for what its worth, I did not find the ZN product to be salty...at all.
Bottom line, if you can stand a very strong "grassy" flavor, and you mix it very, very vigorously (or in a blender or something like that), then this seems to be a good product at one of the lowest price/oz that I found. I will probably buy again.

text:

First, there's a feature called "Find Name" you just text "Find Name" with the first name of your loved one and it texts you back a map showing where they are. HOWEVER, if it can't find the person because they're in a cell-inaccessible location like a basement of a hospital or something, it just sends you a map of the last place you located them. I would rather it just said it didn't know where he was. This is a software issue. All they'd have to do is make it more pro-active where it reported its location more often. Pretty simple actually! Also, the company should have some additional hardware like buttons we could put down low in case dad falls and doesn't have his unit on.
Dad doesn't complain about the weight, but it does bang against things regularly. This triggers the fall alarm. Fortunately, it asks him if he's okay before it sends the alarm. He can cancel it by pushing the button. It's not really loud, so there's another thing that could be improved.

Update: As I mentioned, the locate feature is wildly inconsistent. I discovered that the company is even worse. I told them to remove this charge and I didn't notice they didn't until my credit card expired. I know, that's my responsibility, but it's a small amount so I didn't notice. title: Very Poor Service when trying to set up account
text:
[[VIDEOID:178d9028cdb8022118b36797346ac095]] Purchased this for my 94 year-old mother who has recently had 3 falls. Was VERY UNHAPPY with the company when trying to set up service and to activate. When I first received the unit, I tested the unit following the directions in the booklet. A recording said that the device had successfully connected and the device was working. (see video). I had not even activated the unit yet. When I called to activate, I asked about the recording and was told that if it was actually connected I would have been connected to a real person - that the unit was not working (even though the recording said it was). I felt the recording was VERY MISLEADING - if my mother had tested it, she would have thought it was connected and working and would have thought she did not need to call to activate it - this could have been a matter or life and death if she tried to use it during an emergency and it wasn't even connected. After giving my and my mother's information over the phone, I was told the unit would be activated in 20 minutes, and I could test it then. When I tested it, I got the same recording, saying it was successfully connected and working. However, no person ever came on. I tried pushing the button for assistance (as if it were an emergency) and the unit said it had not been activated.
I then called customer service and was told it WAS activated and to try the test again. I did so while the representative was on the line - and he was able to hear the recording saying it was successfully connected and working. However, it was NOT activated and working as no live person came on the line. He put me on hold for a minute and then came back and said it was NOT yet activated, but the activation was pending. I told him the other representative had told me activation would take place in 20 minutes, and this representative then told me it would take 24 - 48 hours to activate!!!! So basically the unit was useless at that point. Also, I had been told so much incorrect information at that point that I was ready to cancel the service. I decided to wait until the unit was activated to see how it worked. IT DIDN'T! After 24 hours, I tested the unit again, and it said that the cell service was not good and a connection could not be made. I moved to another location in the house and tried pushing the button as if it were an emergency. I got the same recording saying the cell service was not good and to try another location. About 3 minutes later, while I was in the same location, and without pressing the button again, a live representative came on the line asking if I needed assistance.
During the activation of the device, I was given different information and incorrect information. Then once the unit was activated, it did not work and then did work when I was in the same location. There were so many things wrong with this entire process, from the first message saying it was working (when it wasn't) to the misinformation about whether the unit was activated and how long it would take, to the actual unit not working when the button was pressed. I would never trust this unit as an alert system for my mother or anyone! A person could push the button and lie there dying while waiting for "assistance" that they thought was on the way - while the entire time the system wasn't even working! I am returning this unit and canceling the service!

title: Something changed
text: My husband purchased the LifeStation with fall detection in 2019 and he experienced excellent service from the device for two years.  We would test periodically and the responders were always polite and concerned.  Sometimes he would simply sit down too hard in his chair and they would call to see if he was alright.  Then, he took a fall on ice in Dec. 2021 and his device did not come on automatically.  He pushed to button and nothing happened. He was home alone and had to stay on the ice 20 minutes before he was able to pull himself up.  We contacted the company and they told us it had not worked since April of that year -- that we were supposed to test it monthly to ensure it was working.  This did not set well with us, but we kept the unit.  Now it tells us periodically that it is not working due to poor cell reception, however, we have excellent cell reception.  We are returning it, because it does us no good if we cannot depend on it.  Not sure what has changed, but something has, and not for the better.

LifeStation continues to bill us each month for a service we don't have. This has gone on for 7 months and we have to contact credit card services each month to dispute the charges. We are considering legal action against LifeStation at this point. There are much better options available for medical alert pendants. Research the company behind the device. I like the idea of this - especially if you don't like to put heat on your hair. The theory is that you "braid" sections of your hair around these fabric curling "rods" and either sleep in them, or otherwise let your hair air dry with them on.

I found that each time I've used it, my hair comes out inconsistently curled - either due to my hair getting loose on one or two rods, or unknowingly braiding one or two differently. Since I have fine hair, if I braid a section too tight, it comes out pretty frizzy.

Overall, I think it is a good concept, it just takes practice to get smooth, uniform curls. I'm going to keep practicing and see if I get better results.

title: Very comfortable, even while sleeping.
text: I use these to tame my wild tresses by washing my hair the night before and then quickly damp setting it in this funny but effective curling system. I frequently don't even use additional styling products on my hair, except for leave-in conditioning sometimes and it gives me great results each time. I just set it and sleep. It is that simple. The resultant curls are soft and springy ringlets that last all day long that I can simply run my fingers through and go the next morning. It is all padded and has a slick surface, so my hair does not get tangled in it, except occasionally when the tips of my hair are dry and stick in the hair band portion, as is common and expected with long hair anyway. The hairband portions on the tips of each segment are about the size of a medium cloth-covered hair band, and they are more than sufficient to firmly but gently hold the ends of even the thickest locks through the night. And, yes, I sleep in these quite easily. The adjustable band goes around your head as gently or tightly as you desire and is secured in place with velcro. I prefer mine to have a more gentle hold, so oftentimes it comes off my forehead during the night, but my wrapped hair keeps it from coming off completely. So far, it doesn't seem to affect my results when the band slips upwards off of my forehead. It does make it a bit more challenging when removing it, but even that is far easier than dealing with other forms of curling systems that I've tried. If you prefer to have fewer or looser ringlets, you can remove individual cushioned curling bases and use thicker hair segments for the remaining ones. It is that easy. I'd be hard-pressed to find a simpler or more effective way to get lovely ringlets without using harmful curling and styling products. These are silly looking on me at night, but make me look and feel great the next day.

Neptune Krill Oil (NKO) is known for its unique fatty acid (FA) profile, as well as for its rich antioxidant content. NKO's balanced fatty acid content includes not only EPA and DHA, the crucial Omega-3 , but Omega-9 and phospholipids, as well. NKO is a rich source of Astaxanthin, a powerful immune-supporting antioxidant. Clinical studies have shown that NKO can support joint comfort, healthy blood lipid levels, and may reduce symptoms of pre-menstrual syndrome.

KRILL OIL VS FISH OIL: Krill oil is an omega-3 nutrient and is an alternative source of omega-3 than fish oil. Some folks prefer krill oil over fish oil because they believe it has increased bioavailability and better absorption than fish oil, and contains the additional nutrients, Astaxanthin and Phospholipids. In fact, this is correct. Krill oil has better bioavailability and absorption than fish oil and contains Astaxanthin and Phospholipids, neither of which are contained in fish oil.

ASTAXANTHIN: Astaxanthin is a powerful anti-oxidant and anti-inflammatory. It is a red-pink substance found in various seafoods such as salmon, trout, krill, lobster and cooked shrimp. It is responsible for the red color of salmon meat, cooked shellfish and flamingo feathers. It is present in krill oil but not in fish oil.

The presence of astaxanthin in krill oil, combined with other naturally occurring antioxidants in the oil (Vitamins E and A), provides protection against oxidation of the oil, making it stable for a long time. It also protects the body against free radical attacks which can cause aging of the cells. Antioxidants are usually added in fish oil to prevent the oil from oxidizing as they do not have any on their own.
