title: I've always slept better during storms and it's nice to be able to hear one anytime I'd like...
text:
I like this sound machine but it doesn't have as many sounds to choose from as others I've used in the past. For the price, I feel it should have more than 8 choices. The 8 choices it offers are White Noise, Rain, Bird, Brook, Lullaby 1, Lullaby 2, Ocean and Thunderstorm. I like the choices, but since 2 of them are lullabies, that means only 6 are what I would call white noises. The thunderstorm choice is my favorite, followed by the rain. I've always slept better during storms and it's nice to be able to hear one anytime I'd like. The ocean is also very pleasant and it does remind me of a day at the beach and I also like the brook, but have to admit that it makes me have to go to the bathroom more often. (Just a heads up lol) I'm not sure I could sleep to the birds, I associate birds more with waking up I guess, but I do like the sound. As far as the lullabies go, they are nice but they are not my cup of tea, although I can see how they might be a good choice for an infant. The sounds are all very clear and it's easy to tell what they are supposed to be, and the volume can be turned up much louder than I expected. It actually gets quite loud. If this was priced a little lower, I would have easily given it 5 stars, but for the price they are asking, I just don't think it competes since it has too few choices compared to others in that price range.
I received this DBPOWER White Noise Machine for free or at a discount in exchange for my honest opinion. I do not guarantee a good review. I rely on product reviews myself when shopping and will always give my honest opinion-good or bad. All opinions are based on my experience with the product and yours may differ.

title: too loud for baby
text:
So disappointed. It has a way to adjust the volume but even the lowest doesn't create a soft sound that you could let drift in to the background. I ran it in a room with an Ac unit (which runs at 90 decibels when you are right in front of it) just to see which was louder. You can hear it over the Ac unit when I'm sitting in front of the Ac unit and the sound machine is in the opposite corner. I was looking for something like the Ac unit fan but quieter to make soft white noise for my baby when we don't need the Ac unit to run. Well this is louder then that so it wakes her. The white noise sound sounds like old analogue tv static not soft fan sounds. It's terrible. I even tried putting it on the other side of her door, no still sounds terrible and too load. To top it off you have to use a forward and back button to even try the other sounds, which are at different volume levels so cycling throug them while trying to put a baby to bed is counter productive. Last thing, even if you try the nice soft rain track it's got some lovely rolling thunder to wake you dosing infant. Even the lullabies are too load. Very disappointed this thing.Returning. Replacing it with a small 10 in fan, which make a nice soft sounds to which my infant has now passed out to after being woken up by and not being able fall asleep with this dbpower machine.
Waste my time and money on the one.

Update: I have been contacted by the seller/maker. They share that they did a lot of research before making this product. They report that many people wanted a louder machine to fully block out external noise. That's fine and well, but it's also advertised for babies room with special tracks just for baby. So that said, I still stand by my original statement that its too loud for that purpose. Most recommendations say in babies rooms prolonged noises should not exceed 60 decibels. This is over that. After exchanging emails with the company, sighed by Bella (who ever that is within the company , no title or position was listed) I do believe this company wants to make a quality machine and make customers happy. My return was a breeze and money returned with in 24 hours of the item being picked up with no further action needed by me. They also offered me a free item as an apology (and a request to update my negative review) but I didn't take it. I didn't write my review to get free things, just to express how my expense was compare to my expectation based on the item description. They asked me if I will test the next generation which I will. I'd love to see a version that meets the original claim.(and maybe a few other improvements) It could be a great machine if it's improved. I'll hold out hope for that. I'd really like to have a better version of this. I really wanted to like it.

title: WORTH A TRY! IF YOU GIVE IT A CHANCE!
text:
This inhaler does exactly what it is meant for...There are some that have mentioned a clay taste when first using it. Which it very well may be from the manufacturing process of the inhaler. There is an easy way to rectify that issue though, all you have to do is rinse it out with water before your first use and make sure that it is completely dry before adding your salt. It should be a good practice to rinse anything that you may be inhaling, eating, or applying on yourself anyways.

I purchased this for my fiance who has COPD and allergies. It has definitely helped his breathing, the hardest issue is just reminding him to use it since it is something new to him. The best times to get him to use it is in the morning when he is sitting watching the news. So he can just drink his coffee and use his inhaler. Then at night again right before bed when he is sitting in bed watching tv. I am hoping that the benefits will only get better, but they are definitely showing some promise.

Also don't expect this to work overnight! That is just not how this works, time before you notice any benefits can vary from person to person. So make sure you give it a chance to work. It is not an alternative to your Dr. ordered meds, but it has reduced my fiances use....I did not get this in trade for a review, I bought this and wanted to give an honest review ; )

Also key thing here when ordering salt either purchase refill from same company or order VERY COARSE SALT otherwise anything smaller will be too small. I made that mistake myself so I am making you aware of that, the medium coarse was even too small.

title: Good for surface cleaning of books, especially cloth boards
text:
I have been happy with this product for surface-dirt removal on old non-glossy dustjackets, cloth boards and spines, and the page block edges (quick swipe 'with the grain' along the top-edge takes off dust build-up). I have found it especially good for brightening up cloth boards that have become dingy with surface dirt. This is not a stain-remover. If you deal with a lot of dusty books, this is good for freshening them up.

UPDATE: We are about to re-order some of these. We got a good year out of them, and really should have re-ordered at that point. It speaks well of the product that we've been able to squeeze another year out of them. We rinse them now and then, but in the second year the sponges are still functional, but they start to crumble and lose little pieces. It's a sponge, and we use them pretty heavily, so this is not a big problem for me. The price is right for replacement. We'll re-order again I am sure.

We use these to clean dust off the top of the page block, and to take surface dust and mold off of the boards of a hardcover. Sometimes when end-papers get moldy, you can use these sponges to take the worst of it off. Same with the underside of dust jacket that has been exposed to mold.

title: I am SO happy with this product!
text:
I am SO happy with this product!

I like to wear socks with treads around the house; because of a stroke many years ago I have drop foot and slippers fall off my right foot. But tread socks are always way too small, even the ones that claim to be the right size for my feet. I wear size 12W shoes, am tall, and have some edema in my feet and ankles. Until now, every single pair of socks I've bought both with and without treads have been too small and it's a struggle to put them on.

Well, after reading a lot of reviews of various socks on Amazon.com, I found that I am not alone. An overwhelming number of reviewers complain that men's socks sizes always run far smaller than advertised. So with that in mind, and for only about a dollar a pair, I decided to try these Single-Side Tread Socks XXX-LARGE. They were delivered today. I tried on a pair (which I am wearing as I write this) and I can't tell you how nice it is to put on a pair of tread socks that ACTUALLY FIT MY FEET AND ANKLES! They are perfect! They were easy to put on and they're snug enough to wear securely without being too tight.

I'm going to make sure I wash them in cold water so that they don't shrink. And if the tread wears excessively (as some other reviewers have averred), for only $3.24 for three pair I'll buy more. To me they're worth five times that price. Last night we had our first cold New England night of the season, near 40 degrees and it's cool in the house. These socks are snuggly warm, and with my weak right foot I feel confident in walking in them without slipping.

At the same time I ordered these, I also ordered 3 pair of black and 3 pair of white socks in sizes that on the surface would be ridiculously large -- they say they fit feet that wear size 16 to 20 shoes -- and all those socks fit my size 12W feet perfectly also. Lesson learned! I have no idea how the all the various manufacturers can be so wrong about their sizing on so many different brands of men's socks... but I can say with confidence and now from experience: If you wear a size 12 shoe and/or have any type of swelling in your feet or ankles, you'll probably be delighted as I was to find these tread-bottom socks that actually fit comfortably and securely and are wearable.

When I first put them on, the side pieces pressed firmly against the side of my head. At first I thought they were too tight, but I left them on and within a couple of minutes did not notice any discomfort. The snug fit keeps them seated on my face and they don't slip down my nose even with sweat and suntan lotion. After successful use at the beast, I've made them my go-to pair for daily use.

title: A Product Everyone Needs (And Should Own)

I own multiple nail clippers of various sizes and have always found that quality does not always equate to the price paid. I one day came across a channel on YT (I am unsure if I can mention the site, but I am sure most know which video website I am referring to). The individual is a professional that goes above and beyond any pedicure, I have ever had. And they utilize tools similar to the ones found in this kit. Clipping, trimming, and filing your nails are not enough. There are tools in this kit most need but are unaware they do. I find the quality to be high, so much so my nails look the best they ever have after use. The only cons I can share are that the label/emblem on the case is highly sticky. We are talking to the point that I initially had to be very careful not to allow it to touch anything. Fortunately for me, it seems to have lost its adhesiveness over time.

The other things I will never use are the ear tools. While some might see them as a great bonus, you should never place anything (not even a cotton swab or washcloth) in your ear unless you want issues. Of course, you should clean your ears daily, but nothing should ever go inside any part other than the outer ear and pinna. Besides the above, this is a product that everyone who cares about their nails should own (even those who regularly get manicures and pedicures).

title: My search for an awesome shower bomb continues
text:
This would make a great hostess gift - because it's the thought that counts, and the thought behind shower bombs is a really nice one. Sadly, while the scent is as good as any when you stick it right under your nose, I barely notice it once I'm in the shower with it. If you're envisioning being enveloped with scented steam, nope. Just steam. I did try different temperatures, and it doesn't matter. The bomb dissolves in about 6-8 minutes (depending on how much water is hitting it) so it lasts long enough; the scent just doesn't fill the area.

The foil out covering is easy to remove, but you do need the little lime green pointy tool to open the inner plastic wrapping. It's easy enough to use when your hands are wet.

This set has a few unique features about it that make it better than some other options, though. For instance, there's some shredded paper at the bottom which makes it seem a little more gift-like. And there's a little sticky-backed hook to hang in your shower to hold the organza bag and opener that comes with the set, and you can fit two bombs in the bag as well. That helps keep your bombs handy.

Summary: I tried the lavender first, and then tried the eucalyptus the next day. Just not enough scent for me. And while I did put the hook up, and hang the bag, 2 bombs, and the opener, I know I'm going to forget to refill the bag. I normally keep all my bombs in a container on the shelf that holds my shampoo and that makes more sense to me. I think hook and the bag are coming down shortly. Better idea in theory than in practice. But again, I've been looking for a year for a shower bomb that truly works the way I want it to and haven't fond it yet. These bombs are in good company! And they really would make a thoughtful gift even though they don't really do much.

title: Not worth it - and can stain white fiberglass!
text:
UPDATE:
The purple tablet was completely dissolved after 3 days sitting on the rear of the tub. However, I saw there was a faint purple stain on the white fiberglass. Faint in that no-one else would notice it, but I knew where the tablet had sat and dripped, and could see the purple coloring. It didn't wipe off and neither did a spray and soak with bleach cleaner remove it! Hopefully it'll fade, or maybe pure bleach will work if not. The unused ones are in the trash!
.
ORIGINAL REVIEW:
.
I recently reviewed some other shower steamers and they weren’t very good. I saw these in my Vine Listing and thought I’d try them and see if they were any better.
As an Amazon Vine reviewer, I am offered new-to-market products, if I want them, at no cost to me, in exchange for an honest, objective, and comprehensive review.
I get a laugh out of the spelling on the front; these are apparently Showen Steamers! 😊 At least the rear spelling is correct!
Interestingly, the package also includes a little purple nylon mesh bag and adhesive hook, presumably to hang a steamer block in. There is also a little pick, which I have no idea what it is for.
However, after some thought, I think it might be to open the plastic wrap! Each block is foil-wrapped, but unlike the previous steamers, these are also wrapped in plastic. That is very tough to remove without scissors, or a pick! One set of blocks is green and the other is purple. This is reflected in the actual crystal block as well as the foil. I assume the purple is the Lavender.
I say ‘assume’ because the aroma is nothing like Lavender or Eucalyptus & Menthol. It is certainly less “chemical” smelling than the previous set I reviewed, and perhaps less pungent in use, but I’ve no idea what the smell actually is. There’s no comparison with the essential oils I have of these very scents.
As with any of these steamers, you have to place them away from the direct shower spray. They will last less than one shower if you do. I place one so that it is occasionally hit with water, to release the aroma. That way it can last maybe 4 showers.
As mentioned, the aroma is not very strong and if hit with hot water, the block will release a burst of scent, which quickly dissipates and some of the coloring will run in the shower. The scent can be overwhelmed easily by any scented bodywash or shampoo. I certainly didn’t notice any residual aroma the next day, with the block having sat in the shower overnight. I think the product would be better if it were a small tablet for a single use directly in the shower stream and the price were less than 50c each.
.
While this set is less offensive and strongly smelling than the last, I still would not spend my own money of these. At $2.67 each, these are not good value and I can’t recommend them

title: Don't let the price fool you!
text:
I have to admit that I wasn't expecting much due to the low cost of this iron, but as with other reviewers, I was pleasantly surprised! It's initial presentation makes it appear as if it was one of the top of the line (and very expensive) flat irons. It comes with two different options to store it, one being a black sturdy box with magnet closures and the other being a case that is perfect for travel. The inside of the case has a lining that I believe is specifically for "hot tools" but I am not sure and unfortunately, the product brochure didn't elaborate as to if this is the case. Another bonus found inside this case was a set of alligator clips, which also appear sturdy and well made. Having had many flat irons, most of which were on the more expensive side, I was really surprised at the weight of this one. Compared to my well known brand / high end flat irons, this one is light weight, which is a big bonus. I found it much easier to maneuver. With that being said, it is smaller than my flat iron in regards to overall size. This iron is suitable for traveling, for it is small, light weight & comes with it's own bag which has room for additional supplies/accessories. Perhaps it's due to my personality, but I am bothered by little things such as typos. Therefore I was slightly disappointed as to the instructions provided for they had several grammatical issues such as missing words. I know this can be looked at as a very minor and perhaps an insignificant detail, but something that I wanted to mention since it is an overall impression of the company. Perhaps this was overlooked due to their exceptional detail and desire to focus their energy on the presentation of this flat iron, for they did a fantastic job. I gave the iron 4 stars, for I really do like it and will use it for travel. It is missing a few features that I like, such as auto shut off, notification when the iron is at ideal temperature and I wish it were just a tad bigger, but all in all it is a great iron for a fantastic price!

High End Salon Quality Flat Iron.

Included heat protective zip bag to pack if it's still hot.
Cons-
On/Off switch is located in very difficult spot to reach, on the inside just below the bottom plate. Was hard to reach so never bothered switching it off, just unplugged it.
The plates are very small. Granted, this is a travel/compact flat iron so I guess that's to be expected but unfortunate.
There is no heat setting. It's on or it's off. In my opinion, this iron doesn't get hot enough. At best it appears to get mildly warm and just wasn't hot enough for my hair.
Conclusion? Although compact, pretty and packaged nicely, I'd rather take my everyday iron with me and take more room in the suitcase to have something that heats up better, has bigger plates and doesn't take me 5 times longer to do my hair. As far as dual voltage, I won't need that feature often so I'd investigate other options if needed again.

title: Some small problems but overall not bad
text:
Basically, these pads function fairly well; but there are a couple of drawbacks. First, the edges are made of a flimsy material that has a tendency to fold back on itself. This results in not completely covering the underwear between the leg holes. No matter how careful I am, I can't prevent the edges from folding and leaving some material uncovered. Therefore, urine can stain the parts of the underwear that are thus uncovered. While almost all of the leaking urine will be absorbed by the pads, it's very annoying that because of this design flaw you will still get a little bit on the underwear.

The second fault is apparently intended to be a feature since it's obviously an intentional part of the design. There is a protective pocket that holds each pad and this pocket is glued in a couple of places to the strip of thin plastic that covers up the adhesive part of the pad. So the pocket and the pad are actually one piece. You're supposed to remove the plastic material from the pad to expose the adhesive portion so it can stick to the underwear. But due to the pocket material being glued to the plastic covering it is impossible to take out the pad without also exposing the adhesive of the pad. I guess this was to prevent you from forgetting to expose the adhesive before putting it in the underwear. I think it's an indication of how needless this "feature" is when you realize that women's panty liners do not have a similar feature that automatically removes the plastic cover from the panty liner to expose the adhesive. I guess men aren't smart enough to figure this out.

So now you must be careful to throw away the pocket while still holding the sticky pad, or else try to carefully put down the pad without having it stick to something. That is stupid. I would like to be able to throw away the pocket while not exposing the pad's adhesive until I am ready to install it. Now it's certainly not impossible to work this out, but it's an unnecessary nuisance and it just makes no sense that they went out of their way to glue the pocket to the cover piece.

In spite of these annoyances I will likely continue to get these pads since they otherwise suit my needs and will comfortably absorb almost all of any liquid that I leak.

I wanted to try this as an alternate to coffee and energy drinks. I love both but good coffee takes time and energy drinks are pricey and not that good for you. I wanted something that I could take with me into the field or mix into juice or put on food (like yogurt, etc.). title: Great masks that come with extras
text:
Mamlyn 3 Ply Breathable Cloth Face Mask, Reusable Washable Adjustable for Men and Women, Mask Wash Bag, and Pouch to Store The Mask

These are actually pretty standard masks. They have adjustable straps, a nose bridge wire and a filter pocket. They are a bit thin though as far as I can tell, they do have three layers as described in the product information.

For the price, there are two individually wrapped masks included. What sets this product apart from the huge number of masks that have shown up on Amazon in the last few months is the extras. They include a mesh bag to wash the masks in a washing machine (delicate cycle only) and a carrying bag. And the mesh bag is actually good quality and large enough to fit more than a few masks in.

Though the masks have a filter pocket, they do not include filters. They take the standard PM2.5 filters that are more and more available on Amazon. The filters slide in easily and stay put.

The instructions on the back of the mask package are kind of silly. They were obviously written by someone who doesn't have English as a first language. They are hard to understand, to the point of being nonsensical, and even use the word poison. By poison, I think that they mean any contaminants that are picked up while you're out and about. Anyway, it's a mask. Wash it like you normally would.

For the price, this is a great deal. Especially with the extras.

title: Mask protects my face well; adjustable ear loops for good fit
text:
These 2 cloth face masks (each mask is individually packed in its own resealable plastic bag) fit my small-size face in a comfortable manner.
The flexible nose clip helps the mask stay more securely on the bridge of my nose. I find that the more closely the mask fits around my nose, the less often my glasses fog up.
The ear loops are adjustable, allowing a good form-fitting mask without the loops tugging at my ears.

At each side of the mask, the ear loops are sewn into the mask (as opposed to masks that have the loops sewn on the outside or the inside of the masks).

I like that there is a slot inside the mask, where I can put in a PM2.5 filter.
note: filters are not included with these masks. I am fine wearing these 3-ply masks as is, and have not bought filters to put inside the slot.

I like that the bottom part of the mask has a extension such that the mask goes under my chin.

The mesh helps prolong the life of these masks during repeated washings.

There are a number of laundry symbols on the back of the resealable bag. Here's how I interpreted the symbols:
wash in water temperatures not above 30 degrees, do not bleach, do not tumble dry, iron any temperature - steam, any solvent.

On the back of the resealable bag, there are confusing instructions, such as "...wash the poison once a day, wash it with warm water first, then bot and hot to dry..."
The instruction to wash in warm water is in contrast with the laundry symbol that I interpreted above, "wash in water temperatures not above 30 degrees".

Overall, I like how well this mask fits my face from the bridge of my nose to under my chin.

title: Excellent masks with a few disposable extras
text:
These are very well-made masks, though the cloth is quite impermeable. They come packaged with some disposable extras, a laundry bag and a storage bag, which are okay but not high-quality, and each mask is enclosed in a ziploc package printed with hilariously poorly-translated Engrish instructions about cleaning and use.

The fit is excellent, with a well-made curved form, adjustable ear loops, and an excellent, long, flexible nose wire that makes it easy to achieve a tight fit around the nose (though the fit in the chin is still a little tight so that a wide yawn can pull the mask out of position). The nose wire is the best I've used on any cloth mask so far, and actually gives me a better fit around the nose than many N95s — though the mask obviously doesn't seal nearly as well on the rest of the face, and your inhalation and exhalation goes around the sides of the fabric more than it actually goes through, the nose wire still prevents glasses fogging very well, directing exhaled air down and to the sides instead of up toward your eyes. The outer fabric is very dense and impermeable, so there is still some clamminess when wearing it for a long time, but I find these masks quite comfortable.

title: Nice Mask, Poor Translation re Health Tips
text: Per my wife: This package comes with two identical masks, so I'll just describe one of them. This is a very nice mask, well fitting, well made, with good facial coverage for me from my nose to under my chin. It has an adjustable nose band, adjustable ear loops, and a slot for a filter if desired. It's made in China, and the Health Tips as written on the package are a little rough as far as the translation. What the package says versus what I believe they meant : "into the bag after use. Carry this product" (keep the storage bag with you to store the mask when not wearing it). "please divide the opposite side" (open the filter slot and use a filter in it). "do not wear back, anti-external will stick dust powder, direct contact between mouth and nose will be detrimental to health." (Don't wear the mask inside out because the outside can get contaminated). "Wash the poison once a day." (Wash off any contaminates daily).  "wash it with warm water first, then bot and hot to dry". (I think "bot" means "blot it off"). So, no, the seller is not saying the mask is poison, as one person thought who rated the mask a one star because of it. This package comes with two very nice masks, a storage bag for the mask when not wearing it, and a mesh laundry bag to put the mask in when it's being laundered. The universal laundry symbols on the mask say to wash cold (though the Health Tips say wash warm), do not bleach, do not dry flat, okay to iron, do not tumble dry, and okay to dry clean using process A (the dry cleaner should know what that means). Since you can't tumble dry the mask per the universal instructions, perhaps "bot and hot to dry" may mean blot the mask off and dry it in the sun or iron it dry. Not sure. In spite of the language barrier in translation, I like the masks, the storage pouch, and the mesh laundry bag. and am rating this complete package 5 stars.

title: Amazing Deep Massages!
text:
Bought this with my own money, no sample given. I wanted to wait a bit to actually get some real usage in before reviewing this so as to have an accurate perspective. I do own a trigger point roller as well (the black one, densest they have) and this raw roller definitely gives it a run for it's money.

The truth is in the PVC piping they use, and it's REALLY dense. Compared to the trigger point, this thing has some heft for sure. It's still extremely portable though and is definitely not too heavy to carry (they even include a nice carrying bag, but the quality of the bag was sub-par, there's already a rip occurring near the straps). The foam that they use to coat the PVC pipe is very thin, but comfortable enough that there is a bit of cushion between your body and the roller. I'd say it's the bare minimum between comfort and discomfort, which is GREAT! You can definitely feel the deep massage in your muscles with this thing. The trigger point does give adequate massages as well, but if you really want to get DEEP, this roller is the way to go.

I also got a follow up email with cute pictures of the owner's dog in some spiffy shades with the roller next to it, so that was kinda cool. If you're looking for the next best thing to a PVC pipe, this is it!

title: A few things I dislike but an overall decent bike
text:
The scooter was very simple to assemble and adjust to my height. I was pleasantly surprised to open the box & find a blue scooter. I say surprised because I ordered black but had literally just complained to someone there were no good colors to choose from so black was the default. I like the dark blue I received much better. The scooter maneuvers very easily. The dual hand brakes are fantastic bc sometimes I have to carry something in 1 hand & steer/brake with the other. I also HIGHLY recommend getting a scooter with a basket. The basket on this has been so helpful.

There are a few things I dislike. The knee pad is shaped well but the padding is pretty hard and the fabric covering is hard too. After 1 day of using the scooter, my shin felt bruised and sore. You can buy knee pads, but I found putting a soft folded towel on the seat under my leg seemed to fix the problem. The paint on the scooter chips off easily. When I slid the basket onto the 2 prongs that hold it, it immediately scraped a bunch of the paint off the prongs. My other big gripe is transporting it. This scooter is too tall to fit easily in my car's backseat. The handlebars fold forward so you can turn the scooter upside on its seat but you have to take the basket off to do that. I was able to rearrange my trunk to fit the scooter so I found a solution, but it would've been better to have the handlebars hinge the other way.

Other people have mentioned the scooter hitting bumps or cracks in sidewalk, spots where the floor changes from carpet to wood, or in my case large acorns, which cause the scooter to pop up or bounce & lean causing people to lose balance or fall down. I have had this experience but that doesn't happen with just this scooter. That's going to happen with any knee scooter unless you get one designed to go "off-road". It does have a few flaws, but if you aren't needing it for a long period of time, it's a pretty good knee scooter.

Update: Now that I've used the scooter for 1 month, I have discovered things I never would've thought of. The vibrations from rolling over sidewalk cracks & dips & dividers, etc caused 2 of the bolts holding the knee pad in place to wiggle out. I had to go buy 2 new screws from Home Depot. I suggest checking your screws for looseness regularly. I've also found the metal basket vibrates against the metal prongs holding it and squeaks incessantly like nails on a chalkboard if the basket is empty. I suggest wrapping the prongs in electrical tape, duct tape, fabric tape, etc or something to keep the metal from touching. I'm sure these issues are not limited to only this scooter. So be prepared to make modifications to any scooter you purchase.

title: Gentle exfoliation, replaceable inner sponge
text: This is a great body scrubber. It's gentle enough to use every time you shower, but it exfoliates really well too. There is a cellulose sponge inside and you can easily remove it and put in a new one when it  is used up. There are a few different textures on the silicone part if you need a different experience. I bet you could run the silicone outer piece through the dishwasher to sanitize it if you think you need to.

title: Easy to grasp and use, but the sponge is so dense that it doesn't dry quickly
text:
While I really like this design in some ways, the sponge is somewhat difficult to remove and replace because it is dense and likewise never seems to dry out because it is so dense. The sponge appears to be made from cellulose. The idea is that you squirt liquid soap onto the side with holes that lead down to the sponge. This creates a reservoir of soap that can be released when you squeeze the sponge. The soft silicone bristles feel nice on the skin. There is a slit in the bottom of the silicone casing where you can pull the sponge out. I initially tried hanging this bath brush in an airy spot with the sponge inside, but the sponge hadn't dried at all after 24 hours. I pulled the sponge out and put it in an airy spot, but it still took two days to dry out. So, if you use this every day, it's never going to dry out and will probably start to mold.

title: I'm not wowed enough to eliminate razors + UPDATE
text:
First of all, let me say that this wasn't as painful as I had been expecting. Not comfortable but definitely tolerable. This took a while to ship to me, so I had plenty of time to grow out the hair on my legs to give it a test run. Perhaps I let my hair get a little too long because even though this definitely removed most of the hair on my ankles and calves, it didn't give me a smooth result at all. I think it broke some of the hairs close to the skin, causing some stubble that the epilator couldn't pull out with more passes.

It did come with directions but they were pretty basic. Nothing mentioning the desired starting length of hair before using. I did no preparation before using. Unboxed it and gave it a go.

My skin is pretty dry and flaky from the winter air. As I was using it, I could see my dry skin flaking off with the plucked hairs. It took many passes to get both legs (knee to ankle done). Took about 15 minutes. The after result was really ashy skin that was pretty itchy with some minor redness at some of the follicles.

I will attempt to use this again after a hot shower and good exfoliation to see if I achieve a better result. I did give my legs another pass over the stubble left behind with the shaver head and that didn't make anything any smoother. I did use it on my partner's back of neck and it did remove hair but he flinched a few times from the shaver head grabbing and pulling a few of the longer hairs. After a few passes, he ran and refused to allow me to test the product on him any further.

The product itself is not junk but it's not high quality either. The clear covers for each head don't fit snugly and fall off easily. The box it came in is really basic, nothing you would want to keep to store the device, attachments, brush and charging cable in. It did arrive already charged. I ran it for about 20-30 minutes and did not notice any slowing down or lag in the motor.

So far, I don't think that this will replace shaving for me but instead will be another tool in my hair removal arsenal. I have noticed that my legs have remained mostly hair free after using it. I haven't had to shave again in the week after using this.

I feel as this might be a cheaper, less effective epilator than other more expensive models, but can't say for certain as this is the first I've tried. Inexpensive way to see if you can tolerate this method of hair removal to see if purchasing a better unit is worth your time/expense. I don't have the nerve to try this on my bikini area but will attempt it on my armpits after a warm shower to see if I can tolerate it.

I will continue using this but when I come across a higher quality product, I will definitely be upgrading and passing this budget epilator along to my daughter for her to try before purchasing one for herself.

UPDATE: I attempted to use this on my armpits. While the pain factor was tolerable on my legs, I could not withstand the pain it caused while using it on my underarms. However, I came back to give this product one more star. Since using this product on my legs, I have not needed to shave my legs whatsoever. I'm due to give my legs a touch up soon, but I am tickled with how long my hairless legs have lasted. It took a while to do both legs the first time but with how long the results have lasted, I've saved myself so much time and effort in the long run. It's a very worthwhile investment.

The instructions are pretty specific, a few translation errors, but understandable. NOTE: don't leave this on charge. Directions say not to charge more than 8 hours - to which I infer that there's no sensor that will turn off charging when it's full. So be careful. The heads swap out in a snap - literally. title: Uncomfortable but effective.
text:
I’ll be honest, I was worried about trying this item out. I’ve always been curious about epilating, but I’ve only known one other person to do it, and they said it was incredibly painful, but the results were great. As someone who is always looking for a shaving method that won’t leave me prickly after a few hours, I really wanted to try it.
I will say, I chickened out with the epilator after a few meek passes over my ankle. It does indeed hurt, as it obviously will, since the very nature of the thing is tons of tiny tweezers literally ripping the hair out. However, my hair HAD grown pretty long due to my putting off trying this for a while, so that may not have helped. But I’m unsure.
Either way, I ultimately just ended up using the electric razor attachment, and that worked wonderfully. Quick and easy, a lot easier than a manual razor. So that is a major plus. It may take some working up to the epilator attachment, and trial and error.
I will make sure to update if I figure out an easier way to use it.

It removed the hair quickly and easily. I do find it a bit painful -- not unmanageable but not entirely painless. I like that it comes with the razor option to swap in as well which makes it versatile for anywhere particularly sensitive that you may not want to use the epilator on. Its a nice size -- small enough that it's not cumbersome to hold but big enough that it can cover a good amount an area in a pretty short amount of time.

text:

Since May and June of 2020 gave me lots of free time, I scrubbed both patios with 30 second cleaner (also a fine product), wire brushed the many spots where the algae was "barnacled" to the concrete and finished the whole thing with a power wash. Looked really good so I decided to seal it. Researched online and decided to go with a water based siliconate penetrating sealer. Foundation Armor SC25 was frequently recommended online so I bought 5 gallons.
IT WAS DELIVERED IN 2 DAYS! But the best parts were yet to come. Used a paint roller for super easy application. Panicked briefly when all manner of imperfections in the patio popped out when wetted.
Within a few hours, the patio zits all disappeared and the color normalized between the two patio surfaces.
(amazing since they are at least 25 years apart in age)
This morning my wife spilled a bucket of water on the deck and it ran off like it was a ducks back!
Great product, great service. Happy to write this review.

title: Not my favorite
text:
I've used several of these type of machines before but this is my first foot massaging machine. It comes in a nice retail box that would be gift friendly. The actual foot massager looks to be a quality machine. The power cord is relatively short, around 5.5 feet, so you have to be in very close proximity to a power outlet to use. The cord will have to route around furniture you have on the floor which makes the cord feel shorter than it is. As far as the actual settings, it has 2 speeds (slow, fast), you can turn heat on or off, and you can increase the air pressure. I have to be honest, I am not a fan.

- I feel nothing on the arches of my feet.
- The air pressure, even on the highest setting, feels like it isn't enough.
- I can't feel any heat.
- The little nubby massage things under the ball and heel of my foot don't feel good. I embrace massage where it may be painful but you gain something from it. This just doesn't feel right. The nubby things are rock hard plastic. I wouldn't say it hurts, but it is not pleasant, and I don't think I am getting anything out of using it. I feel like if they had a little give to them, if they were firm but slightly squishy, and the air pressure was higher it would be a million times better.

I have sat and used it for 20 minutes on a few occasions and it's not BAD, I just don't care much for it. Feels like it could be so much better with a few tweaks. Two of us in the household tried this and felt similarly. Maybe we have the wrong feet for this and others will have better luck!

title: ❤️🖤💛💚Massage With Compression 💞 Great For Plantar Fasciitis💙🧡💜🤎
text:
For me, the compression with the massage is the cats pajamas. OMG, it is wonderful! The bottom massager is more pointy than smooth which for me, is the only sometimes negative aspect to this depending on how sensitive my feet are at the time. My husband who has Plantar Fasciitis loves the pointy bits.

The bottom rollers are big enough to cover the entire foot, including my husband's size 10 feet. Not all foot massagers are designed this way. Around the same time I ordered this, I also ordered a soft & plush foot rest style massager. It has massage rollers that are smaller, so it doesn't cover the entire foot but the rollers are smooth. No compression, but you can slide your feet into a little plush cave that is removable. That massager is about $100 less than this massager.

If I had to pick between the two, I'd pick this massager by Sharper Image. It is the best massager I've ever owned & I've owned quite a few over the years thanks to my husbands Plantar Fasciitis. This doesn't mean I don't love the other massager. I love them both. The other is more cozy time relaxing, this on the other hand while very relaxing, also offers much more therapeutic benefits. Even though massager means business, I will still fall into a light doze while using it.

This also has a heat function. It doesn't get very warm, but it is still nice; never too hot.

As advertised, you can flip this over for a vibrating foot rest. Personally, I really enjoy the versatility.

If you want something that looks nice, need some serious foot TLC, & can afford it, I see no reason why you wouldn't consider getting this. If you do want it & it's out of your price range (oh how I know that feeling I'm a full time Eco farmer), put it in your carts save for later & wait & hopefully a deal rolls around or you accumulate enough points on your amazon visa to get it free.

If this sounds like more massage action than you really need or want, you may want to check out the other foot massager I mentioned. Remember though, it doesn't cover the entire foot bed. I adjust my feet when I use it to get the rollers where I want them. Link: smile.amazon.com/dp/B09P4P3DB6

title: Mostly MEH
text: I admit that I have higher expectations when you see that this is a reputable brand, Shaper Image. We have a different foot massager from them, and LOVE IT. This one, not so much. It' just a very meh product. There are Shiatsu massagers under the soles of your feet that spin and rotate. The top strap that goes over your feet then has air bags inflate and deflate to create a rhythmic wave like feeling as it causes the massaging nodes to press harder on the soles of your feet. Generally, I have not been a fan of any of the newer massaging devices that use inflated chambers to simulate a massaging effect. It always feels weak and borderline annoying. It's like having someone give you a back massage but doesn't press down with they hands/fingers and just does circular swirling motions. The next problem I have with this device would be the height of the massager. It's higher off the floor than most massagers, so it feels awkward and uncomfortable. Our recliners are a little higher than the couches, and it still feels a little off. Although the fabric is smooth and relatively soft, I worry about how this would hold up over time. Stretching over moving parts and rubbing dirty feet isn't a recipe for long device life.

Just feels like someone is pressing rocks into your feet.  Most "massagers" have rollers, but this has little "rocks" more or less, and underneath those are rotating rollers, and as they spin they lift and lower the little "rocks."  To simulate what I mean, touch the tips of all of your fingers to your leg.  then one at a time press down with one finger, then the next, then lift the previous finger, and just do that over and over, but pretend your fingertips are rough crunching stones.  Its not pleasant.  If this used a standard spinning roller ball setup it could be REALLY nice.  Like, REALLLLY nice.  But it doesnt.  So unless all you want is to feel like youre walking on LEGO, find something else.

title: Soothing but with an unusual taste
text:
The main “cold fighting” ingredient in this is Echinacea which, for some people, has been shown to help fight colds. I’ve taken it in the past in pill format with mixed results – sometimes it seems to help; other times not so much.

This is another way to get your Echinacea along with other herbs. The ingredients are:

Echinacea purpuera herb
red root
green tea leaf
elderberry fruit
thyme herb
red clover herb
myrrh gum

It’s in a base of vegetable glycerin and water, which gives it a syrupy consistency. On the plus side, that can help soothe your throat. On the downside, the taste, to me, was only semi-appealing. It’s not bad or medicinal tasting, just odd – sort of a semi-spicy taste that lingers on your tongue.

The dosage is 1ml (25 drops) 1 to 2 times per day. I like that it comes in a glass bottle with a good quality dropper rather than plastic. However, the country of manufacture is not listed nor is the concentration of the various herbs in it.

I can’t give it a strong recommendation since the taste is so unusual. It’s one of those items that you’re either going to find tasty or really dislike. But I found the taste odd but interesting, so I’ll give it 3.5 stars, rounded up to 4 since it did soothe my throat.

Worth a try but, as with any herbal remedy, don’t expect your cold symptoms to magically disappear.

title: 3rd Generation E.T.
text:
MY BACKGROUND:
I’ve had essential tremors in my hands since I was in my early 30’s. I’m now in my mid-40’s. I'm 3rd generation of essential tremors. (I don't know if it goes back even further than that.) My father also has the same symptoms. My grandmother has it more severely, but also involves head shaking side to side and her voice has tremors worse than Katherine Hepburn.

I was interested in the ingredients and thought I would post some very basic information about them. I really appreciate the combination of these quality ingredients backed by research. It’s aimed at treating tremors and prevention of further deterioration. (Because of the ingredients, I would give it 5 stars. However, read on and I’ll tell you why I docked stars.)

*Methylcobalamin (methyl b-12) 1 mg
---It’s a form of Vitamin B-12.
*Magnesium citrate 100mg
--There is evidence that some people with hypo-magnesium may have symptoms of essential tremors.
*Acetyl L - Carnitine 100mg
*Curcumin extract 100mg
--This is turmeric, which is very beneficial to health in myriad of ways, has also been found to protect nerves.
*Gamma-Aminobutyric acid 100mg
--There is some research that suggests there is GABA dysfunction with tremors.
*L-Tyrosine 100mg
*N-Acetyl Cysteine 150mg
--This has reportedly been found to be very effective in preventing further damage to some nerves due to oxidative stress.
*Skullcap 20mg
--This is a mild relaxant which is also used for anxiety. It has reportedly been found to ease tremors.

I didn’t experience any change in the tremors. However, I only took this for a month. Perhaps after a few months there may be results. I feel like this should be taken over a longer period of time to see if it makes an improvement. And of course I can’t vouch for preventative measures. At the moment, I can’t afford to continue taking it. If I had the financial means, I would take it for the possibility of preventing it from becoming worse. This concoction of ingredients at least gives some hope. And hopefully over time more studies will accumulate to further address essential tremors. At least essential tremors are now being recognized and understood by the medical and science community more than they had 20 years ago! So, although I love the ingredients and the possibility that it may prevent further deterioration, I felt like I had to dock it 2 stars because I couldn’t vouch that it would work, since I only took it for 1 month.

I value credible, informative, and candid Amazon reviews by other Amazon buyers and hope this review helps you. Although I received this product at a discount in exchange for my honest and unbiased review, I don’t spend all this time and energy to post non-truthful reviews. My time is worth more than saving a couple of bucks. I’m posting for your benefit. Please click “HELPFUL” if you appreciate the effort.

I was pretty impressed with this product. I am only 34, but I was diagnosed with essential tremor about 7 years ago. The doctors couldn't explain why, only that sometimes people in their mid to late 20's just wind up getting it (hooray for me). It's not *terrible,* but it gets pretty bad on certain days, especially if I haven't slept enough or I'm not feeling well. There are times when I can almost feel my whole body shake and can even hear it in my voice. Friends and family will notice my hands trembling sometimes and it's very embarrassing as I always worry someone will think I'm an alcoholic or something! Anyway, I didn't have super high hopes for any product to abate my tremor, but this one actually did make a difference! It doesn't make them completely go away (nor would I expect it too), but I do notice a marked difference on days when the tremor isn't super bad to start to with. When it's really bad it still helps a bit, but just not to the same degree of effectiveness as when it's a more mild day. If you're like me I'd highly recommend giving this a try!

As an additional tip for people like me, I recommend doing some research on supplementing with magnesium also (especially magnesium oil that you apply topically to your skin - it's far more absorbable by the body that way). Many, many people are deficient in that nutrient due to over depletion of our soils from commercial farming and other environmental/dietary factors in the modern world. It has an incredibly calming effect on your nervous system, so it's helped me a lot with my tremors and insomnia as well. Obviously you have to listen to your own body and do your homework on what's best for you, but I know it's worked well for me. Good luck!

text: I took Bergamot after reading numerous reviews about how it had helped bring down some users' cholesterol readings, but for me it did exactly the opposite. Even though I improved my diet (gave up red meat and started eating lots more vegetables) and exercise habits (started exercising for a least one hour every single day, up from 3 or 4 times a week) my cholesterol got markedly worse! I had a fasting blood test done just before I went on the supplement and again three months later and I was in total shock to learn that my total cholesterol went from 178 to 202, my HDL went from 45 down to 40 and my ratio went from 2.6 to 3.3. So I stopped taking it immediately. If you do decide to give it a try, please do yourself a favor and get your blood drawn two or three months later so that you don't take something which is actually making your health worse for too long.

title: If you want to know about Magnesium......
text:
As many now know, magnesium is need for hundreds of chemical processes in the human body. Most people buy it for muscle relaxation, sleep or to relieve muscle cramps at night, but there many other positives to taking magnesium. Almost everyone is low in Mg, unless they supplement. But here's the KEY, all Mg is not created equal.
The lowest quality, least soluble form is Magnesium Oxide. This is basically useless and is actually the "rust" or oxidated form of magnesium. This is also the cheapest and most magnesium supplements use only this form.
The next up the chain, with a little better absorption and a little more expensive is Magnesium Citrate.
The magnesium forms that are considered top tier, with best absorption is a class called chelated Magnesium. They included Magnesium Malate, Mg Theonate, Mg glycinate and bisglycinate and a few others. These are the forms that are the most soluble and the best quality......BUT they also cost the most.
This Magnesium uses a chelated form, which is one of the best. "Bisglycinate Chelate" is the form used in this supplement.
This supplement uses a superior form of magnesium, is more absorbable and more bioavailable. I personally take this and also recommend this to my patients.
Side note:. Too much magnesium, taken too frequently, will cause diarrhea, but you can work up the dose slowly to avoid this.

I have learned that not all magnesium supplements are created equally and that some forms of magnesium are more readily absorbed than other forms - the National Institute of Health notes "studies have found that magnesium in the aspartate, citrate, lactate, and chloride forms is absorbed more completely and is more bioavailable than magnesium oxide and magnesium sulfate." As a result, I switched from the less expensive magnesium oxide I had been taking to using more absorbable forms of magnesium. My research led me to find that magnesium diglycinate is one of the most readily available forms of magnesium for digestion. One study, entitled Bioavailability of Magnesium Diglycinate vs Magnesium Oxide in Patients with Ileal Resection confirms how much better-absorbed magnesium diglycinate is over the common magnesium oxide. As a result, magnesium diglycinate is one of the best magnesium forms available for absorption.

title: great for granny
text:
My granny is 95 and still as active as her 95-yr-old body allows her. She is fearful to mount her exercise bike after a tumble this past summer, and she misses the low-impact activity. She was skeptical when she opened her Christmas gift, but once we assembled it and set it up for her, she leaned back in her TV chair and started pedaling with a smile.

It's great for her circulation, and the tension is adjustable enough to suit her needs. It's heavy enough that it doesn't move around too much during use, and it's light enough that she can slide it away from her chair when she's finished.

title: Great Exerciser for my parents
text: I bought this for my mom. She has problems walking and her knees and hips hurt her all the time. Being that she is 78 years old, it is very important that she keeps moving. The Isokinetics Pedaler is quiet, easy to put anywhere and lets my mom sit in a chair that she is comfortable in. I thought she would not like it because it involves exercising but I was shocked, she loves it. She does not put any resistance on it, just the circular motion is enough  and she does it a few times a day. The resistance does not get super hard but that is ok because then she will not over do it. Trust me, I have tried a few other exercise machine but this one actually does the trick. Best of all, it is not a heavy machine, does not take up a lot of room, you don't need any fancy clothes and if need be, my mom can move it around. Plus, I don't have to worry about her falling off of it in any way. The fact that she is using it say it all. Definitely a great buy, would suggest it to anyone who has joint and knee problems.

title: Very disapointing item.
text: I was very much looking forward to this peddle machine since it claimed to be both compact, silent, and easy to use. Unfortunately, all three things did not pan out. While the exerciser is very slender, it is still much to tall to fit comfortably (or at all) under almost any office or home desk. Because of it's tall, narrow built it was also extremely prone to swaying side to side or even falling right over. Furthermore it's operation was far from silent, and while it didn't produce the same "whir" sort of sound a cheaper peddle machine did, it had a very distinct, ear-bending "Rrrh-Rrrh" sort of sound. Perhaps the sound was a side effect of the broken unit I received, though, as the tension settings didn't work at all. Despite reading the directions and checking online, no matter how I tried to set it, it was stuck on the lowest/least resistant setting. At least Amazon was very polite and helpful in getting me a refund.

title: pedaler
text:
this is a good product. the only problem is the plastic they used for the shell creaks when pedaling, and the more resistance, the more creaking. someone took it apart and lined the area where the two halves meet with electrical tape, and no more creaks. I plan to do that soon. once the creaks are gone, it will be almost silent.

UPDATE: i just added the tape, and the creaking is gone. totally worth a few minutes' effort. I used black electrical tape so it is not really even visible. i just unscrewed all the screws on the one side, and put the tape along the smooth seams, on the side with the lip. Wrapped it around the lip so half the tape strip is outside, half inside. I didn't bother putting it on the parts of the seam where there are ridges in the plastic--just on the smooth parts was enough to take care of the noise. It was not necessary to remove the pedal cranks in order to accomplish this--there is enough space after you unscrew the one side to get the tape put on. Much more pleasant without the creaking. The quality of the mechanics looked solid while I had it open.

title: Isokinetics Magnetic pedal exerciser
text: I have used my Isokinetics Magnetic Pedal Exerciser for years and I loved it. So this time I purchased one as a gift for my sister, who also praised it. title: Needs a yoga strap or other canvas strap to work

My display stopped timing after the first day, and the difficulty gauge doesn't seem to do anything.

So why did I keep it instead of returning it? Because with my attach-it-to-the-chair-you're-sitting-in trick, and pedaling fast, I got my heart rate up to about 135 beats a minute for half an hour - that's in my target heart zone. We have a small house, it's tough for me to leave my very high-maintenance family for long enough to go to a gym, and the weather in Chicago often prevents me from regular bike rides. At least I get a legitimate aerobic half-hour in with this thing.

title: Convenient day-to-day solution
text:
I've had a gastrostomy tube for about two months now, and I own two of these belts in size small, which fits reasonably well. It's nice to have one to wear while the other is drying after a wash (after hiking/cycling/workouts). My tube is a "dangler" and has a bulky Lopez valve on the end, so I don't use the hole in the belt -- I just put the tube and valve in the velcro pouch. The belt is comfortable and generally stays in place well. It's nice to not have to tape the tube to myself or use safety pin schemes which seem to invite inadvertent pulls on the tube when something catches.

It would be nice to find a similar product that dries faster (maybe lycra ?) which would lend itself to more outdoor use, but for me this is hopefully a temporary situation.

text:
Wow. Usually when you purchase a product that is not from a big name company, the issue seems to be that it is lacking in quality and power. This is the exact opposite of that. This prodcut, the Shiatsu Neck And Back Massager - FitPlus Shiatsu Neck Massager Pillow With 4 Heated KNeading Nodes 2 Year Warranty Car Chair Back Massager Pillow, is probably one of the most, if not the most, powerful massage products I have ever owned.
Now I would not exactly call this a pillow. It is a hard material, and a very well constructed one at that. It contains four roller points, and each one of them delivers a little slice of heaven and relieve to a tired and aching back.
The hard pillow type object has a strap on the back of it so that you can firmly affix it to the back of the chair you are sitting on. This is a very nice feature especially if you are trying to aim for your upper back. For me, it sits perfectly just at my shoulder blades, but you can adjusted to the height on your back that you are trying to make feel better. The unit itself is pretty lightweight and therefore easy enough to adjust, even while it is on.
It came with both AC and DC adapters. I have a massaging seat topper in my car already, so I use this at home at night when I come home from work. Besides, I really feel like this is too powerful of a massage function to be used in the car. It's much more invasive than your average vibrating seat topper. Perhaps if a passenger wanted to use it, that would be one thing, but this unit certainly should not be used while driving.
I have read other people's reviews, and I think it is important to mention that my unit had seemingly no smell at all and the heat function did not bother me at all and it heated very nice and gradually. The heat function seemed to intensify the massage feature, but I think that's a matter of personal preference.
I did receive this product at a discounted rate in exchange for my honest review. This in no way altered my opinion of this awesome product.

STAINLESS STEEL - The Modern Man® Nose Trimmer blades are constructed in stainless steel. It is durable, convenient, lightweight, and battery powered (batteries are NOT included). The high quality, sharp blades provide you with the smoothest, cleanest cut around!
WATER RESISTANT - You can use our nose trimmer dry, but it is also sealed to keep out moisture, so you can use it in the shower too. The wet/dry convenience makes trimming easy and comfortable, anytime, anywhere!

title: COULDN'T SURVIVE WITHOUT IT.
text:
I needed to place a cold ice on my knee as long a period as possible because II had total knee replacement and need to keep swelling down. Well Ice from the freezer placed in a freezer bag did not cut the muster because the ice could not be distributed over the entire area and I had to hold the ice on because it would slip off because the ice would melt and turn to water then warm up from my hot knee. So to was a constant trek between the freezer and the sink to pour the water out of the bag and replenish the ice in the bag. There was wasted time doing other things when I should be cooling my knee.
So this Aqua Relief System had eliminated all of the wasted time above. You put as much ice inside the unit and fill it with water to the maximum fill line, attach your pad to the hose, wrap around knee, turn the unit on and set to the cooling time, then relax , it will auto shut off according to the set time. No more running to the freezer during treatment for ice.. After one hour the unit still had cold ice in it.

The only problem I had was the small cooling/heating pad that came with it , so I ordered a larger one.
This unit is very light to carry around , It has holes for attaching a shoulder strap. It is also very quiet to operate. In fact the low hum of the motor caused me to fall asleep.
I recommend to anyone needing cold therapy or heating therapy that needs continuous treatment for at least an hour without interruptions.

title: I really like this stuff!
text:
I found this company on Amazon and actually ended up ordering from their website instead (they'll mix the flavors for you) but wanted to leave a review to address some of the things I saw people saying on here.

1) Some people were complaining that the beef protein "foams up" a bit when blending and that "true" beef protein would NEVER do that. I'm not a food scientist who knows the answer to these things, but I have tried other organic, 100% no filler beef protein shakes in the past and they did froth a bit just like this one does. So...I'm going to say a bit of frothing is normal lol. I don't think froth means that all these companies are liars who put sawdust filler in the product :D

2) Some people were complaining that they HAD to mix the flavoring in my hand (which is apparently waaay more physical activity than they're used to). So here's my thoughts:

a) Go order off their website and they'll mix it for you! Problem solved.... :D
b) If you want to pay a lot more money, there are plenty of other preflavored options out there for you, which brings me to my next point of:
c) The company saves money by not having to create an infinite amount of flavor/protein combos and store them alllllllllll which in turn saves YOU (yes, you, the consumer) money in the form of a less expensive but good quality product. If you were wanting to throw away all your dollars on an expensive protein drink, you probably wouldn't have hit the "sort by price" button that got you to this product, am I right?? :D
d) Maybe it's just me, but I'm not sure why some people are complaining that you get the option to CHOOSE your own custom protein base and additives and flavors. Like..........wouldn't you be excited to be able to customize what you want rather than being stock with a stock item? I really liked the ability to customize my drink, personally.
e) Some people were complaining that they didn't "like" a certain flavor (and to them I say: go pick another flavor then and don't dump the whole container in before trying it! It's super cheap and you can pick lots of flavors so why wouldn't you?) and were complaining that ALL the company's flavors weren't available on Amazon (and for those folks, I can say: um, go to their website directly and pick whatever you want??).

Honestly I'm very happy with what I got. I went directly to their website and picked out my protein base and my additives and my flavors. Some people complained that the flavors were too light (and some people complained that the flavors were too strong, thereby reminding us that you can't please everyone and your opinion is definitely an opinion and not fact) so I chose to go "heavy" on one of my flavors BECAUSE I could then just add more water to the drink if I needed to tone it down. (OOO another point! Your drink flavor too strong? ADD water! Your drink flavor too weak? Add LESS water? Magic...... You're not forced to use a specific fl oz ratio; you can customize what works best for you lol).

I even ended up getting a second container with a premade recipe that I thought looked good and I ended up liking that one too!

All in all, this is a really affordable, good quality product that allows for a lot of customization (particularly on their website).

title: Objective review
text:
I am an athlete and true with most, have experienced digestion issues with whey protein. In searching for an alternative that provides needed protein but is easier on digestion, this product is a success.
There have been some comments on flavor. I think they’re wrong. If your expectations are to have a childishly sweat and flavorful shake, then this isn’t for you. Knowing that there is AlWAYS a trade off, this product has a great flavor while giving you good quality protein.
Simply blend it with cold water and some ice, and drink it quickly.
If you’re an experienced athlete, and have had quality protein supplements in the past, looking for a better “adult” product, I highly recommend this one.

title: Almost Perfect Dairy Free Protein Powder
text:
(this is for the Chocolate Fudge Brownie flavour - I have not tried others)

The people on here complaining about the flavour have clearly not experimented too much with non-dairy protein powders. I have tried SO many different protein powders. I have followed a vegan diet in the past and used many different vegan powders, and I have also been a competitive bodybuilder and used many different kinds of whey and casein powders.

This is, hands down, the best *non-dairy* protein powder I have used - both texturally and flavour. Like a previous review said - if you are looking for this to essentially taste like a child's milkshake, then you wont be pleased (but bear in mind all the things that make it taste that great are probably not great for you). This protein powder tastes good. You're not going to write home about it, but it IS good. And it mixes beautifully, and has a smooth texture (unlike every horrible vegan protein powder out there).

But the best part is that it does not upset my stomach. I have a very sensitive stomach and currently have to follow a carnivore diet because of it, and this protein powder is seriously a miracle for me.

I have also heard great things about the customization options that this brand has through their website, but I have yet to check that out. Will definitely be ordering the 5lb bag!

I merely say it's not perfect only because I'm not a huge fan of stevia or sunflower lecithan, but I also understand that sometimes options are limited when you are creating specialty items, and based on my stomach's reactions I would say those ingredients are minimal.

Just as they wrote.......they sent me pictures of what they believed would work, top and bottom sides. I wrote back that I believed these would meet my needs. Therefore, today (8-17-16), I received my new insoles. THEY ARE AMAZING! I will write again, if you need insoles for whatever reason, you will not be in any way disappointed with Langten Speedfeet insoles. Jan C
spent alot of money to have insoles of which I did, not to mention to have them made specifically for you would be a cost I could not afford.

title: Yes, they look flat, but looks can be deceiving
text:
I admit I wasn't impressed at first glance (they don't LOOK like they would make much of a difference when you hold them) but my feet think otherwise. I've been battling tendonitis around my arch from poor support and adding these to my sneakers has made a HUGE difference. It's hurt my arch to put weight on my foot for the past 2 weeks and these offer the perfect amount of support for that, within a day my foot started feeling better and walking was easier. Pain assistance aside, my shoes are so much more comfortable to stand in!

Edit (after 2 months of use): I have noticed a huge change in comfort with these inserts. I tried to switch my running shoes to their standard inserts and could definitely tell the difference. Reference picture: yes, they do seem flat and flimsy but notice that there is a definite padding in the arch area. It's not a drastic amount of support but, remember, most tennis shoes (and boots depending on the brand/style) have a small arch built into the shoe, this small amount of padding adds to that arch. Unless you have drastically high arches, you should feel a difference with these.

text:
First at $9, it puts them at 9 cents each glove. Costly but desperate times, call for these to become a part of the new Coronavirus normal. Also, these food prep gloves are tight in the fingers for a large handed man, they ultra thin and when putting the first one on it caught on my wedding ring and tore a tiny hole on the backside. Fortunately, that little hole wouldn’t compromise the touch area even if it did happen again. The gloves come in a sealed bag labeled in a foreign language, not a box or dispenser. Likely these were counted out of a lager dispenser, but by whom? They are stacked neatly, not tossed into a bag. At first glance of the package you’ll be shocked that there could be 100 in that bag. I’m not counting/touching them all to verify the quantity. Being that they are thin, I’ll take it on faith that there’s probably 100 in there. They are definitely going to serve their purpose in grocery shopping, pumping gas, etc.

UPDATE: After reading a review here that said that they had received only 50, I was compelled to count the gloves. When I got up to about 70-ish I stopped counting knowing that there were most likely enough remaining to make the total 100.

title: Revised review after using for a while
text:
I've tried side to side comparison tests on multiple surfaces like rusted metal, tub soap scum & moldy grout. In every test both this product and my everyday cleaner did the exact same thing. There is no perk to using this over anything else. The down side to using this product is that it leaves everything feeling gritty, chalky and has to be rinsed off in excess with water. If not the item your cleaning looks dingy. Since there's things (like an oven range top) that you can't spray down excessive with water to remove the product, it is not worth it to use. This product did nothing on objects like rusty knives. I'm not sure what everyone is so impressed with. I haven't tried the spray cleaner yet and maybe that's better then the paste but for now I'm not very impressed.

Update: I'm hooked on the paste cleaner. I've never found anything to remove grease so fast. You know those plastic containers you can spend forever trying to clean grease from food off? This stuff should be carried pink magic. It's as though it immediately removes grease. COMPLETELY. Despite my original review of not liking this product I now give it 5 stars. I use it almost every day and will be buying again when needed. It doesn't work on rust but once you figure out how to clean with this product it will become your go-to cleaning product.

title: Very, very Mini but very functional.
text: I bought these as part of my "gear up for potential hurricanes and be prepared for all disasters" Then the box arrived and I looked at it and thought, "hmm I wonder what this box is" because I couldn't figure out what could be in a box that small.  As it turns out, THREE, yes THREE lanterns.  So they turned out to be a little bit smaller than I had expected.  Now this is entirely my fault as the dimensions are listed in the product description.  It does say mini, I just didn't expect them to be quite SO mini.  As for functionality, they work just fine.  The light is very bright and no complaints about battery life.  I was without power for 24 hours and the battery lasted the entire time (so I can't say how long the whole battery life is because the battery did not run out while I had them.) They're light (I mean this is the light-weight sense this time as opposed to the light vs. dark sense.) easy to carry around since they're small and really since they are small they are easy to store.  The only negative with them being small is the way the light is dispersed, with a bigger lantern you'd have more vertical area that would be dispersing light in 360 degrees whereas with this lantern it's a very narrow band that because it's so small.

title: In short, should you buy it? If you need one for your car, and have lots of extra room between you and the dash, then, yes
text:
I'm honestly a bit torn about this product. Frankly there isn't anything better on Awazon, but for the price you hope to really be in love with it.

I can say this much. As a 6ft1 guy, this thing is short. Simple solution, turn vibrator pad behind the unit, and just shift it up. That said, even before compressing the rig I'm already pushed knees to my dash. Not the products fault, my car's seat just doesn't mold well to it (very curved, sudo lumbar stuff). But at the same time, I'm hardly cramped in my car normally....

The massaging is really really rough. I mean, I foam roll with the jagged ruber spike torcher instrument. I will ONLY be using this after crossfit. I keep slamming it hard when I get in the car too, so when not in use it's out of the seat.

Aside all that pretty good quality all around. I can put a lot of force down and stall the motor, but it will rarely happen. Will it last 2 years? maybe.

Second. Vibro pad.. Really? It's weak, and it's clearly not aimed for the guys, cough. I wish it wasn't included so it would be easier.
Also note there is only 1 set of 2 massagers, not 2 sets like on the box.

Wish it could focus on just one spot, but it's clear a drive screw that makes it go up and down is also the part that drives the rotation of the massager. So impossible by design. Hey it's for your car.
In short, should you buy it? If you need it, yes, you aren't going to find a better one on amazon that works (CLEARLY) in the car.

title: Nice Case Fits Up to Ten 5ml, 10ml, or 15ml Bottles of Essential Oil, But Not as Snugly as Some
text:
I'm a huge fan of essential oils, and I'm always lookout to try new cases and find better ways to organize my ever-growing collection.

This essential oil carrying case fits up to ten 5ml, 10ml, or 15ml bottles of essential oil. The bottles are not included with the set, but are merely shown to illustrate what the set would look like when filled. The case is 6 x 4 x 2.5 inches in size and includes prominent branding on both sides of the zippered bag. I purchased the "purple" version of this case, which appears to be quite color-accurate to the product photos.

The case is soft, but has a small amount of padding on either side. I like that the pockets are black vinyl mesh so that you can see through to read what type of oil is in each bottle. The only problem is that since the openings accommodate 5ml, 10ml, or 15ml bottles, unless you're using the largest size, they have quite a bit of wiggle room. I would highly suggest the manufacturer consider making the edging that runs across the bottles out of elastic so that the bottles, especially smaller bottles, are better held in place, regardless of their size. There is also no padding between the bottles.

On the whole, I like this case, and would recommend it if you're considering a nice way to store up to ten of your favorite essential oils. Just keep in mind that it is not as padded as some other options out there.

I am a longtime Amazon Prime customer who enjoys writing reviews in my free time. I was appreciative to be given an opportunity to test and review this essential oils case at a discount for my honest and unbiased review. If you have any questions or comments about this product or my review, feel free to message me and I'll be glad to help!
