title: High Quality Omega-3 Fish Oil Improved Cognitive Function & Mood and Eased My Arthritis Pain
text:
Omega-3 fatty acids are essential to human health and can only be obtained through one's diet. Fatty fish like cod, tuna and salmon are the best sources, but you have to be careful because these foods can be contaminated with mercury and other pollutants. You can also get Omega-3 in flaxseed, walnuts and soybeans, but who is really going to eat enough of these on a daily basis to get an adequate amount? I know I'm not since I hate the bitter taste of walnuts and really don't like dried soybeans. Higher blood levels of Omega-3 essential fatty acids including EPA and DHA are associated with improved cognitive function and mood, protective properties for the heart, and possibly a positive impact on joints and flexibility for people with arthritis.

Taking a supplement may be beneficial, but a lot of the cheaper ones may contain traces of dioxin, mercury, PCBs and other contaminants from the environment. Not to mention the fact that you burp up the taste for hours. After trying several inexpensive brands including a free full-size bottle I received at a health fair, I decided that not all Omega-3 fish oil supplements are created equal. This one is as pure as you can get, has really helped with my cognitive function and mood, and most importantly - eased the chronic pain from arthritis. text:
As the care giver, I was excited to get my cousin this upright rollator. Reluctantly, I had to return it for his use.

PROS: It's pretty and is easy to assemble and disassemble with its instructions. It weighs less than our current comodita roller. It is way more affordable and was on sale for even less at the time. Encourages user to walk in upright position.

CONS: Not enough foot room for someone slue-footed. Was unable to completely rest forearms down in armrests. While can adjust horizontally, cant adjust vertically or diagonally. As a result, could not walk continuously and comfortably.
Too bulky to fit in my large car trunk (Chysler 300) without lowering arms and totally emptying truck. Too bulky to easily fit in back seat. Once I did, no one else can sit in back seat.

Side note:. Non Slue-Footed caregiver can use upright with no problem with foot room or armrest. Good for daily walk and back arthritis. Still has car storage issues. Don't have home storage for 2 rollators.

title: Nice But Barely Fits a Skinny Person
text:
The Rinkmo Rollator Upright Walker was easy to put together; however, I am a skinny disabled senior citizen who is 5' 9" tall, weighs only 145 lbs; and I barely fit between the handle bars when I sit on the Rollator seat (which is comfortable). I also wish the arm rests were 2" taller for a more comfortable fit. It is important to be very careful when rolling over any cracks on the sidewalk that is more than a 1/3 inch tall, as the Rollator tends to easily tip forward. The Rollator is very light (wish it was a little heavier and studier), and a little wobbly that can roll fast on sidewalks, so be sure to tap the brakes to slow down, otherwise an accidental fall can happen. I do like the two side handles by the seat, and I do use them to lift myself up to stand; this is a great unique feature that other upright walkers do not have, and the main reason for me to purchase the Rinkmo Rollator. So if you are my physical size or smaller, the Rinkmo Rollator will fit you. After using this walker for a few months, I've updated my rating from a 3.5 star 4 stars because I've learned how to use it safely. I've been using it everyday but with caution, and now I can walk a mile

Very Important:
Be sure to rest your elbows firmly on the pads to add stability when using the Rinkmo Rollator; when I first tried using it, I almost fell before realizing I have to rest my elbows firmly on the pads to keep the Rollator from leaning (falling) forward. This is especially important when you apply the brakes or when you hit a small crack on the sidewalk, otherwise you will fall forward. It does take a bit of a learning curve to be able to safely use this Rinkmo Rollator.

title: Good product and excellent customer service
text:
I ordered this for my brother who was badly debilitated by COVID. He is 6'2" and about 260 pounds. This rollator fits him pretty well considering how tall he is. His forearms rest on the pads and he has to lean forward a little bit.

He lost most of his hand and wrist function due to COVID so the upright position of the brakes is in the perfect place for him. The brakes have just enough resistance that he can safely operate them. They are secure and can lock when needed.

He used it pretty extensively for about 5 months when we noticed one of the forearm pads had cracked and the assembly for collapsing it had broken from so much use. I wrote to the company and explained how beneficial their product was and asked if there was a warranty or if there were replacement parts. They were very prompt and extremely accommodating and sent an entirely new device! My brother has now used that one for just over 2 months with no issues. He currently has 3 different walker styles and this is his favorite. He never uses it for seating so I cannot speak to that.

Pros:
Easy to assemble
Lightweight
Fairly sturdy at full extension even when used by a large man
Maneuvers extremely well
Upright hand brakes are easy to use and work well
Excellent customer service

Cons:
The trick to collapsing it is to reach underneath and release the clips. They are also attached to a handle in the seat (it lies flat so no worries when you sit down) but repeated pulling will stretch the metal clips and prevent them from working correctly.
Once fully extended (for my brother's height) the arms do not easily retract for loading into a car. I could have tried something like silicone spray and that probably would have fixed it, but I have a small SUV so it didn't matter.

Over all he is thoroughly happy with this item and the customer service. Of all the pictures I have of him, I don't have a good one of him using the rollator!

text:
Ok. they are affordable. BUT
One of the hardware packs was missing 1/2 the washers. I could let that go for the price. (What's a few washers cost?)
However, installation is a pain. The bottom bracket is too narrow (small radius) to mate nicely with my 4runner's stock roof rack. (Yes. they match the dimensions that the product calls out). It works but not cleanly. It would mate better if the bottom radius was the same as the top bracket radius. The REAL negative is that the 2 bolts that tighten the brackets to the roof rack are so long that there is not enough room between the room and the bolt to to install. Well, you CAN if you back the bolt out of the frame but then you have to monkey with trying to get the carriage head into the frame again, with the stuff on the end but you can turn the bolt...I'm not doing it justice as to the difficultly. I installed just the tightening nut (the nut embedded in a knob) and I could get it pretty tight, but after a short trip, they were getting loose as expected. Even if I could get every thing on, there is essentially no room for my hand to turn the tightening knobs. This is compounded by the other 4 bolts used to put the frames together being longer than necessary (~10mm extra sticking out below the nuts). It isn't like a 4 runner is a tiny vehicle and the roof racks are cosmetic. The straps are okay. I can see where others have had issues with them letting loose. I can make racks work with some modifications, but that's my time and money. Save yours and keep on shopping.

(Read last paragraph for proper application.)
I’ve tried about every brand and type of adhesive bandage out there to keep my prescription estrogen patch on. And keep it dry when I shower. Finally success with this product! I’ve included a photo. I’ve had this adhesive film over my patch for 4 days so far, and have showered and the patch is still in place and dry. It’s not bulky, and it doesn’t lose its adhesive quality like all the other things I’ve tried. I haven’t tried to remove it yet since I don’t change patches but every 7 days, but I’ve read others saying it was easy to remove.
BE SURE YOU DON’T REMOVE THE “OUTER” EDGE COVERING “UNTIL” THE PATCH IS STUCK IN PLACE. That outer edge keeps acts like a picture frame that keeps a canvas from wrinkling (and in this case, prevents it sticking to itself.) Once the inner portion is stuck to your skin, there is a cut in the framed outer edge that allows you to peel it off in a long strip.

I decided to MOVE my patch to a different spot, and discovered the clear adhesive film is easy and painless to pull off. Then I applied my medical patch with a NEW clear adhesive film to a new spot. All went extremely well. You cannot re-use the clear adhesive film; use a new one when you need to reapply.

I love this adhesive film!

Part of my problem is that I'm hairy, and part of the problem is that I perspire. I have to shave an appropriate area on my upper arm to apply my medication patch, but I've still had them fall off, sometimes in an embarrassing situation.

These are a relatively inexpensive way to keep my patch attached. They cause NO skin reaction, and as long as I place them correctly on shaved areas, they adhere fairly well, and they DON'T cause any discomfort on removal. They are MUCH more effective than the adhesive tapes I've tried.

Used in conjunction with a compression bandage I made by cutting an athletic sock at the ankle, and sliding the cuff up on my arm, they are 100% effective in keeping my patch in place for the full week, even in summer.

text:

Perhaps those who hated these are still eating other processed foods, because the first time I ate these after years of no treats or sugar, I absolutely thought I was in heaven! Perhaps they would taste gross to someone whose taste buds are used to regular chocolate and candies, but I found them to be absolutely delightful.

I love these so much, but I actually found that in the long run, they cause weight gain, so I no longer buy them. All sweeteners cause an insulin response, including stevia. Insulin is something absolutely undesirable in every way, especially when it comes to pursuing weight loss, since it can cause increased hunger and cravings. I cannot post links, but here are the titles to a couple of studies discussing the insulin response caused by stevia (google these and you should find them):

"Effects of stevia, aspartame, and sucrose on food intake, satiety, and postprandial glucose and insulin levels"
"Rebaudioside A potently stimulates insulin secretion from isolated mouse islets: Studies on the dose-, glucose-, and calcium-dependency"

title: Tastes Like Strawberry Quick
text:
We typically use SlimFast Keto shake mix for chocolate and vanilla, but of all the other KETO SHAKE options, this is my husband's favorite. We typically blend it up with creamer, ice, water, Stevia, and the KETO SHAKE powder. We live in Florida, and so smoothie-like shakes help get us through the heat of the day.

I am a chocolate shake fan, but this strawberry shake reminds my husband of NESTLE strawberry syrup to make strawberry milk as a child. He loves it!

I like it too, for strawberry, but as I already mentioned, I am a chocolate girl.

Some have mentioned issues with the color and strength of the flavor. Yes...it does NOT make a pink-colored shake...but come on, do you need food coloring to drink something that is strawberry flavored. I've always found food coloring deceptive anyway, and so the missing "pink" does not bother me. One less chemical to ingest if you ask me!

As for the flavor...it tastes like strawberry. But to bring out that flavor more, we add some extra stevia. We are sweet addicts (thus the need to go on KETO), and so an extra bit of sweetener really makes a difference. If you think the flavor is too weak (which I don't think is the case...I think people are confusing the flavor with the sweetness) simply add more sweetner and I think you will be thrilled with the outcome.

Thickness: the powder gets creamy in water, but as I mentioned earlier, we add creamer and water to ours.

To make 2 drinks...
Take a blender.
Add 1 cup ice.
Add 1-2 tbsp(s) pyure (to liking)
Add 2 scoops KETO powder.
Add 1/2 cup creamer.
Add 2 cups cold water.
Blend on high.
If too thick, keep adding small amounts of water until it is the right consistency.
Blend more.
Pour into 2 very large cups.
Add straws.
Share with your spouse!
Enjoy!

title: Good taste, stays "clumpy". $$$
text:
I ordered this product as it was listed as a "buy one, get one at half price" promotion, and it was created by the folks at Speed Keto, so I figured, sure, why not?

Pros:

Taste: I was looking for something other than chocolate, and this strawberry flavor is pretty good. it is very sweet tasting to me, although not overpowering. I like to add ice to it after blending and making an iced smoothie - yum!

Ketosis: I don't have this every day but on days when I do, I have not noticed any problem remaining in ketosis as indicated by ketone measuring strips. It isn't designed to be a meal replacement although I have used this as a meal replacement on days when I have fallen out of ketosis to get back on track again. So, it works!

Cons:

Price: When I purchased the product, the cost was $44.95 for one (about $67.43 for 2, or $33.71 each on promo). The non-promo price has since dropped by $5.00 to $39.95 each. I think it's way overpriced, although one can argue that everything that says "keto" on it is too expensive.

Blending Power: Not good at all! Even when I use a "Ninja Professional" mixer to try to dissolve all of the powder, I end up with too many clumps of dry powder within my drink, as compared to using Slim Fast's Keto powder in the same blender (which blends quite well, but really isn't all that keto friendly, but that's another story entirely).

The Bottom Line: In spite of what I think of the price, and the subpar blending results, I still ordered another container of their product: the salted caramel flavor. Overall, the impact to staying in ketosis is a big plus in my book. I also realized that there are plenty of similarly marketed keto-shake powders available on Amazon.com which are just as expensive, if not more so (per serving), than this product. If the manufacturer could just work on the recipe so that the resulting drink isn't filled with so many undissolved powder balls, then I would likely rate this product four stars, if not higher.

It has an adjustable blade length directly on the clippers themselves so you can add just a little more length or shortness to your cut. I personally only use them to trim the hair on my dogs feet because she chews on the hair between her pads when it's too long. She doesn't seem to mind these clippers and they work far better than the beard trimmer I had been using!

title: Love these cordless dog clippers
text: I absolutely love that these clippers are cordless. My biggest issue with other clippers was the cord and now I have these and they work perfectly. I feel like I did a faster cut with these today. True to the low noise and they cut with precision. It comes with 4 combs but I only used 1 (the lowest- 3) because my dogs hair is already short. Also comes with a cleaning brush and charging cable.

title: Nice clips and adjustability.
text:
I picked this item because we wanted to save money on haircuts for the dog. I’ve never done a haircut with this, but I would say it did a good job. I don’t know if they normally need to have more power to them, but this one seemed like I had to compromise a lot to get it to cut. I was cutting the hair on a poodle/Schnauzer mix and the guards didn’t seem to channel the hair properly to the blades. I ended up just taking off the guards and being careful with the trimming. I feel like this needed a bit more power to be more precise. Sometimes I had to hold the hair up and run this across it to cut it. It wasn’t very seamless. Like I said, I have never cut dog hair but it seems like I had to do a lot of compromise to get this to cut well.
I would buy this again because it is saving me money from sending the dog to the groomer, but it loses one star because it seems like it takes a little extra work to get an effective cut.
The blade seems like it’s a ceramic blade. I’m guessing that would help with the hair not pulling.

title: Nice
text: They work good. I just didn't realize they were pet clippers. They definitely work.

title: Wouldn't recommend for a professional
text: These pet hair clippers are advertised as professional dog grooming clippers. This isn't accurate. While the clippers worked fine shaving out my dogs' paw pads every few weeks, I don't think the quality is good enough to withstand hours of tough use every day. The body of the clippers and all of the accessories were plastic, and not the heavy-duty kind. So, if you're looking for a cheaper set of pet clippers to do some touch ups between grooming appointments these will work fine. However, if you are a professional pet groomer I would look for something of higher quality.

title: They work Great!
text: I have two long-haired miniature dachshunds and they’re always getting little tight mats under their armpits, behind their ears, and in their feet pads. I’d try and cut them but by time I got one in my fingers they’d freak out and I couldn’t do it safely or the scissors wouldn’t cut through. My husband opened these new clippers and called me over. Within 5 minutes we had every single mat off my dog. I didn’t use any of the attachments for this. The only time was spent locating the mat, once found these clippers removed them effortlessly! We couldn’t believe it. We even were able to get the ones in his feet by using the corner of blade. These cut so well you don’t even have to use your opposite hand for leverage like others I’ve tried. I then used the attachment and trimmed his hair. I am so excited to have these clippers and look forward to doing the next pup.

title: Great simple grooming clippers!
text: These clippers are great for quick SMALL jobs.  i wouldn't use them for a full groom, but they're AWESOME for fixing little areas or doing small interim trims.  They're especially handy keeping the underside of my Doodle's ears free from long sweaty hair.  It's handy that they're rechargeable so there's no messy cord to deal with getting tangled around your dog.  Highly recommend!

title: Worked very well!
text:
If you're like me, you read reviews before you purchase anything. No one wants to waste their hard-earned money! That's why honest reviews matter, good or bad, so here's my thoughts...

Pros: lightweight; quiet compared to my old clippers; cuts smoothly & evenly
Cons: absolutely none!

title: Great trimmer for our best friends...
text: I'm not a professional groomer, but I have a dog that needs to be shaved in the warmer months. He has some health issues so can't currently go to a professional, so I bought this to try and tide us over. It's very quiet and my dog doesn't mind it at all. It does need to be oiled fairly frequently, which is probably normal, and there is definitely a learning curve which is also normal. I wasn't ever able to get the comb attachments to work very well, but adjusting the blade height itself worked fine for us. The scissors are very sharp, and the clipper works better than expected. We are grooming a Maltese puppy, 4 months old. easy to use, works, and feels like a professional tool, they do a pretty good job.

title: Minor Flaws, But Does The Job
text: Having three small long hair dogs that need groomed frequently gets expensive. While I am by no means a professional, these are easy to use with a small learning curve to getting used to it. The clippers are smaller and lightweight, so you aren't holding a heavy clipper while near a small dog. They don't pull or snag the hair and the noise level is really low. The dogs don't get scared by the noise thankfully. The fact they are cordless makes them easy to use on dogs. I can't speak to cats because I've only used these on small yorkies, but I'm sure they work for cats too. I'll be saving us money each month doing standard grooming at home.

title: These work great!
text: This is my first time buying and using Pet grooming clippers and I have to say I’m pretty impressed with these! I wasn’t sure what to expect honestly, I sure didn’t think the charge would last through cutting two dogs without recharging but it did. The digital window that shows how much charge is left is kinda weird because it likes to stay at 88 even after a full charge. I did get it to view 99 but went back to 88 after a day or so, So i wasn’t even sure if it was holding a full charge but apparently it did we groomed both our long haired dogs and it was still going. It’s very low noise just as it advertises. I like that it comes with 4 different size combs to change for different lengths also it has a dial that you can turn for different cut lengths. This was very handy while trying to figure out how close a cut we wanted on our girls. It comes with a USB cord to charge it up and oil to keep the blades from rusting. I feel like this is a good price for what you receive. Good product! My dogs look great!

title: Thrilled to have this wireless clipper

Braggs has been a life saver for me. I have had so many health issues with GERD and my lower LES its been a nightmare that I started to give up. The doctor basically put me on PPIs such as Prilosec, prevacid 24hr, Nexium but they never did anything except make me sicker then a dog all day long.

I started researching APV but made the wrong choice in brand. I thought you could use ANY shelf ACV so I tried it for weeks but all I got was extreme burning and zero results. I decided to give up then after awhile I started researching again. Then it hit me I was using the WRONG stuff. I went to the store and bought a bottle of Braggs and the very first day about an hour later after I drank 3 teaspoons with 8oz water I felt alot of relief. Still the food still backed up that day because lets face it, It was the first day.

Been using this stuff a good month and what relief. Zero backing up or throwing up, No heart burn, pooping regular. Im afraid to stop using it now in fear symptoms will return so basically this will be my new daily ritual for life.

text:
Pros:
2 cases for the typical cost of 1.
Semi-Rigid shell for better protection.
Fits larger sunglass frames.

Cons:
Products smelled HEAVILY of smoke when unpackaged.
Belt-clip fob stitching of VERY poor quality.

I bought these to replace a softshell case of similar design (different manufacturer), used to hold my off-pair of motorcycle riding glasses. I ride to work before sun up so, I ride in wearing a pair of yellow lensed glasses in the morning and carry a pair of glasses with smoked lenses for the ride home in the afternoon. I don’t have bags of any kind on my motorcycle and I don’t ride with a backpack so, I rely on using the clip of the sunglass case to attach the case to a D ring on the beltline of my work pants.

My initial impression of these cases was overall positive, except for the extremely pungent odor of smoke that permeated both cases and was immediately revealed upon opening of the zip-lock type baggy they come packaged in. Unfortunately, my initial assessment was quickly proven inaccurate when after only 3 days of use (riding to and from work), the first cases carry clip nearly tore completely off (see picture). Wanting to give these cases a fair shake and understanding that once in a while, flaws creep into a products manufacture, I wrote the first cases near immediate failure off to bad luck.

Unfortunately, my optimism was repaid with disastrous consequences when the second cases belt clip failed completely on the next day’s ride into work, costing me not just the case but, my other pair of riding glasses that were in the case when the fabric securing the case to the clip failed and the case was lost somewhere on the highway during that mornings ride to work. Please, save yourself the financial loss and frustration of losing your own glasses. DO NOT BUY THESE CASES.

title: Work great for precise mixing and reusable.
text:
I use these to measure 2 cycle oil for small 8 ounce batches that I make when doing yard work. I have both 50:1 and 40:1 trimmers.

I did the math and found 4.81 milliliters gets me the 50:1 mix with 8 ounces of gas, and 5.91 milliliters gets 40:1 with 8 ounces of gas. Allows very precise and clean mixing. I use an empty Seafoam can or similar as the screw cap seals well and to avoid having lots of unused 2 cycle mix sitting around going stale. I use a measuring cup with funnel to get 8 ounces of gas spot on from my gallon container.

50:1 requires 2.6 ounces of 2 cycle oil per 1 gallon of gas. 8 ounces is 1/16 of a gallon. Divide 2.6 by 16 to get 0.1625 ounces of 2 cycle oil. Convert ounces to milliliters and you get 4.81.

I used the same formula for 40:1, substitute 3.2 ounces, divide by 16, get 0.2 ounces, convert to milliliters and get 5.91. Ratios stay the same and my trimmers are happy.

It's so hard to describe smells. I liked the smell of this, it's lightly fruity. And a test I have with lotions is to rub it on at night and then see if the scent drifts over when I wake up. This lotion passed my sniff test, and I am very picky about perfumed products.

text: I live in the southwest in the desert and this hand cream is awesome for fighting scaly hands. The scent is very mild and is very "hand lotion-y" and not offensive. The best part about the cream is that it isn't sticky on my fingers but really soaks in. Because I put lotion on every time I wash my hands it is nice that this isn't oily and cause problems using a laptop mousepad or screen. I'm really impressed with the Mountain Falls products and already use their face cleanser and really like it.

title: Mild, pleasantl scent cream which moisturizes well and tends to last at least the full day.
text:
Got this because I have 'lizard skin' in some parts of my body (mainly joints such as elbows, heels, and knees), and the wife gets severe dry skin on her hands off and on, especially in the fall\winter.

Has a mild, pleasant smell, is thick and applies easily, leaves a mild to moderate oily film for a while if you're over-generous (I tend towards that, myself), but no worse than most others I've used. Does, in fact, moisturize well and tends to last at least the full day. Skin creams\moisturizers are largely a matter of personal preference; Some people insist on no smell, or heavy perfume, others want a thin, watery cream that soaks in completely and leaves no film (unlikely anyone shopping for 'Intense moisture' falls into that category), and so on. I will say that I find it not offensive, effective at what it does for my, admittedly not ultra-severe needs, and will recommend it unhesitatingly.

title: The perfect unisex smell
text: We've been suffering severely dry skin with the coming of winter and my husband and I used this on very dry areas of the body, from hands to back. It's thick, spreadable, soaks in quickly, and does what it promises. The areas I applied it stayed moisturized for 12 hours or more. The scent is subtle. It's enough for a woman, muted enough for a man. The perfect unisex smell.

title: Love the Light Scent, Smooth and Absorbs Fast
text: This Mountain Falls Intense Moisture Hand Cream is in a small and convenient tube, that you can carry w you anywhere. It provides an instant amount of moisture, and if I had to describe the way it moisturizes/ protects, i'd say there's more of a wax base than oil or stickiness (like in some seaweed  products). The texture is thick and creamy,and you don't need much- maybe a pea size for your hands. The scent is very pleasant imo, and it seems to be a light mix of citrus notes over a floral base. Hard to say tho, since scent is so personal. I asked my son what he thought this smelled like, and he immediately said, "lotion."  oh well, there's that.  I'm liking Mountain Falls products, which seem to me to be a very good basics line, w/ their broad range of personal grooming products at very decent prices. This is a solid lotion for the price, and I'd use it again.

For the price I would recommend it.

You get what you pay for. I got this chair as an open box so I didn't pay that much for it. It is fairly comfortable and looks nice but...

The vibration is super loud. So much so that I don't use. The heat feels good, but seems to only work when the vibration is on. It's really light and slides around to easily to really function as an effective recliner. It may work for an office chair or a gaming chair in a child's room. I've moved it to my bedroom because it's not worth the effort to pack up and send back but I will be looking for a better chair for my living room.

It may be worth a couple of hundred dollars, but don't expect much and I would not pay any then that.

... as an added note a bolt fell out tonight, but I have no idea from where. I've had it for 4 days.

But just to be sure I took it off and tried turning it on. I would have been happy if it had turned on, but no 😑… so I put it back on the charger, this time for an hour… same result. Well I put it back on and honestly forgot about it so it’s been on the charger all day today.
You would think that it would be super charged by now and not have to be charged for a whole damn month and a half, but this snot catcher 2.0 is a gone with the wind. I haven’t even had it for a full year yet. But mostly, I’ve only used it 4 times since I bought it… and it’s little battery spirit decided that it had enough and took off…
Like I said, it’s a really good product. The only thing that bothers me is the fact that it seems to not live that long. I promise there has been no damage to my device. It’s been in its box hidden away from my toddler so that she can’t play with it, so I have no Idea why it’s dead. I tried to see if I could get a replacement, however Amazon doesn’t seem to want to give me one for a faulty product. I really love this aspirator, but I wish it would last longer. It’s been the only aspirator that my toddler likes so far and it’s convenient considering the basin being washable. I would have given the product two stars if I didn’t really like it. title: I LIKE IT! :)
text:
I have "been into" aromatherapy since the 1980's and I LOVE the current ultrasonic trend! I have several ultrasonic units of differing brands. When comparing my others to this one, I rate this product 5-Stars (the others would be rated less than 5-Stars, in comparison to this one). Nonetheless, I do have two details outlined below which caused me to "sigh" in disappointment.

THE GOOD STUFF: This diffuser is quite attractive & diffuses the stated durations, effectively (30+ feet away from the unit, I still enjoy my chosen scents). I use the continuous mist setting most of the time and the auto shut off works well when the water/oil mixture is gone. As an aside and to update previous reviews made about the cord.... the diffuser I received does have a BLACK cord, so to those reviewers, it appears you have been heard and taken seriously by the manufacturer!

DISCLOSURE: However, I was very disappointed to discover that the inner water reservoir is PLASTIC (not 100% glass which I was looking to purchase); also, the plastic is evident on the exterior top (opening) of of the unit (about 1/2" in diameter). Alternatively, I assume because the exterior IS heavy glass, the diffuser does become top-heavy when filled & is easily knocked-over if bumped or jostled; positioned on a surface that doesn't see much "action" when it is in use should alleviate this potential issue.

SUMMARY: If these 2 details, above, are not stopping points for you, I HIGHLY recommend this Aromyst Glass Diffuser: it is VERY good-looking...the exterior is made of quality (heavy) opaque, glass in a neutral but decorative "cut" pattern; it disperses the oil very well & runs continuously for a long duration. ENJOY!!!

text: I will divide my comments into pros' and cons for this. As an overall rating I think this is great because it gets to spots that you cannot reach yourself. Now while it is nice to have a fill blown massage chair that cannot reach your neck, this can and of course it doesnt take up the same space.  So PRO 1. PRO 2 it is composed of the traditional shiatsu rotating balls that we have all seen, they can go forward - backward or reverse direction and they heat up. Now the heat could be warmer, but thinking thru this if someone ever left this unattended it would not be hot enough to burn or scald so points here warm not hot - good. PRO 3 you can use this on just about any part of your body again you dont need someone to hold it to apply pressure so simple one person operation. The only CON that I can come up with is that the power cord could be a little longer -- this was simply solved by adding an extension cord.  The unit comes with the neck unit as shown in the pictures, a power supply cord that detaches and a cigarette lighter plug cord which for the life of me I dont understand. This is a superb single operator neck, back , massager that I have used. Totally portable and when not in use you can just put it in a drawer, it takes up very little space.  I love it.

title: Beat the Keto flu and stay in ketosis more consistently!
text:
I’ve done carb cycling for years and began noticing how much better I felt by my second low carb day. After doing a lot of research, I decided to give Keto a shot, mainly because of the rave reviews on how amazing people felt — including performance athletes. If you’ve looked into keto, you’ve heard of the Keto flu. On day 3 I became brutally aware of it when I had zero energy, felt sick to my stomach, etc. luckily, these arrived at the end of day 3 and within a few hours I felt somewhat human again. The next morning I was completely back to normal!

I take 3 in the morning and don’t eat anything until lunch (seemed to be recommended over and over by people.) Honestly, these were a life saver for me! I’m in nutritional ketosis and I truly think these are what’s keeping me there. I even over-indulged last night and had some port wine and after taking these, downing a bunch of water and a good gym session, somehow I am STILL in ketosis! These are the only brand I’ve tried, so I don’t have much to compare to, but so far I’m a big fan!!

title: Perfect for sensitive stomachs.
text:
The Sunwarrior Classic Protein is perfect for those who have a sensitive stomach. I have a sensitive stomach, and the other lines of protein by Sunwarrior make me really sick and sluggish. The classic protein is the only kind that does not give me any adverse reactions. I haven't eaten sugar for years, so the fact that this isn't sweetened with sugar doesn't phase me. I prefer it. I usually get the chocolate but occasionally get the vanilla. I love both. I use a blender bottle, and it blends it up really well. Occasionally I'll use my vitamix to blend this protein up in some unsweetened vanilla soymilk with ice. It's really good.

**UPDATE**
I've been using this product for 3-4 years, and whether or not the company changed the product, I cannot tell. The powder tastes the exact same as it always has, and I generally always buy the chocolate flavor. I've just started again on the keto diet, and this protein powder is working extremely well in between meals to keep my blood sugar stable as I'm adjusting to low carb. I still highly recommend this product.

text:
Since I've started using these my dental hygienist has raved about the condition of my gums. So I'm going to say the technology works. Unfortunately the execution of this particular device leaves something to be desired.

I can't comment on these devices crapping out after one or two uses, but I have found that not all apparently dead ones are in fact done for. I've found that some will come back to life if they're charged correctly.

The little metal pieces must be lined up just so and stay that way during the entire charge cycle. Unfortunately it's very easy to misalign the parts or to jostle them out of alignment. A pair of magnifying eyeglasses and a very steady charging station are invaluable here.

Although this has been a (temporary?) solution for me, this company is crazy to sell a consumer item whose maintenance is so exacting. They could at least warn people to take care when setting up the device for recharge.

Please note that Starlight Smile also sells a corded device. I haven't used one so can't comment, but if recharging this one continues to be a nightmare, I'll probably try it. My gums and my hygienist are happy, and it's worth some trouble to keep that going.

title: Callus remover
text:
I ordered this product for my husband to use. His feet are gross. He has calluses and dead skin. His feet crack and bleed. He works in construction, so he is on his feet all the time. I was excited to order this product to see if it really would work.

This O'vinna electric callus remover works great. Included in the box is an instruction manual, a cleaning brush, the callus remover, and 4 grinding rolls (3 extras and one already in the machine). It runs using 2 AA batteries that are not included, so make sure you have some on hand. My husband has used this product for 6 days in a row and we still haven't had to change the batteries, so it will last you a while.

This callus remover is small but mighty. It has a powerful motor that can reach up to 7500 RPM. This is incredible for how small this machine is. It is small and lightweight. Would fit very well inside a suitcase for travel use, and doesn't take up much room in your bathroom cabinet.

This callus remover is easy to use and hold. It is small and fits very well in your hand and is comfortable to hold the entire time you're using it. I love the grooves on the sides that make it slipproof. It is also high level waterproof, so you can use it directly out of the shower. The one downside I could find about this product is that it doesn't have anything to catch the dead skin, so make sure you use this product somewhere that is easy to clean.

This callus remover worked very well on my husbands cracked, dry feet. I recommend it to anyone who needs to clean dry skin off their feet.

title: Where the past meets the present
text: After practicing yoga and meditation regularly for a few years, I have developed an intuitive sense of when I am deeply calmed. When I reach this state of calmness, I can feel my whole body throb with my heart rate, I can then "clock" my inhalations and exhalations to my heart beat. I also see distinct visual patterns with my eyes closed. But I never knew if these sensations were indicative of a good practice of meditation or if I was just imagining the whole thing. The Healing Rhythms method works very well for me. It was a pleasure to see heart rate variation and Galvanic skin potential applied to the ancient practice of meditation in a visually pleasing manner.  I can achieve all the visual targets using techniques I have honed through my intuitive practice. The instructions that precede the biofeedback exercises are quite nice themselves but it sometimes feels a bit inadequate. Yet if you stick with it you can usually divine what you need to do (or what to let go) to reach the final state. I find myself closing my eyes during the practice and seem to get to the goal without much feedback.

title: For a sale item great buy

title: Upgrade and support issues
text:
I've purchased all the basic programs from The Wild Divine Project, and I've found them to be very helpful in developing useful biofeedback skills. Unfortunately, this company that creates expensive "enlightenment" software often disappoints me with their unenlightened business practices and unenlightened product support.

For example, they don't exactly make it obvious that there are no new biofeedback scenarios in the repackaged set sold as Relaxing Rhythms (formerly Healing Rhythms). It's all old graphics, albeit with an attractive new navigational interface, interspersed with some thoughtful discussion from well-known gurus. I'll bet many buyers were as disappointed as I was, to find out they'd been sold the same graphics twice. It's an old trick but I didn't see it coming from this company.

As another example, Wild Divine is currently (October 2010) selling only the XP/Vista version of their software for PCs, even on their Web site, though they have upgrades for Windows 7. Those upgrades will cost you an extra 20 bucks (each), but Wild Divine doesn't tell you that up front. (Why charge once when you can charge twice?) Again, an old trick, but I didn't expect it from this company.

I've also been disappointed with their product support. Their online information seems poorly organized, poorly communicated and incomplete. Some of their software still has annoying bugs that should have been patched out years ago. If you attempt to contact their tech support, don't hold your breath waiting for a reply. You may or may not get a response.

So yes, I still recommend this software, but it's ironic that the business practices of the maker are so out of sync with the intentions of their product. Be prepared for some frustration.

title: Great way to learn stress management and lower blood pressure
text:
It doesn't take much to increase medical bills if anxiety, stress, and blood pressure are a concern. Instead of spending an hour waiting for your doctor and then additional expense on prescriptions, use that time to learn breathing and relaxation techniques that you can use most anywhere.

This is not a quick fix, not a gimmick, it takes practice and patience, and the program gives you immediate feedback on your progress, and has the option to keep a history of your gains. There are various exercises and challenges. I found some easier than others, so each person is likely to run into something that will keep interest going for a long time to come. I anticipate it will be a while before I master all of the possibilities.

There are multiple levels of difficulties. If over the course of a year, a person spent 100 hours on this program, that comes out to about $3/hour to learn lasting stress reduction approaches that are built on natural principles, that can be used anywhere.

A good set up will help a lot - comfortable chair, quiet room, minimal external stimulation and interruption. Think of it as "quiet time" with yourself. Noise cancelling headphones can be used to shut out distracting sounds as needed. Others may have different experiences, but for me at least 30 minutes/session has worked, a couple of times/week. I find myself looking forward to it. I've done it as much as an hour at once, with rewarding progress. The better I get while hooked up to Healing Rhythms the faster I am able to induce relaxation while away from it.

The program instructions mention something that is absolutely true. If you are the competitive type and try to outwit the program, you won't get very far. The harder your try, the more you impede your progress. You learn quickly that "less is more."

If you are serious about managing unhealthy stress, are willing to do your part and take the time to pay close attention to your body and teach yourself natural approaches, Healing Rhythms will do its part to take you on that journey as far as you want to go.

I know there are other approaches for controlling blood pressure naturally. I haven't tried any others. This is to say that Healing Rhytms isn't the only way to achieve such goals, but so far my experience is that it is a good one.

title: Good product with lackluster tech support
text:
The program is simple and effective for learning the basics of meditation. The biofeedback helps refine the meditation process. Many books and videos intellectualize the process where this explains and guides your body as you go into a state of relaxation.
My reservations about the product are only in the area of tech support for the Macintosh version. The program is written for Windows and only uses a conversion program to run on a Mac. When the program had an error I reinstalled it but that didn't fix the problem so I contacted tech support. From the first email their only suggestion was to format my hard drive and reinstall the operating system.
The installation process adds and or modifies more files than just the main program file. I was able to find some of them on my own but not the one causing the problem. Wild Divine tech support didn't answer any of my questions directly. Instead they repeatedly made suggestions about reinstalling my operating system and not using time machine to restore my other files.
In the end I got the program to work at the expense of some of my personal files. The process of getting the program to work was very stressful.

title: Myth breaker
text: It was easier to me to understand what is concentrate my attention in only one single point. Keep me focused in that point. Finally learn that this is meditation... Nothing different than regular procedures we already knew. The great difference is the result we get learning how keep concentrate and increase our results in our regular daily life. title: READ THIS FIRST...
text:
I own the first two products they put out, Journey to Wild Divine and the Passage, with the original lightstone. If you own either of these you should recognize that this product is not really NEW. It contains much of what you already have. Also note that I can't use either of them anymore becaue they didn't upgrade the lightstone software. I also had an issue after I lost my disks. They told me they had no record of my purchase. Luckily I keep paperwork and was able to send them the original purchase order that came with the product...but it took a good deal of time to get through to them.

The problem here is that they don't appear to be a real hardware/software company, just product promoters who subcontract as needed. They purchased services to create these products which they have now re-assymbled by adding new dialog and an enhanced interface. There does not appear to be a full time programer on staff who sends out updates to registered users. As one viewer remarked, you have to purchase upgrades to Windows 7. That is not something a registered user should have to do, especially on a "new" product. This also suggests that there is no programmer on staff, so they pass the cost of subcontracting one to make changes on to you. They design and sell updates when they get complaints about things not working or when a new operating system forces them to. Unlike Heartmath, the company that makes EMWAVE they are just three men with reputations that can sell and a product that can be rehashed every so often for resale. Companies like Emwave produce new products periodically because they intend to stay in business. This should be another concern here. If they are rehashing old stuff, do they really intend to be around next year when you lose your disk or need a new driver for Windows 8?

text:

Anyway - as a first time user of happy lite/SAD/sunshine lights - here's my take. In the evenings I get very, very sluggish and dragging around. I took it out of the box, assembled it, and tried placement where I wanted over my computer. Although it was 9:30, I flipped the switch on and thought I would try it for 15 minutes - but no more. (Take 1 hour to get 10,000 LUX and in 30 minutes you get 5,000 LUX). Anyway, the little 15 minutes I used it I definitely could tell a pick me up. I felt a little more energy and clearheadedness. Really I did. I popped up and cleaned up a little in the kitchen and set myself of to knock out some paperwork. After a while I started to settled back in to a late evening sleepy mode. So - I say it works based on the brief exposure I had tonight. I can't wait until tommorrow morning to try it out for the full time. I look forward to having 'full energy' again during the remains of these somber wintry months, so I can get things done and not be walking around like a zombie.

RE: the cheapness of the product stated in earlier comments. Not a problem. It's not THAT cheaply made. It's a solid plastic cover on the outside and metal on the inside. The outer plastic cover (called a diffuser) lines up in the ridges ok, but one side seems to not exactly lay flat in the ridge. No biggy. I can live with it. I'm not touching it all the time and after all, I'm using it for the 'light' it produces.

It was MUCH bigger than the picture makes it appear. It is as tall as a shoe box standing on it's side. A little taller actually. I'd best describe it as the size of a half a bread box standing on it's side (the old plastic ones that nobody has used in the past 50 years). Or expect it to be about 1/3 of the width your computer hard drive box (assuming you have a standard one).

Anyway, I figure in the morning this will have the same effect as a good cup of coffee.
I look forward to having energy and being highly active all day and getting lots done!!
It is sure to help me reclaim my days and hours.

Yaaaaaaaaaay. I'm so glad I finally tried this!
I say if you have *any* slow, sleepy, fatigued, groggy, slumbering, lethargic symptoms at all during the day in the cold months - this is well worth the money!!!

title: Necessity for the unhappy cubicle monkey.
text:
No...it's not pretty. AND it's not a 10,000 lux lamp designed specifically for SAD (I also have one of those) but for what it is...it's perfect.

I work in an office with no windows. I've been working in an office with no windows for the last nine years. Every winter...work becomes nearly unbearable. The dry, overheated office air. No sunlight. Getting up in the dark...leaving from work in the dark. For anyone who suffers from SAD...it's like slowly descending into hell over the course of three months.

I use a 10,000 lux light in the morning with my coffee. It helps with the worst symptoms...and allows me to get to sleep at night. But it really doesn't give me the perk in the day like getting natural light does.

The Verilux light is just what it claims to be...supplemental sunlight. I start work at 8:30 in the morning...and keep it on the "high" setting until lunchtime. (When weather permitting, I try my best to spend at least a few minutes outside.) Then I turn it on the "low" setting for the rest of the afternoon.

The effect that it has had on my productivity is dramatic. My eyes stay open at my desk. I can concentrate. I am no longer contemplating grabbing my belongings and making a mad dash for my car in the middle of the day. (And unemployment.) I keep the light behind...and about 45 degrees to the right of my computer screen...so the light is almost in my peripheral vision...and have had no problems with eye strain. To the contrary...I find that I have a greater ability to focus...and need to take fewer breaks.

The only cons are that the light is a little flimsy. If you have a dedicated desk and can just set it up and leave it...then it's totally worth it. If you need something portable...one of the smaller LED lights will hold up better. And it's NOT a SAD light. But it IS a great supplement to the outdoors for those of us tied to a desk all day.

title: It's Far From Perfect
text:
The Deluxe Pedal Exerciser from Isokinetics Inc. Isn't a perfect piece of exercise equipment, but works well enough to at least keep you active during the work day. If you're like me, you work anywhere from eight to ten hours a day, and exercise is definitely a necessity, but not necessarily something you have the time or desire to do once you get home at night. This machine helps me keep active by allowing me to peddle here and there throughout the day, and keep my metabolism moving and calories burning.

Now, with that said, this is not the kind of "bike" I would recommend for someone who is looking for a fast paced, heart rate raising workout. It's a light weight piece of equipment, so it probably wouldn't hold up to that kind of routine, nor does it function well when used as such. I find it's perfect for a nice paced rotation of the pedals, and it keeps me from being sedentary all day. The end result is that hopefully I'll drop a few pounds here and there as my metabolism speeds up, but I'm not necessarily banking on that.

It's important to note that your weight could be a key factor in how well the machine operates - if at all. I'm roughly 260 pounds, and I was able to keep the pedals rotating fairly fluent without the machine moving or shifting. Someone else in my office who was roughly 120 pounds couldn't even get the thing to work. It wobbled, and slid on her. Admittedly the pedals are a little stiff regardless of whether you get it working right or not, but I'm hoping with use that this will ease up over time.

For now I give it three stars. As long as it holds up to the use, and keeps me mobile throughout the day then I'll be getting what I expected for my purchase.

title: An ideal humistat for any humidor other than just travel-dor's!
text:
Suffice to say up until the past week over here on the eastern seaboard, it's been extremely humid and extremely dry outside, and since I'd been out of town the week prior I had one of thirteen humidors that needed a decent boost in humidification while I was away. So I placed the order via Neptune through Amazon the Saturday before the 30th of June, it arrived a few days later, well within sufficient time before I headed north. A little background on said humidor, it's a large glass-top rosewood Savoy that has never kept a decent humidity level even with a large Diamond Crown humidifier which was empty every other week for seven+ years, and I'd seasoned it well over a dozen times; approximately a year and a half ago I had pulled the DC from the humidor and plied it with crystal jars and humisticks. They've been fluctuating the humidity between 63-78%... Not ideal at all; however after the short prep time of thirty seconds with the "nano-pearls" that are in all the Cigar Mechanic systems, that one pouch inside of a 100-150ct humidor even with the all those crystal systems has systematically isolated and regulated the humidity at a steady 72%. I think I'll be snagging at least two-dozen or so more of these bags for the rest of my humidors.
[...].

title: Beads are the way to go for proper cigar humidification
text:
I did a lot of online research and after all was said and done, I was "sold" on the beads 2-way humidification capabilities. As soon as this product reached my door, I threw away my old "foam-based" humidification system that came with my humidor. I combined using beads with a transition from analog to digital hygrometer (an important shift!). Analog hygrometers may look nice, rustic, pretty, what have you, but they are terribly unreliable. Get a decent digital hygrometer; you won't be disappointed. Back to the beads: After switching, I noticed how much steadier the humidity remained inside the humidor and also, how much *less* I had to tend to it (i.e. add water). The only reason I didn't rate this product a 5 was for it's packaging. Shortly after I purchased this item, I found another product that came in a disk with an adhesive/magnet system that mounts on the inside lid of the humidor. I purchased that and started using it; strictly because I retain more space in my small humidor (50 ct) with the disk mounted on the lid's interior vs setting this bag in a small bowl in the bottom of the humidor.

As far as this product is concerned; it's aces! I would like to see them come out with a mountable disk-type option.

You cigar aficionados, if you haven't already

1. Ditch the foam humidification system. Literally, throw it in the garbage; it's no good.
2. Get your beads!
3. Get a digital hygrometer (Mine's a Xikar; I'm sure there are a few different brands to choose from)

Your cigars will thank you.

I doubt most people would even notice the mild beet flavor, but I have a profound abhorrence of beets, so I'm uber sensitive to the flavor and can pick it up in things where most people wouldn't have a clue it was even there, so unless you loathe beets as much as I do, it's probably not a big deal. I only notice the beet flavor when mixed with straight water. If you make a smoothie using this powder, vanilla protein, a few frozen strawberries and coconut milk, It's absolutely delicious and I don't pick up on the beets at all. This product is definitely on the pricey side, but as with most things in life, you get what you pay for. I would order this again.

title: Carefully crafted antioxidant red blend
text:
I have a bunch of "Greens" blends but wanted to round things out and try a "reds" blend. I've tried probiotics by this company before and they are unique in that they don't just resell some random blend but actually research and make unique, science based supplements. Given my experience with their probiotic and what I knew about the company from then I was excited to try this.

This blend basically has 4 components: a phytonutrient/antioxidant blend with a variety of red berries and beets, some medicinal mushrooms, some gluten free grains, and a small bit of probiotics. In addition this is sweetened with monkfruit, my favorite sweetener. You can tell they really put care into these ingredients because for example they do mention they used fruiting bodies, and they could have used stevia or even some junk coconut sugar and they did not.

I have tried this a few different times and it is just a neutral pleasant beet type flavor maybe with a bit of a berry undertone. I wouldn't recommend this just on its own but I don't think many of these powders really are meant to be just thrown in some water and washed down. If you are thinking of it being particularly "berry-y" it's more of a beet type powder. In any case I haven't had any problem with things I've mixed it in with as long as a beet and sweet taste is OK in that food.

The reason I took off a star is because it is pricey and I'm not sure if I'd get it again due to this but I do think it's justified in this case as they used premium ingredients such as fruiting body mushrooms, went of their way to get GF grains, sweetened with monkfruit instead of stevia, and so on.

text: I love the look of this scale, but it's accuracy is way off. The box that this scale was packaged in was a little scuffed up, but nothing too damaging. When I first stepped on the scale it read my weight but the C popped up meaning the measurement was off and it needed to re-calibrate, which is to be expected the first time you step on it. So after it re-calibrated I stepped on it again and it and my weight reading seemed to be more accurate. I wanted to test out the accuracy so I stepped on the scale for the third time and my reading was different. Then I stepped on it a 4th time and it was different again. I probably stepped on the scale about 10 more times and received 5 different readings within a 10 minute span. The range of weight difference was over a pound. Whereas some people may not see this as a major issue, I am a woman, that pound counts! That's one more glass of wine I could potentially have if I chose the lowest weight reading. This scale is just not as accurate as I'd like it to be. I don't want to have to second guess if my scale is reading the correct weight every time I step on the scale. I also don't want to have to step on the scale several times to prove that the weight shown is indeed the correct weight. All in all, I'm going to buy from a different company. title: Making a huge difference in my life
text:
This review is for the blue cloud tri-core pillow. I am an average-sized woman with a largish head and shortish neck, which I mention in case that helps someone else choose a pillow size.

I was always a stomach-sleeper, which was so cozy and comfortable for me for 38 years, but I believe it contributed to my current neck problems. A few months ago, I began to have debilitating pain in my neck that made it impossible to even turn my head. I saw an orthopedist, who told me that my neck vertebrae were on the verge of rupture. She recommended a cylindrical neck pillow from a big box and beyond store, so I bought one.

I found it really impossible to sleep on that cylindrical thing. First of all, it rolled out from under my neck a hundred times a night. And it made me snore -- the angle of my head caused my mouth to fall open while I was sleeping, so I would wake with a sore throat. Also, staying on my back was the only option; if I tried to roll to my side, it caused intense pain. I went back to sleeping on my regular pillow, but on my side. (I can no longer sleep on my stomach, which vexes me.) My neck pain was still horrible every morning when I awoke.

I saw this pretty cloud pillow online and hoped it would be the answer to my prayers. So far, it is! I've had it for a couple of weeks, and by the third day, I was used to sleeping on it, and my neck pain is absent for the first time in months. I start out sleeping on my back, but rolling onto my right side or left side no longer causes problems because the pillow is firm enough to support side-sleeping. I have also stopped waking up with a sore throat, so I think this pillow isn't causing me to snore even when I have to be on my back.

title: Expensive but Effective
text:
MagSRT provides a higher dose than other available slow release formulas, and avoids the digestive distress that can be associated with regular release versions. However, given the cost, I would not recommend this as a first line magnesium supplement - try a regular release version, then a lower dose slow release if needed, and use this only if you require both the slow release and the higher dose.

This version of MagSrt also provides B vitamin supplementation (B6, B12, Folate), which they say enhances absorption of the magnesium. The evidence for this is quite thin - some limited in vitro studies, but no in vivo human trials with positive results that I'm aware of. That said, there's no particular problem with the B vitamins being in the mix, except you may be taking something you don't need. Jigsaw does offer a B vitamin free version (MagSRT B Free), although the cost is the same.

The pills are large, but not absurd (as some supplements can be), and have a uniquely smooth coating that makes them easy to get down. They have no particular odor or taste and no aftertaste. They can be split cleanly with a pill cutter, although I don't know what impact this has on absorption.

Four stars for quality, one off because of the cost. A years worth, at the recommended dose (4 pills/day) is over $250.

title: UPDATE below: Adorable, but not very effective
text:
Update:
Our baby girl is sick with a cold and this little gadget has been a lifesaver. While a manual nasal aspirator still offers better suction, our little girl tolerates this WAY better than the NoseFrida and actually smiles and laughs when we use it. The highest setting can get the most stubborn snot out but does take some poking around. No worries as the snot tip (wide, rounded tip) is soft and doesn’t bother her. The music and lights keep her engaged at not swinging her head from side to side.

All great things as far as an update goes BUT… the instructions say to boil the parts to sanitize them, including the snot collection cup, but the plastic pieces did NOT survive boiling water. I’m hoping the seller can send out replacement parts. So DO NOT BOIL THE PLASTIC PARTS despite what the instructions say.

Before our son learned how to blow his nose, we used the Nose Frida exclusively to remove snot and boogies. For our new baby, I thought I’d give this cute little device a try. First off, it’s adorable! The lights and music are great for distracting little ones who aren’t too keen on having the snot sucked out of the faces. There are several songs you can cycle through to find your little one’s favorite. You can also cycle through the suction strength to find one that’s effective for you. Unfortunately, even on the highest setting, the suction was still lacking, when compared to the manual Nose Frida. This can still work well for those who aren’t fans of the manual booger sucker, and definitely a better option than the ones the hospitals used, but it does fall short for us. I’ll keep it for the times when baby isn’t cooperative with the Nose Frida as the lights and music make it much more appealing than the blue tube.

text:
I purchased this as a lightweight backpacking solution. In theory, it is! But I haven't used it in the field for a number of reasons:
(1) It just seems like an awkward thing to carry because the attachment doesn't fit neatly into the bottle (it rattles around). You should be able to screw the nozzle back into the bottle in reverse so everything's self contained. I'm not sure how to carry the attachment (I don't want it touching my gear and don't want to carry something extra just to protect the glass.
(2) Glass - why? It seems fragile and I don't want to break it in a heavy pack.
(3) It should come with an extra cap for the bottle so you can carry water inside the bottle (then when you need it, the water is ready to go and you don't need to grab your hydration system to fill it). If you're in a rush, I can't imagine this being a quick process.
(4) Carrying the extra water it requires to use is heavier than a roll of TP.
(5) Cleaning the device when backpacking seems like a mess all by itself

I'll give this 2 stars because it's a decent idea, but need to subtract a few stars because it isn't practical enough for real-life use. Not to mention it's way over-priced for what it is. text:

I automatically realize how weird my tooth feels…realizing that all that glue was left behind to stick to my tooth. All night I tried to get this glue off my teeth. I can’t even close my mouth right to eat or anything!! Desperate, I get online to the reviews of the order and slowly realize that these are molds!! The glue it comes with is what goes inside these molds to “form” the fake vampire teeth that you then have to buy your own glue for to place the formed vampire tooth to your tooth. You DO NOT glue the fake mold to your tooth!

I am in tears bc this will not come off my teeth and I have great teeth! 5,000 dollar mouth that is now probably ruined because of this product! Nowhere did it explain this! The directions make it sound like you place the mold to your tooth! Wtf?! I’m so mad right now and so uncomfortable!

Make sure you read the product reviews fully before ordering!!!

title: High Quality
text: I ordered these on a Wednesday and they were delivered 3 days later so I'm already impressed with how quickly this seller shipped my shoe stretchers out. I ordered two so I could do a pair at the same time vs. one shoe at a time [since these aren't sold in pairs]. My first impression is, these shoe stretchers are very high quality. They're HEAVY - solid wood, and I slid them into a pair of size 9.5 pointy-toed 3.5" heels without a problem. I placed the 'bunion button' where I needed it - I don't have bunions but these shoes need to be made wider [I have narrow feet, so I now know why these Nine Wests were on sale... lol], so I need to stretch them out to be able to wear them all day at work. They're man made uppers with patent leather, so we'll see how it goes, but I have a feeling it's going to work great. I've already been able to widen the stretchers a second time after leaving them in for a while. I'm excited to stretch out a few more pairs of heels I avoid wearing, so in the end these shoe stretchers will more than pay for themselves in 'saving' several pairs of shoes I may have eventually donated having never been worn for than to dinner a couple of times. I read a review at some point that said they couldn't get the shoe stretcher out because they couldn't get it 'in reverse' - if you squeeze them [and your shoe] while you turn them counter clockwise, they will narrow out again so you can get them out. I didn't have a problem.

text:
I have owned about a dozen shoe stretchers - from Target - over the years. The Target shoe stretchers look similar to this one - albeit with a shorter handle and without the angled last. The target stretchers have a plastic end on the screw and a plastic plug. I break a Target shoe stretcher every few years - the plastic plastic end separates from the screw or the screw device becomes stripped and inoperable. I continue to repurchase only because I need it and it never dawned on me I had other options.

The problem is that my Target shoe stretcher never worked with my high heels. It has no angle, so it would not go in deeply enough or create the tension that is necessary for it to actually stretch a high heel well. After wearing a pair of expensive and agonizingly tight high heels over the holidays, I searched for a specific "high heel stretcher." I bought this one - really because it had the best reviews. It looked remarkably similar to the Target version I own, so I expected it to be a similar stretcher with an angle that works for high heels.

I was very pleasantly surprised. This stretcher is incredibly well made, the handle turns smoothly and the bunion plug and screw mechanism are metal - not plastic. It was easy to operate. At first glance, it may look like my cheapy target version - but it is FAR SUPERIOR to it! There is nothing flimsy about it and it works really well. I am sure it will last for many, many years. Do not hesitate to buy it!

title: Simple DIY Laundry Detergent for Seriously Sensitive Skin (read below)
text:
I make my own DIY laundry detergent with this brand of washing soda and just two other ingredients. I'm sharing the formula in this review. It's simple - just three ingredients, and cost effective. This is for folks with seriously sensitive skin, e.g. autoimmune issues etc. One proviso: this is not for laundry with heavy staining, e.g. motor oil, but for normal laundry with mild-to-medium staining. For heavy staining, I recommend treating the stains with vinegar first. Also note: never use borax or the two popular-brands of castile soap as these are likely to irritate sensitive skin. Also, when handling washing soda, throw a face-mask on to avoid breathing in any particulates.

Have a large plastic or glass container with a screw top to store your DIY laundry detergent in, a one-cup measuring utensil, and a cheese grater. If purchasing a 5lb bag of washing soda, also purchase 5lbs of pure baking soda (I use Arm & Hammer). If purchasing a 10lb bag of washing soda, purchase 10lbs of pure baking soda, i.e. always a 1-to-1 ratio. Scoop 3 cups of washing soda into your container (with your face-mark ON) then 3 cups of pure baking soda into your container. Use a cheese grater to then grate 1 bar of Cetaphil Gentle Cleansing "soap" into the container. Finish off by scooping 2 cups more washing soda and 2 cups more baking soda. Close the container tightly, turn upside down a few times to distribute the 3 ingredients around inside. Whether using a top-loader or front-loader washing machine, the process is the same. Use 1/2 cup of the DIY detergent per load. Load half the clothes, shake half the 1/2 cup in over the clothes. Load the rest of your clothes, then empty the remaining 1/2 cup in over the clothes. I hope my DIY laundry detergent serves you as well as it does me.

title: Excellent Pair of Cleaners for Laundry & Dishes, Very Fine with No Lumps
text:
I have made my own laundry soap for years and two of the chief ingredients are Borax and Washing Soda (Soda Ash).

This is two 5 lb bags--one of Borax and one of Washing Soda. Each is finely ground and no lumps which makes them easy to dissolve when making my laundry soap.

I have a liquid version and a powdered version. I am currently using my liquid version.

For the liquid version I use
3/4 cup super washing soda
3/4 cup borax
Shake well to dissolve in a 1 gallon jug about 1/4 full of warm water then add water to fill the jug leaving room for the
3/4 cup Original Blue Dawn
This makes 1 gallon of laundry soap which uses 1-2 TBL for front loader or 1/4 c for top loader for fresh, clean clothes.

The powdered version uses
1 bar (5 oz.) Fels-Naptha laundry bar, grated or run through the food processor
2 cups (14 oz.) borax
1 3/4 cups (14 oz.) washing soda
Instructions
Grate the entire bar Fels Naptha (or other laundry bar soap using the fine side of a cheese grater or food processor.
Pour grated soap, borax, and washing soda into a large mixing bowl.
Stir to mix well then transfer mixture to quart-size or larger container. (I like to run it all through a food processor to make it all very finely chopped)
To Use: Add 1 tablespoon powdered laundry detergent to the wash load. You may need to adjust depending on your conditions and washer size. You will not need much to produce excellent results.

I go back and forth on which I use depending on whether I can get some fels or not.

As you can see, these bags of Borax and Washing Soda will last me a very long time for my laundry needs which makes these a good value. And they come right to my door!

title: Very satisfied with Nic-Out
text:
UPSIDE:
After using numerous boxes of these filters I've never came across a cracked one, as some reviewers have.
It's true, the filters DO NOT change the taste of the cigarette, and they catch most of the garbage that would be going into our system.
And for me, as a 30yr smoker, my cravings have fallen big time. I've gone from almost a pack a day habit to 4-5 smokes a day (consistantly for over a month). YEAH!!
When I look in the mirror, after brushing, my teeth are noticeably whiter (family and friends have told me so).

Now, for the DOWNSIDE:
Nic-Out claims that each filter is good for 5 smokes. For me, they're only good for 4. The 5th time I use it, the tar and nicotine slides back onto my lips making a pretty nasty taste, besides the fact there is no draw factor.
Sometimes, even on the 4th use, the draw factor is clogged and barely useful. This doesn't happen often and I have turned the filter around and blown the clog out, then it works.
Often, the yellow fiter (inside the unit) is all cockeyed so I have to use my tweezers to sit it in it's place.

The downsides might be kinda annoying but they're not a big problem that isn't easily fixed.
I hope you all have as good experience with these filter as I have had!

title: Great start to the perfect kit
text:
Just got my kit today. It looks like a great little kit. I was pleasantly surprised by the hard cloth case. This is actually great for having cold packs in because if they get smashed or broken then they won't be useful when you want them. Now we won't have to worry about cold packs in our soccer bags already being "used" when a child actually needs one. I think this is my favorite feature of this item and probably the only thing to consider when thinking about how much you are willing to pay for this item as many of the other items are cheaply replaceable. For example, there is a big assortment of wipes and bandaids - this makes up the majority of the kit. Most of these things you can probably get fairly cheap with sales and coupons.

I didn't care for the tweezers as they are big, plastic awkward things. You will probably want to replace them.

Also, the inside plastic dividers were a little confusing. I am assuming you may be able to buy more of them as one of the plastic items has velcro on both sides, but only one spot to connect to in the case. Maybe you can add on plastic dividers and connect at the velcro spot? The cases do not have a solid closure but really just a flap that goes over. The big inside pockets can be handy for larger cold packs or other large items you might need in your kit.

Not sure I would pay $24 for the kit, but I do think the product is a great start to a perfect first aid kit. There seems to be lots of room in the case to add the things that are the most important to you along with a few simple things to get you started.

title: Effective and Durable
text:
These things make washing your hair (or your dog's fur/skin!) so easy. I'll use these forever. They detangle gently when properly used, relieve scalp itchiness or head pressure, and speed up the lather process of washing ones hair.

As a per brush, it pulls a lot of shedding fur out and makes scrubbing your dog easy. The rubber spikes massage and pull undercoat out gently when your dog's fur is wet.

They do eventually tend to get water inside and mold as the pressure from scrubbing your scalp with it pulls the rubber from the plastic and creates a crack for water to seep into the handle, but by then, it's normally time for a new one anyway, as the spikes become less firm (like a toothbrush almost) and even discolor over time due to effectivness of scrubbing the scalp.

I will say that because of the eventual moisture-inside-the-handle issue, the transparent scrub brushes are the ideal choice. With the opaque ones, you won't necessarily be able to see when water is inside.

Plastic use could also be reduced... it feels wasteful to get these every 6 months to a year.

text:
I recently found out that I need to go on a anti-inflammation diet, and most of the protein mixes out there have ingredients that cause my inflammation to act up in not so great ways. Despite the reviews that hurled down curses on this mix for its sweetness, I went ahead and ordered it, and I haven't been disappointed. In fact, I've re-ordered it many times. When I was first looking into the anti-inflammation diets, especially the Whole 30, I came across some people who approached it with a near religious fervor, ranting about their epic battles with their sugar dragons. My dudes...relax. You ain't battling dragons. You're putting down the Twix bar for once. Just because this tastes a little sweet from the monkfruit doesn't mean you've committed a mortal sin.

I haven't noticed any skin or hair benefits from the collagen like many people report, but that might be because I'm freakin' old. My skin and hair have pretty much thrown in the towel.

Bottom line: if you're looking for a protein mix that won't make your dairy, gluten, chemical sensitivities flare up, order this. Drink up.
