title: Delicious caffeine delivery device - but keeps you wanting more
text:
The reviews show mixed opinions on taste and texture - my experience with the espresso version is that they tasted wonderful to this coffee lover (coffee ice cream is the best!) and were moist and chewy as I expected from a Clif bar.

The caffeine is a nice morning pick-me-up, but I'm not convinced tying the caffeine to a Clif bar is a wise idea. First off, I want to eat two or three and I'd never have that much coffee during the day otherwise. So I'm tempted to have them when I'm hungry even if I don't want the caffeine hit. It is something I have to keep away from the kids also as they are tempted. If I a healthy snack, there are many options, Clif and otherwise. If I want a caffeine hit, I can do it with fewer calories, be it an actual drink of coffee/espresso or some other caffeinated beverage. The times when I want both a snack and a caffeine hit are more rare.

Overall it is a very good product, especially if you have more will power than me and don't have to worry about teens eating four espresso's worth at a time.

title: Coffee lovers will love! It’s like chewing a morning cup...
text:
One of the more interesting developments in the world of bars are these mini espressos.
Had 3 tasters try them at once & here’s how it went:

~ wow, they’re small
~ glad they’re small because they’re strong
~ it’s like eating crushed coffee beans & brown sugar
~ they’re chewy & easy to eat
~ I could see having these on a long car trip instead of spilling hot coffee
~ not for kid’s lunches!
~ 65mg caffeine is about a 6 oz cup of coffee or 1 espresso
~ $.56/ea. isn’t crazy for a quality small bar loaded with caffeine
~ 2/3 would buy again & the other would still have a cup of coffee with a White Chocolate Macadamia Clif bar!

(Thanks for reading this review & I hope that it’s Helpful!)

title: Clif bars for the win!
text: Gotta love the good old clif bar. They really delivered on their original quality and creative ingenuity. These are just the right size for a snack at work (see my picture comparing the size of the mini bar to an original sized one I had on hand). They look really dark in color...probably just because of the coffee that has been added. You can really taste the espresso flavor, though it is very pleasant.

title: like chewing on coffee beans in a tootsie roll
text: I realize that this bar is "espresso" flavored, but I expected a little more depth and complexity than something which tasted like chewing coffee beans. The ingredients list includes other flavors, including chocolate, but I couldn't taste them at all. I also wasn't a fan of the texture, which was on the gooey side with little crispy bits scattered throughout. I liked the crunch, but was less a fan of the gooey parts. text:

I like that they offer this downsized "mini" version the bar (but maybe just a little too small) and I also liked that they incorporated the equivalent caffeine of one espresso shot (you can definitely tell). I also like the added grit that I assume is from ground espresso beans.

They are almost too small, however, a normal Clif bar is definitely too big for a snack and too small for a meal replacement (I know that's not what they are supposed to be). Overall, the size may hit the sweet spot for many and the taste is amazing! I will definitely purchase these in the future!

title: Review of Espresso Flavor
text:

This brownie does not disappoint. I ate one and it gave me some umph to cut grass in 92 degree heat the other evening. I will say that even getting this in the mail, they did not melt or anything. I like that it is a small snack instead of the larger bar; too much of a good thing and all.

title: Strong coffee flavor; satisfying treat for coffee fanatics
text: The espresso mini bar truly tastes like coffee; it gives an instant punch of flavor on the first bite.  It pretty much tastes like a soft, solid form of the liquid beverage.  The mini bar is not large--approximately 1 oz--and contains 100 calories.  The consistency is not exactly moist, but it's not dry and crumbly, either.  I did not find the bars to have a 'granular' taste of coffee grounds.  The flavor is not particularly sweet, so I was surprised to see each bar has 8 grams of added sugars.  It takes me four bites to eat this mini bar, if that offers a sense of snacking proportion.  Each bar is purported to contain one shot of espresso, though I can't say that I feel any noticeable jolt of energy after eating one.  However, as a big coffee fan, I am fairly well-caffeinated most days, so the effect of the espresso shot may be lost on me.  Still, these mini bars provide for a very pleasing afternoon treat.

title: Great pre-work snack!
text: This snack is great for when you need a quick energy boost before work or even in general! It tastes great and gives you a good amount of energy and I haven't felt a crash since using them (I've eaten about 8 so far). Clif bars never fail to deliver!

title: Nasty Coffee Taste
text:
These aren't very good. The texture is what you would expect of a Clif Bar. That's the not quite cooked, chewier than you'd expect brownie texture. If you've had a Clif Bar, and you don't mind that, then don't worry about it. The thing here is the flavor.

This isn't for coffee lovers. And it's certainly not for espresso lovers. This is for the long-distance biker or runner who needs energy on the fly or right after a workout. They will tolerate the taste (maybe). Nobody else will.

Imagine the worst coffee you've ever had. Maybe it was at a gas station on I-80 near Joliet. You know, the kind that's been sitting there for a few too many hours. It wasn't good when it started and it didn't get better. The Clif Bars here aren't this good.

The coffee flavor is stale and overcooked. I think they used real coffee. But they didn't use the good stuff. And they didn't use the mediocre stuff. They went much deeper in the barrel for this stuff.

As you can imagine, I'm not at all thrilled with these. I don't recommend you buy them. And I don't recommend you accept them when your friends offer them to you. They're that bad.

--Brockeim

title: great inserts for stinky feet!
text:
Hi all -- first disclaimer: I have purchased about 20-packs of these liners, and I put them in EVERY pair of shoes I own. Now, ChuShu has asked me to write a review in exchange for one packet of their liners. Needless to say, I'm writing it -- but not for the one packet (although I do need to re-stock!) but because I truly think these are the best shoe liners I have used in years. I live in Baltimore, with 100-degree days, as well as sub-freezing days. Either way, I hate to wear nylons because my diabetic feet sweat, and my shoes were developing the familiar 'sour stink' thank simply cannot be cleaned out. I was, as others have mentioned, throwing out shoes that were not worn out because of the odor. Then, I found these. They are a shoe saver for me. I really do wear them in all my closed-toe, and peep toe shoes. I do not wear them with sandals, although I may try that this coming summer.

My only recommendations are that they make these a tad wider (make them for 'wide' sizes, and those of us who wear 'B' width can trim them if needed. Right now, they do not cover the width of my B-width shoes.) The second suggestion, along with other reviewers, is that they improve the 'sticky' material on the bottom. I have found that some stick like glue, while others move around -- and it does not matter if your shoe 'sockliner' is make of leather or vinyl. I have not used them in fur-lined shoes, so a merchandising line for that would also be nice. Nor have I used them in shoes with a 'Nubuck' sole, like my sandals have -- I will try that this summer.

I strongly recommend these liners. They really do help keep the odor down, and help to eliminate some of the 'stickiness' your toes feel after wearing shoes for an entire day at work. I'll be ordering more - and waiting to see if they start making them wider and tackier, too!

title: ... in the mountains where I was having too much fun and forgot to refuel
text:
This stuff has really saved me on a few occasions out in the mountains where I was having too much fun and forgot to refuel. It pushed me away from the wall faster than anything else I've tried.

Pros:
1. It works fast, faster than the GU Roctane that I will also use from time to time. In fact, after taking this stuff in, I can literally feel the surge of relief and boosted endurance in my muscles within ~10-15 minutes. Nothing else I've tried gives me such a noticeable boost.
2. The unflavored version doesn't have any flavor (or rather it has a neutral bland flavor). It is what it is.. that's a big pro for me.
3. Using a blender, I can make a calorie dense liquid that will last for hours and hours. I like to do (3) scoops in 20 ounces with 80 calories of electrolytes for 500 calories.
4. It's relatively cheap. As of this posting, this stuff is 111 calories per dollar. But you'll need to mix in your own BCAA'a and electrolytes to make it a more complete intra fuel. That could get expensive. By comparison, GU Roctane is 50 calories per dollar so it's more than twice as expensive (for the variety pack), but it has electrolytes, BCAA's and OKG to make it a more complete fuel. Maybe blend (2) scoops Vitargo and (2) GU Roctane together to make a 500 calorie super fuel?

Cons:
1. It doesn't mix that well on the go. Drinking a clumpy energy drink is distracting and I don't like it.

2. The high absorption rate causes brief stomach distress directly after ingesting. I've almost upchucked this stuff a few times, I had to slow down and walk a few minutes until the nausea passed. I think I can experiment with taking smaller sips more often to fix this, but for now I am calling it a con.

title: First impressions of Vitargo S2
text:
So, this is my first use of Vitargo so I am not giving it 5 stars yet. I use it as a post-workout recovery supplement. Decided to give it a try after investigating the product from various sources such as Bodybuilding.com. The premise behind this product is that it is suppose to help rapidly restore the body's skeletal muscle glycogen levels that were depleted during vigorous exercise. Per the advertisement, it can also be used pre and intra workout but I find with a proper diet I can push hard in the weight room without it. I would rather use something like C4 or Jacked3D as a pre-workout. So what did I think?

I was a little concerned at first about bloating. After mixing it per the instructions and adding a scoop of BSN Clean Whey, this was a lot of liquid to consume (somewhere around 28 oz.) I am happy to report that my fear was unfounded and the claim of no bloating is true. I can also report that I did not experience any gas as reported by a few others. However, as with any other product, your results will most likely vary from mine. My body sucked it right in and my stomach fullness was gone in minutes. Almost all of it was pulled directly into my muscles and I experienced less post-workout fatigue immediately and the following day. So far I give it a thumbs up.

I found the product mixes well with water (I use a shaker cup). It does froth up which gives the appearance of there being more liquid than there actually is. If you follow the instructions, mixing should not be an issue. I use the tropical fruit flavor. The taste is tolerable which is a nice way of saying I would not drink it by choice but it is worth it for the benefits. This is of course personal preference and you might love or completely hate the flavor, texture, etc.. Stay Strong and Fight On.

Update 1: So...after about a month I can say I am sold on Vitargo and use it religiously three times a week post workout. All else being equal in my diet and workouts, I am seeing a noticeable improvement in my physique. They do recommend that you take a second serving after intense exercise of over 1.5 hours. I have not tried that yet but might as my recovery time has slowed down slightly. In the end, I think if you are serious into weight training and gaining muscularity you should consider adding this to your stack. If your goal is just to stay fit you could probably find better places to spend your money.

title: If anything, a really good multi-vitamin product.
text:
Who doesn't want thicker, fuller hair? I know I do! As someone who suffers from Hypothyroidism, hair loss is a daily frustration, so when I had the opportunity to receive this product at no cost in exchange for an honest review, I was extremely happy to give them a try!

So....what did I think?

If anything, Will’s General Super Hair Growth vitamins are a really good multi-vitamin product. If you look at the label, there isn't any magical ingredient that would cause the hair to grow super fast.

The smell is not too bad and the pills are easy to swallow in my opinion. During my evaluation of this product, I did not experience any bad side effects.

I will continue to use these vitamins until my supply runs out in order to see if hair growth is noticeable. As of right now, just normal growth has occurred. This product is full of the good nutrients I need anyway, so I will continue to use this product until it's gone, if for anything, my daily multi-vitamin.

*Update 6/11/15* After taking 2 bottles of these vitamins, I will have to report that there was not a bit of SUPER hair growth obtained by taking this supplement. If you are looking for a good multi-vitamin, then this is a good choice. If you are looking for a product that claims to grow your hair super fast, look elsewhere......this product does not live up to it's claim.

title: Works great!
text: Works perfectly with my Audeo Marvel M90- and 2018 LG TV via optical connection.  Allows for both the TV external speakers and the optical audio to this device at  the same time.  No lag at all in the audio.  Once initially connected to the hearing aids the box will automatically connect every time the TV is on and you are in range (in the same room).  When you walk away out of range,  your hearing aids will chime as the signal drops out.  When walking in range they will connect with no indication.  Actually wish I could turn off the chiming.  If you walk in and out of the room a lot with the tv on it can be a bit annoying but other than that I’m very happy with the device.  My new hearing aids are a great improvement over my 6 year old previous hearing aids  and I’ve been able to get away from using closed captioning.  The LG TV also has a “clear voice” setting which also helps a lot.  But this is icing on the cake, for perfect audio.

title: Phonak TV connnector - a wonderful add on for Marvel hearing aids
text: I have had the TV connector for only a few days but I am truly impressed with the sound quality streamed to the hearing aids.  The TV connector includes both the analog 3.5mm cable and the optical cable for connection to I believe virtually any TV.  I have both TV sets one with the 3.5mm plug and a newer smart TV that has only the optical sound port. I connected to both and to my ears I believe the sound seems even better with optical port.  The sound is so crisp and  clear that it seems someone who does not have hearing loss may in fact want to use hearing aids just to couple to the TV connector when watching TV.  The amazing thing is my TV sound is turned down to 1 which is virtually turned off but the sound streamed over to the hearing aid is excellent even at that setting.  It is as though the TV is broadcasting to me personally as every little sound made in the telecast  is heard by me.  I can even hear the sound in other parts of the house where there is no TV set.  Someone may say I have the hearing aids and therefore why does one need the TV connector.  The answer to that is the sound is so, so much better with absolutely no background from any other source.  I am happy to have purchased this device from Hearing Accessories on Amazon. The item was shipped very quickly and they answered several questions for me prior to the sale.  They appear to be a very reputable seller of this product.  This device has generated a renewed interest in watching some TV programs for me.  It is a great addition to the marvel hearing aids.

title: Something works, I woke up pain-free for the first time in over a year
text:
Got a free pair of the low intensity rings (not neodymium) over 10 years ago. I was pretty sure he was a scam artist, but just wanted to get my free rings. When they didn't arrive quickly, I fired off an email to him complaining. To my surprise, the rings really did come a little while later after a nice apology from Alex.

I didn't notice much out of the free rings, but I did notice a little something and since he had instructions on how to build your OWN rings right on his website, I decided to do a little test. Still skeptical and not wanting to give a scammer any of my money, I found a website which sold neodymium magnets in the range his website suggested and created 2 rings according to his instructions, with a compass to determine which side should face up. Once I had it all figured out, I wrote a big R on one ring to indicate it should be worn on my Right pinky and an L on the other to indicate it should be worn on the left just to make sure I always wore the rings correctly.

I wore the rings a couple times back then but noticed they gave me really bizarre energy spikes and seemed to almost give me anxiety or something. I was in my late 20s or early 30s and I was just worried they were doing something unhealthy, so I stopped using them and wrote Alex off as a quack.

Fast forward to last night. I am now almost 42 and I have had increasing pains in my legs, joints and especially problems with my feet. It's really weird when you start developing pain for apparently no reason. I have to make an appointment with the doctor soon, but at first I attributed the pains to low magnesium, ill-fitting shoes, and straining my body with starting a new yoga and walking routine too forcefully. However, the more time that has gone by (over a year now), I began to suspect it's some underlying health issue, which is why I need to see the doctor for a complete checkup again.

For the past year, I have had what I believe is plantar fasciitis. The yoga helped for over a year until I sprained my big toe and had to stop. Still, when I would wake up in the morning, my heel and hamstring were tight and sore and required stretching, which is the basic symptom of plantar fasciitis. The bottoms of my feet begin to hurt if I stand too long or walk too much. My ankles and knees also hurt if I exert myself too much running. My lower back often is a bit sore because I have swayback and if I do not do abdominal exercise regularly, it starts to LOOK like swayback and also gets sore. Again, the yoga greatly fixed this problem: I had a straighter stance without belly tipping forward and butt sticking out (makes you look 20 pounds lighter and about 2 inches taller) and this also meant I had no pain in my lower back, not even if I slept too long on a bad mattress. Yoga was the answer to most of my prayers until I had to stop doing it. I am very much looking forward to the day my toe heals up so I can begin again!

ANYWAY, with all these pains increasing and not being able to do yoga or run, I bought night splints to stretch out my feet while I sleep so that hopefully my plantar fasciitis will be healed eventually. And I bought several supplements which I have been taking for over 6 months now trying to address any deficiencies which may be the cause of this apparent degeneration. Nothing has really helped much as far as I can tell.

LAST NIGHT, on a whim, I got up from the couch and found my homemade "Alex Chiu" neodymium rings and put them on before I went to sleep. I did not put on my night splint for plantar fasciitis. I woke up today with no pain in my feet or back and feeling well-rested after just 5 hours of sleep. I went back to bed for another 3 hours, which borders on too much sleep for me (especially after doing nothing but lay on the couch the previous evening) and still woke up with no lower back pain.

I have no idea what the rings did, but it is obvious they did something. My guess is they improved circulation which may have in turn moved something carried in the blood that may settle in the extremities of legs and feet, but that doesn't explain why my lower back doesn't hurt.

I can honestly say that I wish I had worn these rings when I first made them now. I will definitely be wearing them every night for the foreseeable future and if anything interesting happens, I will update this review.

These are homemade rings, but if I feel they really start to improve my health, I might just buy the very expensive (and most powerful) foot bar magnets as a way to say thank you to Alex. He certainly has received a lot of negative attention for his website and I was one of the people who made fun of the site back then, too. I got a free pair of rings from him, learned how to make my own, and never gave him a penny or even thanked him. Instead, I continued to joke about the website with people online until I forgot about it. Now I feel like a complete jerk because there is no way my pain-free body is a result of anything but these rings. I have woken up daily with these pains for over a year now, there is simply not a day that I get out of bed and don't stumble immediately to the wall to stretch out my hamstrings due to pain. Today I did not. Last night I wore the rings. End of story.

I started wearing these rings when I was 20 years old & 17 years later I don't believe I've aged a day. I still get sick & depressed, but not moreso than I did in youth. I didn't expect to look like I'm 25 or get carded for a bottle of wine at 37.

I originally didn't plan on writing this review until I was 50. By that time, I reasoned, there could be no ambiguity between my chronological age & my apparent age; some 40 years olds might pass for 25, but no 50 year old could. I still intend to update this review when/if I do reach that age, but I feel compelled to write something here. Some who read this may not be alive by the time I am 50. I encourage people, especially older folks, to give these a try. You can order these rings & wear them every night without anyone knowing except your spouse (if you are married). You have nothing to loose but a relatively trivial amount of money & the rather dubious pride of a cynic.

title: Life changing!!!
text:
My oldest child has been horribly motion sick in cars since he was 6 months old. Nothing we did helped. If he was in the car for more than 10 minutes, he'd lose it. When he turned 2, we started him on Dramamine. The Dramamine has worked for years, but it's not exactly convenient. It takes an hour to kick in for him before he can get in the car, or he'll throw it up. And he needs it every 3.5-4 hours, instead of the usual 4-6 hours, so he hits his daily limit faster than normal. And they are DISGUSTING, so it can be a battle to even get him to take them.

He's now 9 and that's been our routine for 7 years. I saw these things and figured they were worth a shot since we've tried everything else.

Today we took a 1.5 hour drive to a nearby lake for a day in the sun. He put these glasses on (along with a pair of Seabands on his wrists) and we hit the road. By the 30 minute mark, I became cautiously optimistic. By the hour mark, I became hopeful. And when we pulled into the park, I was in shock. He hasn't made a trip like that without puking unmedicated since he was 6 months old!!

For the trip home, I feared it was a fluke. I spent the first half hour expecting his usual "uhoh, I need to throw up" followed by instantaneous vomit. But no, he was drifting in and out of consciousness due to exhaustion from swimming for hours. At the hour mark, I got excited. He was awake at that point and calmly staring out the window. And when we rolled into the garage, I could have cried with joy. 3 hours of driving within 12 hours, completely unmedicated, and not even a funny tummy.

I don't honestly know if it was the Seabands, these glasses, or a combination of the two, but I know I'll be buying more sets so there is a "kit" in every vehicle.

This changes how we live our lives. We can be spontaneous and just go places. I don't need alarms to remind me to give him his next dose. I don't need to worry about forgetting to buy more when he's running low. And he doesn't need to stomach those nasty pills anymore.

We are planning an 8 hour drive to Disney World this winter and I was incredibly worried about how it was going to work with him. Plus the rides! Now I'll just put a band on these glasses so they don't fly off and he can wear them on the rides that could cause him to get sick. The relief I feel is unbelievable.

TRY THESE!! I know they don't work for everyone, but for our family, they are a blessing.

I will say, my ONE criticism is that they come in that case that is pictured, but they are shoved in there so tightly that the frames are bent at a wonky angle and can pinch the nose a bit. They are more concave then straight. I've been trying to bend them back and the kid says he can do the same when they start to feel pinchy and it helps for awhile, but I do wish it wasn't an issue because these things are a godsend. This issue isn't bad enough to stop me from buying more though!!

title: Nice, strong massage, but all settings are the same
text:
[[VIDEOID:f4dc4c038460254b3c6d84f812c5d24e]] My wife's feet are always hurting and, therefore, she's always asking for foot rubs. In order to ease her pain and my sanity, I thought I'd give this product a try. Before I even got home from work on the day it was delivered, I got a text from her, "the foot massager rocks!" That is certainly a good first sign. After I got home, I ran it through its paces.

There are 4 options under Auto and 3 options under Custom. Clicking through all 7, they did not feel different whatsoever. Exactly the same. That was a little disappointing. Putting it into manual, you can select between 3 different speeds and then select if it moves forward or reverse. Apparently this is the setting I'll be using on this, since the others are all the same.

The remote is useful if you are like me and have a little belly that makes it hard to reach down and touch your toes when seated. You have to point it really close and sometimes press the button more than once, but it works.

The actual massage is pretty nice. Its deep and rough, so if you are looking to get your foot tickled, this machine is not for you. It will borderline hurt sometimes, but it really gets in there and massages your feet. My wife is a size 7-8 and I am a size 12, but narrow feet. I could see how, if you had wider feet, this might be a little too tight.

As far as long term reliability, the jury is still out. If you search around Amazon, you can find this exact unit badged under many different names. The 3 with the most reviews are [[ASIN:B00F7SC2K6 Kendal]], [[ASIN:B000C1KUHA Tripact]] and [[ASIN:B004EXOFVY Carepeutic]]. Looking through those reviews, the average rating is about 4-stars, but you'll find where some had issues with reliability. The problem with a unit like this breaking is expensive return shipping costs due to size and weight. Have a read through some of those reviews and decide if its worth the risk. If you really need a product like this and can't afford the ones at Sharper Image, it might be worth the gamble.

The video clip is a brief view of it working from the top view (with some slight Christmas music and my newborn in the background :-). I received this product at a discounted price in exchange for my honest review.

title: Finally, A LARGE Compostable Trash Bag!
text:
Most compost bags are between 1-3 gallons. Our composter is about a mile from the house, so tiny bags are a pain because we tend to leave them outside where they get invaded by ants before we feel like taking them out to the compost pile. And anyone who composts knows those bags (unless pure paper) don't ever really break down in the composter. With these large bags, we can put about a week's worth of compost in a large 13-gallon stainless steel trash can before having to trek it out to the compost heap. I have tried several brands, this is a keeper. I need a compostable bag that holds up for at least a week. These bags did not leak, tear, smell, or break down. I like the small box it comes in that fits small kitchen draws.

Hope you found this review helpful!

title: Some limitations, but overall a good compostable bag
text:
These are nicely done compostable bags. The material is thick enough to deal with an acceptable load (e.g., full, but not overstuffed full) without breaking. They are sized fine for a 13 gallon container. It would have been nice to have an extra inch or so of length for an even better fit, but as-is I'm finding them to fit without any significant issue provided they are placed carefully when initially put into the can.

If you were to compare these to conventional plastic bags with regard to strength, ability to stretch and puncture resistance, these would clearly come up short. But they are not plastic bags, they are compostable bags. On that basis, they are very well done, with enough strength to be useful but still retain the ability to break down.

They come on a single roll with perforations between each bag. I've not had any problems tearing off the bags without damaging them. There are no ties, either provided separately or built into the top of the bag. Again, that's not a con since these are compostable rather than traditional bags.

Very helpful to have when dealing with compostable material or even run-of-the-mill trash. Well worth considering if you need a compostable bag in a larger size.

title: AWESOME!
text:
I REALLY like these. They made it possible for me to extend the life of all my pants (including work trousers/slacks- but you have to tweak the way you use it for slacks: see below) until the end of my pregnancy. I have 6 weeks left, and the only snag I have found is that I may have needed one more extender that was longer than the longest one in the pack. It's getting just a little bit tight! I will probably utilize the longest one of the extenders with a hair tie through the hole and around the button. Kind of obnoxious, I know, but its worth it to me to not have to go out and buy maternity pants. I love my jeans and I know how to put outfits with them, so I want to try and use them as long as I can. I would have loved to have had an extra long denim extender, but the longest option is a black, faux-leather extender, which is fine. Oh, and you HAVE to make sure your tops are long enough to cover the zipper! Even if you pull up the zipper as far as it will go and then turn down the little handle to lock it, it will never fully close.

To wear with slacks: put the button through the hole on the side WITHOUT the little metal hook(s). Slip the most comfortable hook through the slit on the extender. Don't try to put the slit on the extender over the button on the side with the metal hook(s)- in the third trimester, it's just too dang tight and you'll be miserable. If your slacks have 3 hooks, then you have even more options/lengths for comfort!

title: Having used Woolite with cold water on clothing and towels, I would never go back to detergents.
text:
We have been using Woolite in cold water for all of our clothes and towels for over 3 years. Previous to this, we used the usual name brand laundry detergents and either warm water for colors or hot water for whites. In time, colors faded, tee-shirts became shorter, towels were less absorbent, etc. This was all accepted as the result of aging fabrics. Woolite was only for hand washing delicates in cold water, right? We thought clothes just wouldn't get clean if we didn't use either hot or warm water washes.

I read an article about using cold water for laundering clothes that stated hot or warm water was not necessary. The article suggested Woolite for a laundry detergent and white vinegar for softening. Having used standard laundry detergents and fabric softener for over 40 years, this was a totally new concept for me, but I decided to try it.

As mentioned earlier, I have been using Woolite in cold water for all of our clothes and towels for over 3 years. What I have noticed is t-shirts I have bought since have not shrunk, faded, or become misshapen. Towels I bought over 2 years ago still look like new and are just as absorbent, if not more so. By using white vinegar as a softener, everything seems even softer than it did when I used fabric softer, and nothing holds wrinkles or creases.

In addition to all of the benefits mentioned, washing in cold water saves energy since the water does not to be heated, and vinegar is much less expensive than fabric softener. Personally, I would never go back to the old way of laundering clothes and towels.

title: "Cure" for Crohn's Disease!
text:
Well, there really isn't a cure yet, but Boost Plus helped my son go into (and stay in) remission from his Crohn's Disease. In Europe, and many parts of the world, Crohn's isn't treated with drugs as much as in the USA. Other countries prescribe "nutrition therapy," whereby solid foods are eliminated and a liquid sludge is mechanically pumped into the stomach via a nasal feeding tube. The sludge has all of the nutrients required by a person, including proteins and vitamins, etc. Unfortunately, the sludge is not palatable and many people report that they cannot stand the taste.

Hence, we tried a Boost Plus liquid regiment. Our son drank 7 of these per day for a couple of months, and the drugs were all eventually eliminated. We now continue the mostly-Boost diet, and only have added some safe foods for a rescue from the monotonous repetition of the liquid diet. The Boost has led to an accelerated growth rate (getting close to normal), and has allowed for healing of the GI track due to being gentle on the system. Our son also likes the taste better than alternative formulas (hence we buy these bulk Brikpaks).

We, of course, worked with our doctor and GI specialist, and have been on this plan for about six months now. If you or a family member are suffering from Crohn's or a similar GI condition, this therapy should be a consideration, as it is easy and effective.

I am not a doctor, so please do not consider this to be medical advice. I am simply a cautiously optimistic parent whose son is thankfully in remission from a nasty disease. Good luck, and please feel free to comment on this with your own experiences with similar conditions and/or treatments. RR

*** 2017 Update ***
After a year on the "mostly-Boost" regiment, our son did start to get some relapses of his Crohn's conditions (after trying to drop the percentage to 50% Boost). We now administer a bi-weekly immuno-suppressant but we continue the partial Boost diet for helping to keep his growth maximized. We are still happy we tried the all-Boost diet, but it became impractical after a while to keep him on an 80 to 100% diet.

title: Does what I need it to do.
text:
Most people will tell you that consistency is the most important part of any routine. Included in my "routine" are quarterly measurements of the areas on my body that concern me.

First and foremost, this device is not going to be precise to the 1/100th of an inch. It does, however, provide consistent measurements each and every time.

The best part : the self-tensioning mechanism. It always, without fail, puts the same amount of tension on the tape giving me accurate, repeatable results.

My advice is to formulate a plan to measure those body parts (quads, arms, chest, waist, hips, etc) that matter to you and find a way to measure them the SAME way the next time you use the device. Sure, you may have +/- a few pounds the next time, but if your tape placement strategy is sound, then you'll get consistent results that you can track over time.

I've used this device for approximately four years and logged my measurements through the years. It does what I need it to do. I am not a competitive body builder nor do I need to publish my measurements to any publication, so the measurements are good enough for me to track MY progress. I recommend it, its inexpensive and easy to use.

text:
I recently started the power 90 workout program and needed a body tape to keep track of my progress. The myotape is an excellent instrument that does the job in a quite fanciful way. No manual came with the package which would have been useful. I will try to explain how it works, since some reviewers had difficulty in utilizing the myotape.

First, pull on the tape and circumvent your waistline; make it as loose as possible, leaving enough space to fit your hand between your stomach and the tape. In the product picture there is a pocket where you can hook the tape extremity you just pulled; insert it in the pocket. Once completed there is a button below the symbol "MYOTAPE". Press it. It will retract the tape, tightening it around your waist. Make sure the tape is nicely snugged around the outermost part of your stomach, and use a mirror in order to read the measurement.

I would recommend this tape to anyone who wants a fancy body tape. But on serious note, a singer tape measure is just as efficient in my opinion. $4 vs $10. You make the call.

text:
This is, simply put, the best finger brace I have ever used. I have hEDS, a genetic condition that gives me very bad joints, so I've got an entire collection of assorted braces and splints, and this one is by far my favorite. I'm very prone to trigger finger, but I mostly get it in my pinkies and less often in my ring fingers, and most splints are designed for index fingers, since that's the "normal" finger to get it on. But this brace is comfortable on any finger with no modification required. It's also very lightweight and comfortable, and the removable second strap is a godsend.

The finger strap is very adjustable, and I am able to comfortably put it around two fingers at once. I have small hands though, so that might not work for everyone. The longer strap is very useful, I wrap it around my palm for stability while awake, and I can wrap it down to my wrist under my thumb at night, to keep the brace from slipping off while I sleep, which beats having to use a bulky hand brace like I did before. I ended up ordering a second one so I could have one for each hand for nights when they are both acting up.

So yes, I would definitely recommend this splint! Comfortable, adjustable, useful, and great quality for the price.

title: Met my low expectations, but already starting to wear down
text:
I needed new nail clippers as my other clippers is very clumsy. I came across these relatively inexpensive nail clippers and decided to give them a shot. Here are some thoughts:

• Look/Feel: I like the fact that these come as a pair, with a larger pair for toenails and a smaller pair for fingernails. They feel normal, but one thing that I would have preferred was a nail file on the back side of each clipper.

• Effectiveness: Given how inexpensive these are, I wasn’t expecting all that much. That being said, I did feel like I had to press down harder to clip the nails (and it’s not as if I have nails that are thicker than normal). The biggest issue, however, is that the clippers are already beginning to show some wear after just one use. This is particularly evident on the smaller pair, where one edge of the cutter is showing noticeable indentations. I think it’ll be only a matter of time before these clippers become dull.

• Case: One positive that I’d note is that the clippers come in a very nice case. This makes it easier to keep the nail clippers together and conveniently tucked away in the drawer.

In summary, this was a fair purchase of something that I had very low expectations on. The clippers worked fine, but the noticeable fraying of the edges confirms my initial thoughts that this will probably not last that long. If you need a backup pair or are in a pinch then go for it, but otherwise I’d get something that is a bit higher quality.

title: Try the plain flavor!
text: While I appreciate all the comments about the flavors this product comes in, why are people complaining that it's too sweet?  Just buy the plain and sweeten it to your taste - it's so simple.  I make a basic smoothie with flaxseed milk, a big dose of cinnamon and another of turmeric (antinflammatories do wonders for my little bit of osteoarthritis pain in my fingers), and small squirt of Jordan's Salted Caramel sugar-free coffee flavoring.  I've made pumpkin spice with 2 tablespoons of pumpkin puree and pie spice, I've added a  dollop of nut butter and a bit of mashed banana or applesauce - the possibilities are endless, and you control the level of sweetness.  I put the powder and my spices and add-ins into a small glass bowl, add a bit of flax milk, and beat the heck out of the mixture with a wire whisk - I could also use my little beater thing which I've forgotten the name of, but I'm too lazy - the whisk works fine (it's actually from my electric mixer!).  I put the liquid  in a sports shaker I found in my pantry cupboard (!), top it off with the rest of the flax milk to 8 ounces, shake it once more for good luck, and drink up.  I love this product.

It's a nutrition dream for someone on hcg diet as most other protein powders "not allowed".  100 calories is good too and 0 fat.  I'm also vegetarian so this is great.  Also 0 cholesterol.  The bad thing is the gross taste BUT I counteract that with Stevia and shake it in a mixer.  It mixes great.  Just drink it real fast (don't sip it) and get over the 10 second yuck of the after taste.  Then drink coffee or something after that. title: MhiL Collapsible Walking Cane with Light
text: This is a wonderful cane.  Safety, convenience, lightweight, portable, LED light all wrapped up in one. This cane comes folded and collapsed in a 14" long nylon storage bag which weights about 19 ounces total cane and bag. Flat enough and lightweight enough to easily fit into a suitcase for traveling. The lightweight metal cane expands up to 37 inches with 5 possible adjustable height slots. The handle is a silky smooth rubber comfortable to hold, there is a wrist strap and I love the built in LED flash light in the handle (2 AA batteries not included with purchase). A flash light in the handle is a great feature for dark or dimly lighted areas. The light is not adjustable and shines directly forward. It would be nice if there was the ability to adjust the light in a downward position. The tripod footing of the cane allows the cane to free stand yet will pivot and turn giving a more flexible natural function when in use. Three replacement rubber tips for the tripod foot were included. I would have appreciated the inclusion of instructions, recommendations, safety features, precautions when using a cane as well as what kind of batteries are needed, where and how they are applied. Even better if batteries were included. I like the lightweight flexible portability of this cane. I am submitting this evaluation freely and of my choosing.

title: They WORK! But bring two, they dry out quick.
text:
I'm happy with this product. IT WORKS! Just used it for the first time yesterday on a hike in a Hawaii rainforest (aka, mosquito heaven). Here's the results:

1. I received two mosquito bites, both through my clothes, which were areas I didn't apply Ben's.
2. Overall it felt like the bugs were just leaving me alone, weren't flying around me, etc.
3. I required TWO wipes to get my arms, legs and neck coated well enough to suit me. First wipe was all dried up after my arms & neck.
4. This product DOES have an odor when you apply it, but it seemed to go away once dry. Also, after the stuff dried, I felt like there wasn't any greasiness or stickiness to my skin, like happens with OFF!.
5. I will start carrying hand wipes though, because I wasn't comfortable having this stuff on my hands. I was worried I might touch my eyes or nose and create irritation.
6. I have sensitive skin and was concerned about skin irritation. Right after applying, my skin looked blotchy, red & white. But during the hike, my skin was fine, the blotchiness went away, I did shower when I got home after my hike, and I can confidently say I had no skin irritation.

Minus one star for requiring two wipes, but even double the cost is a small price to pay to avoid mosquito bites!

title: BEST affordable ergonomic seating solution!  A+++
text:
I've spent months looking for an affordable, backless, height-adjustable seat. So many "ergonomic" stools, kneeling chairs, yoga ball chairs, drafting stools, and ergonomic desk chairs are astronomically expensive. This is a fantastic, realistic solution for any seating arrangement!

Using a pneumatic, backless stool was originally recommended by my physical therapist. It is a great option which allows your surroundings (computer, desk, study area) to adapt to the changing needs of your body -- as opposed to forcing your body to work within the strict confines of a non-adjustable seating system. I fractured my neck a few years ago in a car accident, and until I found this stool I thought I was doomed to a life of painful studying -- or until I could somehow afford a $500-$1000+ "ergonomic" chair. Now I can study, read, type, write, practice music, and use my sit/stand computer platform all with the same stool.

This stool is very, very comfortable, sturdily built, and has a great adjustment range for height. Unlike other stools, it is nicely padded and the seat has a big enough circumference that it doesn't feel like you're going to fall off. It's very light, and was incredibly easy to put together. HIGHLY, HIGHLY recommended for anyone looking for more mobility and less back pain!

It was difficult to find one that could handle the weight, was adjustable, had a big enough seat with enough cushioning, and was affordable.  We gave it to him as a Christmas gift (a couple of weeks before Christmas), so he's been using it for about a month now.  At first, it kept rolling out from under him as he tried to sit on it, so we thought either he wouldn't be using it, or we could get wheel cups for it.  However, after just a few days of using it, he got used to how it moves and has adjusted himself to it.  He now uses it for every dental procedure as well as certain other procedures and his back pain has dramatically improved during these procedures.  The stool has also held up beautifully so far.  I would highly recommend it!

title: Quiet and Efficient
text:
For many years I'd used foil shavers to get a close shave; they worked well but were noisy and needed expensive replacements for the foils and cutters, so I decided to try a rotary shaver. The first one I tried was inexpensive, worked well for a while, didn't hold a charge well, and totally died after six months. I've had the Dynabliss just a short time, but at this point it works very well.
This shaver costs much less than the replacement parts for a foil razor. It's quiet, shaves close, and keeps a charge very well. It is easy to clean without a brush--just run water through the cutters. The shape and size of this shaver is the same as that of the failed rotary shaver, but the cutting blades on this one seem stronger to me.The body of this shaver--like the body of the previous shaver-- seems slippery when wet; it would help to have something rough or rubbery to make the shaver feel more secure in my hand.
The shaver does a good job on the neck, cutting close with no irritation when shaving wet. In fact, my experience tells me to use electric shavers wet--never dry--and using shave cream or gel (not foam).
I don't expect to return to foil shaving again. Incidentally, this shaver is so quiet that I can listen to music while shaving.

title: Better than a Plastic Scraper
text:
I have spent years making homemade bread for my family and one of my most important tools has been a plastic dough scraper I got from a King Arthur seminar several years ago. Without explanation, my scraper simply disappeared without a trace and no one knows what happened to it (I think it got tossed in the trash by accident). I went about finding a replacement and after looking at a number of products I chose this one based on the price and the positive reviews. It has proven to be a good tool, a little different than my old scraper but still fine for my needs.

Instead of plastic, this one is stainless steel encased in silicone. There are a couple of important factors here. First, because of the silicone shell the scraping edge is soft and pliable. This is helpful for scraping around crevices and getting as much dough from a round plastic bowl as possible. Because of the stainless steel inside, the whole is stiff though still slightly bendable which allows it to flex just enough to clean the bowl of my stand mixer without fatigue or permanently getting warped or bent. It is stiffer than my old plastic scraper, and while this is a positive thing it does require getting used to it.

Unlike my old plastic scraper, this one will work on a hot saucepan. That’s good news for when I am making candy and don’t want to wait for the syrup to cool and harden, requiring a lot more effort to remove. I did not find any statement regarding the temperature limit for this scraper but based on other silicone utensils I have it is probably safe up to around 400 degrees F.

title: Well designed, sturdy, but they aren't completely stink free and yes, they actually do expire
text:
The reviews saying that the counts were off are unfortunate but I've not experienced being shorted. These kits hold a considerable amount of waste but it can be difficult to gauge how many uses you can get out of the, at least at first. You don't want to overfill them. Each kit consists of a small bundle of TP, a wet wipe, a larger bag and a smaller ziploc bag. The larger bag fits into the netting of the Cleanwaste toilet which eventually gets inserted into the ziploc bag. Setting up is easy -- drop the ziploc bag into the mesh liner, underneath the larger bag where it will wait patiently. When you go to gather up your waste in the larger bag, gently squeeze the air out, tie a loop to seal the contents, and your ziploc is handy for the next step of double bagging since you've stashed it in a place where you won't lose it.

I can verify that over time, likely many years and with improper storage, the bags disintegrate and the Poo Powder solidifies and the whole kit is rendered useless. This unfortunate outcome was discovered when I came across what I believe was an ancient 12 pack that had been improperly stored or was just incredibly old.

The issues about stink are a matter of opinion, but my expectations are calibrated appropriately. If you leave the waste in an enclosed space, the sun is shining or humidity is high, then yeah, there's a bad stench. Using extra Poo Powder doesn't seem to help all that much to "cover up" the stink, but it's reasonable.

With each use of a bag, I get a pang of guilt that this is the epitome of single-use-plastic waste and the perfect example of an environmental problem in miniature. There's no getting around it so I try to conserve the usage and use real facilities when possible.

text: I show on the hunter/jumper circuits and was looking for a boot polish to keep my tallboots nice and to cover any dings and scratches that they've gathered. I LOVE this boot polish. It does a great job repelling dust and returns the luster to older boots. My tallboots were not that expensive, but this polish has them looking like I paid much more for them than I did. THe sponge applicator is great for keeping polish off your hands and clothes and the cleaning rag is soft and buffs the leather beautifully. I've had no issues with the polish drying out my boots like others do, and unlike some tackier polishes, this one comes off so cleanly that the boots repel dust and sand rather than attracting it. It also lasts a long time, with a little polish going a long way, so you really are getting a great bang for your buck.  I would highly recommend this polish for anyone who is looking for a high-quality product at a very affordable price.

title: Surprisingly effective
text: I purchased this product for next to nothing through a deal site. I was skeptical that it would work, and even more so when I actually received it and saw it, but for the price I figured it was worth a try. I have tried other products that provided no help and were extremely uncomfortable to use/wear. So far, I have worn this during two workouts and I am surprised by the results. While it doesn't make things perfect, it definitely provides support and allows me to work out much more comfortable. In a normal workout, I have to be very careful not to put too much pressure, especially at any sort of angle, on this knee. Wearing this, I found that my range of motion is much improved. I also found that I was able to do moves like lunges using a full range of motion which I had to be very careful about before. It does get a little warm, but nothing too horrible. So for now, I'm giving it four stars. As I use it more, I may revise my review.

title: Cheaply made, cumbersome, second hand goods
text:
I am charging this scrubber and have not yet used. Given the positive reviews, I had high expectations. Initial impressions are not very good. I will update once I have used it.
1. Box had obviously been opened and there are no instructions (one previous reviewer mentioned need to follow instructions). These facts indicate this is a returned product.
2. As to missing instructions. I did not find assembly to be intuitive but think I have figured it out (except for one part no idea what it is).
3. This may be an excellent product but it looks to be crudely and cheaply made. On the job use will be needed to understand best method to use.
4. The battery is in the long pvc tube (charging port is at end of that tube) so apparently must be connected to the engine to use. If so, there is no hand scrubber feature. The colored piece is the actual engine. Purpose of the wand is unclear. Perhaps to provide a further reach. Even with the wand, it is necessary to stoop to reach the floor. Bottom line, does not seem to be the product for easily scrubbing in tight spaces. With wand, the device is almost four feet long. Without wand, almost two feet. Wonder why such a long battery. Who knows?
5. Purpose of each brush? Who knows?
6. Red light in the battery (the long pvc piece) probably indicates the battery is charging. Will it turn green when fully charged? Who knows? How long to charge or tell if full charge? Who knows?
7. During assembly, it was necessary to force connection between wand and engine. Connection between battery and wand was smooth.
8. Connection between brush and engine does not seem to be complete (not a tight fit). Will see how well brushes stay connected when I operate the scrubber.
9. As mentioned by other reviewers, speed (torque) seems to be minimal but that may improve upon full charge.
10. The box describes this as a "multifunction power scrubber." What is the "multi" feature? Who knows? Perhaps fact there is more than one brush. As to the "power" part, see comment 9.

May be a great product but I am keeping all contents and watching the 30 day clock.

title: Comfortable on the feet
text:
I suffer from lower back pain and have been seeing a chiropractor for my condition. I purchased the HappyFeet Massaging Insoles as part of my treatment plan for my lower back pain. I wear a size 9.5 in shoes. I trimmed these down only a tad bit. Here's my feedback on the product since using them:
-The insoles are clearly labeled which made using them a breeze. The insole is labeled for the left/right foot and the size of the shoe is labeled so you know where to trim if needed.
-I put these in my casual lace up shoes that I wear to work. I did remove the existing insole as my shoe didn't fit comfortably with both insoles in.
-When you remove the plastic cover from the insoles, the gel side is a little sticky. This allowed the insole to stay in place and not move when I walked.
-The upside of the insole felt nice on my feet. Didn't get any blisters from my sock rubbing on the insole. I could wear my shoes with or without socks with these insoles.
-The gel arch was a nice touch and gave my flat feet some arch support.
-The gel insert was pleasing for my feet and lower back. However, the insoles didn't completely alleviate my lower back pain, but I did notice it was not as pronounced.
-I did notice a positive difference when I used these insoles in comparison to the ones that came with the shoes.
Final recap: All in all, these are comfortable insoles and they felt pleasant to my feet when I wore them. However, my lower back pain was still present.
I did receive this product for free in exchange for my honest and unbiased review. I have not been compensated in any way. Any questions please ask.

title: Good fit for my sneakers
text:
I wear Dr. Scholls sneakers because I like the arch support, the overall fit, and the insoles are already in the shoes. When I received the Happy Feet massaging insoles, I first placed them in my sneakers on top of the original insoles. I quickly learned that did not work. My feet weren’t seated well in the shoes, and they constantly moved and “squeaked”. So, since this is a good pair of shoes, and I’ve had them for a while anyway, I took out the original insoles (which were very easy to remove - obviously designed that way). Then, I put these new insoles in my shoes, and it’s like I have new shoes.
Pros:
Very comfortable
Fit well
Easy to insert
Cons:
Have to cut to fit
Do not fit in my regular shoes (my heel rubs wrong), they’re too thick for MY shoes

They’re very comfortable, with a good cushion when walking without slipping around inside the shoe. My only complaint is the need to cut them down to size. I understand the convenience of making one size “fits all”, but it almost never works out to fit correctly, and my toes can feel the difference. If I cut to the shoe size, the insole is too big to fit; if I cut it smaller, it’s almost always too small - but that is a minor frustration. I received this item for free in exchange for my honest review. My experience was not influenced by that discount in any way.

title: Very comfortable!!!
text:
I have Degenerative Disk Disease combined with Arthritis and suffer from lower back, hip, and knee pain 24/7. I've purchased a set of Dr Scholl's inserts before and they helped somewhat but not enough to really make a difference. When I had opportunity to try out the HappyFeet Massaging Insoles I thought I'd give gel insoles another try and am happy I did! The bottom of the insole has a guide for different sizes so you can trim them if needed as well as labeled for the left/right shoe. I cut mine down a little bit at a time until I had the exact fit for optimum comfort for me. The honeycomb design lets the gel act like a spring, absorbing shock and reducing stress, so they massage your feet as you walk. I especially liked the arch support, it really helped my feet ache less and the usual pain in my knees has not been as bad either. When I removed the plastic cover from the insoles, the gel side was a little sticky allowing the insole to stay in place and not move when I walked. The gel insert does help with the pain in my feet and lower back but didn't completely alleviate the pain, although I did notice it was not as discernible. title: Good for what it is
text:
What do you expect? It's a $12 mechanical scale.

If you are looking for 0.1 lb precision, don't buy this scale. If you are looking for something modern and stylish, buy something else. If you want to be able to step on this scale and just "get a number", you will be disappointed.

So why buy this scale?

You will be able to step on this scale and get a rough idea of what you actually weigh for years. No worries about batteries or sensor malfunctions in a few months.
If your weight is a bit off, this scale comes with a handy calibration wheel so you can adjust it. If your electronic scale gets out of calibration, well, too bad.
While internal friction may interfere the readings of any mechanical scale, if you think the number you get is odd, you can hop back on with no waiting!

text:
I had a different brand that broke after a month but I loved that thing, so I began the search for a replacement. This fell in a comfortable price range but sadly is no good for me.
The head strap was not adjustable enough. Even let out as far as it will go it just felt too tight on my head. My head is not big but I do have thick hair.
As others have commented, the bridge area over your nose is very uncomfortable. With my old device I'd be asleep before the 15 minute cycle was even over. With this one,however, I kept having to readjust the mask to get the pressure off my nose, but then the mask was too high up on my eyes and more adjusting had to be done. I was ready to turn it off before the session was even complete.
I think in an attempt to cover the motor sounds the music coming through the mask is played too loudly. The melodies were fine for me but the white noise was too much. One is supposed to sound like a babbling brook but comes out sounding like people splashing their feet in a pool. The birds sound more like squawking than chirping. It was not relaxing. There may be an option to turn the sound off, I didn't try since I already knew I was unhappy with this mask,, and you can connect to your phone so you can play your own music if you choose.
I'll be returning and looking for another option.

title: Poor design
text:
I read quite a few reviews before I bought it and found most of them to pertain to real issues. I was excited to get it quickly and try it. I was disappointed as it cost me time and effort.

- It is poorly designed for an average person's nose bridge and eye socket. The designers chose a profile that does not fit 95% of people. The nose ridge area needs to be wider and 'sloped' back to allow average person to have it fit comfortably. I had six people try it on and it did not fit a very small nose to a larger one.
- Average eye glasses could have been used to create a design that fits most people. I have never had to get customized glasses for size fit. Most people can wear off-the-shelf glasses. Disappointing that the designer did not undertand human physiology.
- The heat is almost non-existent compared to a mask that can be heated in a microwave. With the plethora mask available, it is shameful that the designer did not consider the measurement in this design. I have used several brooder mask from cheap to expensive and never had a fit issue. Because of poor design of the nose ridge, the eye portion of the device does not even come close to a normal person eye width. Again, even cheap sunglasses could have been a design prototype
- The massager does not work as claimed nor is it possible for it to work since all it does is make noise to pretend it is working! Shameful
- I saw a lot of talk about music in the reviews. That was not an important feature for me but it seems to be ok. I think lot of reviews are not used to reike type music.
- The hard case (I know it is needed to house the motors) is a big design flaw when a normal human skull size is not considered. It barely fit a small person let alone normal or large person
- The temple thumper is way too aggressive and may cause some injury. I am not sure why it is not mentioned in any reviews. It is almost dangerous on how hard it pushes on your temples
- The strap is designed for a ten year old child's head and not an average human adult.

This was a big disappointment! I sent it back

text:
This is not the same product I've been getting for the last year. They changed the formula, added stronger mint and lemon and it does not taste as good as the old product. I spoke with customer service at Silver Biotics, they said that these new drops have more silver in them, but the flavor is awful. The recipe used to be simply organic brown rice syrup, manuka honey, silver solution 60 ppm and organic mint flavor. Now its evaporated cane syrup, tapioca syrup, honey, the silver solution, a much stronger peppermint flavor, lemon flavor, citric acid, lactic acid...the flavor of the drop is not the same and I'm very disappointed in this new product and will no longer buy it. I've complained to Silver Biotics and I hope others who agree with me will do the same so maybe they'll go back to the old formulation. As far as I'm concerned they took a perfectly wonderful product and ruined it.
Update: I had an upper respiratory infection, tried several lozenges and these did seem to work the best. I added back one star. Funny, they taste better after using some of the others, which didn't taste very good at all. I really wish it was just mint and not lemon, this formula has a medicinal taste the old formula didn't. title: melt in your mouth strips, no peeling off afterwards
text:
These are different from the whitening strips I used to get (the popular brand in drugstores and everywhere) because you just stick these on and let it melt in your mouth. There is no peeling anything off after the 15 minutes, which seems to be a better concept than the ones where you have to peel off afterwards. The strips are thin and tiny, should most likely fit the row of teeth. There is no folding or tucking required, no bulky feeling. Once you stick these on, your mouth will feel a dry and the inside of the mouth will be stuck to the strips. I didn't want to move my mouth too much as the strips are working so that made my mouth feel even drier. I'm only on day 2 of these strips and although the instructions say to use twice a day, I am only doing it once a day because I'm worried about teeth sensitivity. After the 15 minutes was up I did rinse my mouth with tap water, and the water did make my teeth feel a little sensitive. It felt fine afterwards. I think these strips are great and I can't wait to see the results at the end of 4 weeks. If used twice a day, the instructions say you'll see it whiten to 7 shades in two weeks. There are 56 strips per box. The expiration date is printed on every foil packet (all 56 packets).

My only improvement feedback for this product is they could have packaged two strips in each foil packet instead of one, just to cut down on the waste. I have to say Moon's outer box and the individual strip packaging already seem to use much less material than the big name brands but it'll be even better if they put two strips per package, as most people are going to whiten their top and bottom teeth together anyway.

title: Easy, healthy whitening strips
text:
I shy away from most of the "heavy-duty" whitening strips/ gels because I prefer to use more natural products, so I was excited to try these whitening strips from Moon, which use hydrogen peroxide combined with a blend of health-promoting botanical ingredients. My teeth aren't badly stained, but I drink a lot of coffee and tea and they definitely aren't as white as they used to be! This package contains 56 strips, enough for 2 weeks of twice-daily use on top and bottom teeth. I'm about a week in, and seeing improvements already! Even more important, they're not causing any issues for my teeth, gums or mouth. I have sensitive gums, and experience some discomfort from certain brands of toothpaste, but these strips don't have any ill effects for me.

The strips are individually wrapped, and easy to position on your teeth. Once you've got them where you want them, they'll take about 15 minutes to dissolve, leaving a pleasant minty flavor behind with no residue. They do turn a bit tacky while they work, so I only use them when I can get away with not talking for 15 minutes, usually right before bed and after I've brushed my teeth in the morning. I feel reassured knowing that all the ingredients are safe to ingest.

My only complaint so far is that I wish the strips were a tiny bit longer - there are some stains on teeth they don't quite reach when I apply them front and center. Granted, I'm probably the only one who notices these, but I feel like they'll be more noticeable by contrast with my freshly whitened front teeth! It's a minor issue though, and I'd definitely use these again over other types of whitening products.

I'll update this review with progress photos once I've finished the full 2 weeks!

title: Great for maintenance

They do have a lot of sticking power. Maybe too much because they really stick to the inside of my mouth and I fear my tissue ripping every time I put them on. title: Strips a little small; does it matter which side goes against teeth?
text:
I had previously tried out some whitening strips that had two different sizes, one for the bottoms, the other for the tops. It was readily apparent what to do with those strips. Just peel them off the film and place a specific side against my teeth. However, after the set time period, I had to peel the strips off of my teeth and was left with a ton of good that I had to spit out. They were easy to use but messy. I saw that these were dissolving, which sounded interesting.

When I opened the packet, I was a little confused how to use these strips. They look as though there’s a piece that you peel off of something, but I wasn’t able to do so. It also wasn’t clear to me if there was a specific side that goes against my teeth. In the end, I just stuck them on and hoped for the best. They did dissolve, though they did leave some goo on my teeth, which I basically ended up swallowing. I assume I did it right, but I wasn’t entirely sure in comparison to the other strips that were easy to tell how I should put them on and what I should do.

The strips are kind of small and not as long as I’d like, so I do wish they were a little bigger. The minty flavor was strong but not overpowering.

These use hydrogen peroxide for whitening.

title: Won't recommend
text:
7I cannot say for certain this product caused my issues, but this is the only different thing I'd done. Here's my story:

I had a deep cleaning done at the dentist in September. I've waited about two months since having that done and continued with my thorough dental hygiene routine. I wanted to try to keep my teeth nice and white like after a dental cleaning so I decided to try out these Moon strips.

They are all the same, top and bottom. I find them to be a little small. The instructions say to use twice a day for two weeks. I find the twice a day to be a bit of a hassle. I tried doing it about 30 minutes after brushing in the morning and evening. The strips are pretty sticky in your mouth, but start dissolving pretty quickly. It does leave a bit of a film on your teeth once it's gone. The flavor is fine.

After 3 days of use, I noticed some discomfort along my bottom gumline. Upon further inspection, the gums at one of my bottom front teeth is now receding. I immediately have stopped using the strips and no longer feel the discomfort but my gums haven't gone back. I didn't notice my teeth looking any whiter after just 3 days. I have another dentist appointment now for December.

So, be weary trying these. Even without the issues, I don't think I'd recommend these strips anyway because of the instructions, tedious and inconvenient.

I’m not sure what the cause of the difference is, but tooth spacing is the likely culprit followed by how you floss.

If it doesn’t work, you could probably just refill it with a different kind of floss refill. This bottle style seems pretty generic and there’s probably only one manufacturer of the bottle (or at least the lid) so chances are good they’re all interchangeable.

The first time I used it I fell in love. The more tubular shape of this floss feels like it cleans more between the teeth but I went slow. It requires a bit of a tug unlike the super slick type. I’d say it was just over a week of regular use to be able to floss without incident. I went camping and didn’t think about bringing this floss as my travel toothbrush, paste and floss kit was already cleaned from it last use on a short trip. What a noticeable difference! title: Surprisingly bad
text:
I didn't realize that dental floss could be a hard thing to produce. Well, apparently it is.

1. The way this stuff is wrapped makes it impossible to pull out of the container without unscrewing the cap and taking the "ball" of floss out.

2. If you do manage to pull some out through the cap, the hole in the cap will cut the floss instead of the part that should cut the floss.

3. This floss is thick and ends up breaking frequently in my teeth. I end up using 2-3x as much as I would with normal floss.

4. Taste. Meh. No real taste.

5. So here's the thing, once you get past all those issues, the floss manages to get the gunk out from between my teeth but there's no way it's worth 2-4x what normal floss is. And, while this stuff is good for the fishies and dolphins and iguanas I'm not sure that having to buy it 2-3x more often is better for mama earth.

The packaging is a glossy cardboard that we will send to recycling, but it will not go in our compost pile. The price of this one was only 1/2 of what we paid for the thinner bamboo floss.  So, in our house we are divided on liking this or not, but I am rating for the 2 people who don't have tight teeth because other than it not being the right fit (like a piece of clothing), I do not perceive any flaw with this product.

title: Soft, gentle, soothing. Doesn't irritate my nose/face/elsewhere with repeated use. No scent.
text:
What is included in this product:

--- 18 boxes of Kleenex Expressions (soothing lotion)
Each box 65 tissues. Each tissue has 3-ply feature.
Each box is shaped like a cube. It measures just a tad above 5 inches tall, when I have the box positioned upright, ready for me to lift a tissue out of the box.
Overall measurement for each Kleenex box is 5-inch x 4-1/2 inch x 4-1/2 inch.

I easily removed the serrated, oval-shaped cover. Then, I removed the thin plastic lining, with help of the scissors, as the plastic is quite stubborn. Then, once I removed one tissue, another tissue popped up in its place.

These Kleenex facial tissues are soft, gentle, and soothing to my skin.
As I hold a tissue to my nose, I could not smell any scent.

With the cold weather, I am more prone to getting a runny nose. I used these coconut oil- and aloe-infused Kleenex tissues repeatedly, and it doesn't cause irritations to my nose or the area under my nose and above my upper lip. This is very important to me; in the past, I have used other brands (with different features), and after repeated use on my runny nose, I end up rubbing the skin raw, causing painful cracks in the skin.

Also, when I needed to blow my nose, these tissues held well under pressure.

note: the large box that contained these 18 Kleenex boxes were dented in on one side, resulting in 3 Kleenex boxes being dented because they were located on that side. It didn't matter to me, as the Kleenex tissues function in the manner that I needed them.

5-stars for the excellent way these Kleenex tissues function in addressing my needs.

text:
I love the idea of this - brightly colored little pill containers (pods?) which are sorted out 1 color per day and contain both morning and evening doses of meds. And that is my concern. The design implies to me that it would be great to just grab the day's dose and throw it into my purse. I'd be concerned that it would pop open in my purse and spill the meds out.

Clearly, these are not for households with small children - households with dogs should also probably use care ...they are just a little too easy to open.

text:

She performs all her morning tasks in her room with the lamp. She has said she wishes she could take it with her everywhere!!!

title: best one I've tried
text: I tried the Phillips previously (see review there) but just couldn't get it to work.  The NatureBright is easy to figure out, the controls make a lot more sense and you can easily see that it's set.  Also makes a great bedside lamp.  It doesn't give you the "dawning" effect, it just turns on.  But you can swivel the head pointing away or to the ceiling so it's not a shock of white light in your eyes.  The little cricket backup alarm is cute but I doubt it would actually wake me if the light didn't.  I use my Fitbit on a vibrate alarm for a backup.  On the whole, for now, I'm happy with it.  Now I just have to find a solution to actually get to sleep so I can wake up with the liht.

title: Great lamp, bought a second one
text:
I spend alot of time in front of my computer and indoors, so I wanted to mitigate the potential long term bad health effects of sitting indoors like that. So I bought a pretty long computer desk (48"), standing height to keep me off my keester and two of these lamps. I then made an "18 stand and put it behind my two monitors so that light comes down and covers the whole desk area nicely.

Plenty of brightness, and angling options built-in. Keeps me awake as the hours go on, and I use the timer feature that changes at 1PM and dims a bit at 9PM. I don't know all the science behind the importance of our body's internal biological clock and the processes it controls, but on a common sense level it makes sense to me since most of our evolutionary history when our body has been evolving, we were outdoors.
