title: Do some copies of the manual show the wrong icon for dawn simulator ?
text: I think there may be a missprint on the manual I got.  I have 4 icons on the clock screen.  First is one with clock hands, then one that looks like an alarm clock, then a bell, and then a cross shape.  But in the manual, there is no alarm clock shaped icon.  So I wonder if the alarm clock is really the icon for the dawn simulator?  It doesn't make sense to me that there would be the same icon for setting two different things (wake up time vs. actual time of day).  Are there bad manuals floating around, and some customers got them while others got corrected ones?  If my hunch is correct, then the missprint is what made this clock and alarm so insanely difficult to set.

title: Good daylight alarm, worst user interface imaginable
text:
This functions well as daylight alarm. It's best feature is that the LED's arc out over the bed and shine down, as opposed to other models which shine straight out horizontally, which means you have to be on your side facing the lamp when the alarm goes off or else the light won't actually reach your eyes and wake you up. And the head on this lamp swivels, which makes it even better for increasing the chance the light will be pointing at your eyes when the alarm turns the light on. So, of the 3 models of daylight alarms I've tried, this one wins hands down in actually waking me up with the light.

BUT: this lamp has the absolute worst user interface imaginable. Zoom in on the control panel in the main picture and look at the controls. Now guess how you turn the alarm on on Sunday night and off on Friday night. Go ahead, guess - I'll wait.

Did you figure it out? No, of course you didn't. Because it's completely un-figure-out-able. To turn the alarm on or off, first press and hold the top left button (which, mysteriously, has two overlapping squares) until the border around the top left indicator icon in the display starts flashing, then let go. Then press and release the same button again to make the border around the next indicator icon down start flashing. Then press the second button on the left (which looks like a gear) to make that second icon either start or stop flashing (flashing means the alarm is enabled, not flashing means the alarm is disabled). Then wait 15-30 seconds for your change to take effect. Could you ever possibly have guessed that from looking at the controls? Absolutely not. Why doesn't it just have an "alarm on / off" switch? Seriously. What on earth were they thinking?

Want to know what time the light will turn on in the morning (or, more accurately, at what time the light will be at full strength)? Care to guess by looking at the controls / panel? Don't bother. Because YOU CAN'T TELL WHAT TIME THE ALARM'S SET FOR WITHOUT SETTING THE ALARM TIME. Care to guess how to set the alarm time? Don't bother - you will literally never guess.

I could go on, but you get my point. I use this every weekday as my alarm, because, at least at the time I bought it (July 2014), it was the only daylight alarm that allowed me to direct the light towards my eyes in the likely event that I'm not lying on my side directly facing the lamp at 6:30 am. But if you buy this, be prepared to read the user manual a few times. And definitely keep the manual next to the light for a month or so until you get used to using the absolute worst user interface ever conceived for an alarm clock. Oh, and be patient. Very patient. Because just turning the alarm on or off, which should happen with the flick of a switch, instead takes at least half a minute.

text:

Bad: I have become adept at turning off yet another form of alarm in my sleep, and this one isn't unpleasant enough to wake me up sufficiently that I remain awake for long.

Most jarring thing: the sunset simulator goes from full daylight and fades over a half-hour. This sounds great. In practice, this means if you are using the lamp on automatic light temperature cycle mode and initiate sunset after 9pm (when the lamp switches to "night" warm-white mode), there's a slight delay, and then all six LEDs turn on full blast. That means a jump in illumination and a strong shot of blue light, although the ramp-down of the light is nice and smooth and helps me go to sleep a little more quickly than I otherwise might. Minus one star.

The people who complain about the user interface are not wrong. It's amazing, and I say that with astonishment and fear. The icons are tiny. You do need the manual. This would be minus two stars on its own. There were some details in the manual that were slightly inaccurate (exact button sequences to save/escape), but I managed to puzzle through with some trial and error and button-mashing.

You can tell that you have the feature enabled if the relevant icon is blinking. If the icon isn't blinking, go back through and try again.

If you want to test the light alarm to see how it turns on, don't set the alarm for 1 minute from now, set it for 31+ minutes from now. It's not programmed to realize that a newly set light alarm less than 30 minutes away should turn the light on immediately and bring it quickly to full intensity, it will only activate at the 30 minutes before alarm time mark.

The lamp will shut itself off after a while when it's turned on as an alarm.

title: Good size light with excellent timer feature
text:
I have a small hydroponic window garden at work near a south facing window. The plants get a decent amount of light but not all day due to nearby buildings, and they get a bit leggy, pulling toward the window as a result. I added this 3 head gooseneck light to project a bit of extra light to the plants for only 4 hours a day, but more importantly to project from the other side to help incentivize the plants to grow vertically.

After only a week I can definitely see a difference in the general lean of the plants - they're straightening out slowly but surely. These are very bright and I don't run them at full brightness to not bother the people around me.

I love the built in 24hr timer cycle because it truly becomes set it and forget it, and every day the lights come on about a half hour before I'd like to be leaving as a reminder to start wrapping up. Double duty!

title: Kidney stones are painful and this product is a little difficult to use when you're in pain
text: I developed a severe pain in my back a month ago. The pain was so bad that my spouse took me to the ER.  I've never felt such pain. After several hours of waiting which involved various levels of crying, moaning and pacing around the hospital room, I was sent for a CT scan. Subsequently,  the doctor diagnosed two 3mm kidney stones in my left ureter. The doctor gave me narcotics and sent me home. I ordered the SPECIAL PACK OF 3-Calculi Strainer Kidney Stone Collector so I could collect the stones when they passed.  Anyway, they come in a three pack. They are small, around 8" in diameter. You need to hold the collector in one hand and hold your business in the other hand. It is awkward, particularly when you're writhing in pain. Anyway, they work. The screen catches the stone. I would prefer a product, though, that fits or rests on the toilet rim, obviously a bigger product that I don't have to hold in my hand, a product that can stay put i.e. which I don't have to have handy and carry with me to the bathroom whenever the need to pee arises.

title: Holds air doesn't leak
text: [[VIDEOID:2d1754782a22b2c34cf0203b7ab2448e]] I have years of experience going to the physical therapist for my neck injury. I'm going to continue to use though because I figure my neck injury has been there for 20 years so it is not going to get better in just 3 weeks. title: surprisingly effective
text:
I write software for a living so am on my computer a lot - I use a standing desk and sometimes sit, but no matter what ergonomic changes I make I still get some neck pain into my trapezius muscles (particularly on my left side). Using my smartphone for email and other things seems to make things worse too since you look down to use the smartphone.

I thought I would give this product a try and I am glad I did. The product arrived in a decorative box shown in the picture. I was a little surprised at the solid quality of the inflation pump and valve. The item did not come with any instructions but you can easily figure out how to use it based on the product description on Amazon [which is what I did].

The inflatable rings inflate when you use the hand pump and have some light felt-like covering that is soft to touch on the face/neck area. I pump up the rings until I get a good stretch, and use the valve to close off the airflow to keep the inflation, and will wear the device while sitting up or standing. Trying to look at your smartphone screen is a bit difficult but its a good since it prevents you from putting your neck in a bad position. My face gets a little squished and it looks awkward (I wouldn't walk around in public with it) but my neck definitely feels better after wearing this device for awhile.

I actually wore the device during my work day--2 hours in the morning and 2 hours late in the day (of course not during any video calls)--my neck & trapezius muscles felt so much better than normal at the end of the work day. I plan on using this more often during work now.

Highly recommend!

title: Future long time customer
text:
I have used many different pre-workouts over the last several years, and have had a variety of different experiences. Due to my work schedule, I have to rotate between early morning workouts and late evening workouts, and if you try to take supplements to maximize the benefits of weightlifting, it can be discouraging to do so when things like staying awake or falling asleep are important to you. That being said, I wanted to try this product for about a month to get an accurate depiction of what it does for me.
My initial reactions:
I work in the chemicals industry and fully appreciated the fact that no coloring is added to this mix. It mixes clear and tastes excellent (Watermelon). It does not have the typical artificial sugar aftertaste that is really common in pre-workout supplements. I knew that it was a higher than average stimulant product, so the first time I tried it, was during my early morning workout.
It hits hard and fast, but in a very good way. I was able to take it as I pulled into the parking lot, and felt the effects quickly. I definitely felt that I was able to get more out of my workout, more weight, more reps, before I felt my muscles fatigue. I don't know if it was a placebo effect, however I will note that I did experience this same thing every time I used the product. One the days I forgot to bring it with me, I felt a markedly different way during the workout (I keeps some other powders in my truck just in case) and did not feel the same surge during those workouts.
There is no crash when the product wears off. This was huge for me. I was able to go throughout a 12 hour shift, without feeling wiped out, needing an additional pick me up.
When working out at night, I was worried about the potential difficulties falling asleep, however I was pleasantly surprised to find myself falling asleep with no difficulties.
I would normally take about 4g of Beta Alanine, along with some vasodilators, but found this made it so I didn't have to take any additional pre workout supplements except for my creatine.
I can see myself using this product for a good long time, not only for my workouts, but occasionally when I need to use a little bit of a boost during a busy day.

title: Super Soft Bristles
text:
Included are 4 toothbrushes with handles in black, pink, green, and white, perfect for the whole family, as you won't mix up whose brush is whose. Convenient and handy, each brush comes in its own protective travel tube.

Used to nylon bristles that tend to aggravate sensitive gums, I've never felt anything as soft as these toothbrushes. Feathery soft and gentle, with more bristles than the average brush, which truly cleans teeth, gums, and tongue. There are so many bristles that it almost looks solid- impressive.

The ergonomic handles aren't super shiny plastic, so they're not slippery when wet, so no worry over slipping out of your hand. I also appreciated the softer pastel colors of the handles, no loud designs that clash with my bathroom decor.

The travel tubes are an added bonus.

title: Such a soft brush - no gum discomfort
text:
Wow!! What a soft brush! When brushing my teeth, it feels so smooth - like getting a polish from the dentist. I didn’t feel any gum discomfort but yet I did feel like my teeth and gums were getting clean. Even if I push hard, these brushes cushion the pressure so that I continued to feel soft brushing.

Now, I just wish these had some sort of approval from the ADA. While I would assume my teeth are getting the brushing they need, I can’t be so sure. Some parts of the product page don’t instill a lot of confidence (for example, the picture in the product page of the before and after teeth - the woman’s teeth become several shades writer after using these brushes - makes no sense, so can I really trust some of the other claims about my teeth getting a good clean with these soft bristles?) Also these came in some traveling toothbrush cases, that didn’t give the brushes a lot of protection from possible dirt and grime within the package, so if you get these, I suggest giving them a good wash - I did so in baking soda and water.

Assuming that these work to clean your teeth the way a toothbrush should, I really do like them!

title: Yes, very soft bristles.
text:
If you have sensitive gums and/or teeth, you're going to like these toothbrushes a lot. They look the way they look in the pictures because they are jam packed with fine, soft bristles, not because they're made with some sort of plush foam.

Comparatively, a "soft" toothbrush from oral-b is hard.

I didn't notice anything ergonomic or special about the handle, so no bonus points for that, but it is a competent toothbrush for humans with sensitive gums, or for pets.

1 star off my rating for the storage tubes, which arrived a bit nicked up and kinda dirty-looking. Not actually dirty per se, but it didn't fill me with confidence about the sterility of the toothbrushes. The tubes are vented on the bottom so at least the toothbrush may may a chance to dry out even when encased.

title: Soft, yet effective.
text: I was afraid these brushes could be too soft to do good job, but I was wrong. The brush is soft, but the bristles are quite dense and in fact do a pretty good job while being gentle. Half of the tubes I received are already damaged, but I will not reduce my score because of that. text:

I do have sensitive gums and I found this to be a nice toothbrush, it is extremely soft and almost feels like you’re brushing your teeth with foam as there are so many soft bristles.

title: Very soft brush
text:
I usually use an electric toothbrush, but I wanted to try one of these just because I was curious if it really was easier on gums. Yes, it absolutely is easy on the gums. In fact, I didn't even feel it on my gums at first. It wasn't until I tried really scrubbing with a lot of pressure that I could feel the brush. Even then, I didn't feel the bristles or the usual brushing sensation you have with a regular toothbrush. It was just a little pressure and that's it. If you're gums are so sensitive that even a regular soft toothbrush is too harsh for you, then these brushes will be great for you.

That being said, if you try to brush the same way you do with a regular toothbrush, it may not get your teeth clean. You will definitely have to floss before brushing your teeth in order to get food bits out of your mouth first. But, really, you should be doing that anyway. No toothbrush is really able to clean everything out from between your teeth all on its own. You may also have to kind of scrub a little harder to get the area just above your gums clean.

The only real complaint I have about this brush is the handle. Since it isn't textured my hand kept sliding up the brush.

title: What a surprise!

title: Extremely soft, different from other traditionally "soft" toothbrushes
text: I honestly found these toothbrushes to be a bit strange. I always buy "soft" bristle toothbrushes, as I have sensitive teeth and gums, but have never used ones that felt like this. The bristles on these toothbrushes are extremely soft, somewhat short, and very tightly packed, so they don't really move back and forth or get between your teeth as well as other toothbrushes. The feel of the bristles honestly reminded more of a makeup brush than any other toothbrush I've tried before. title: Don't Listen to the False - Bad Reviews. Excellent Nutrition Bar.
text:
I'm always amazed at how people can throw out statements without any facts to back them up. Please don't listen to these people who are stating their 'opinions' that this has the same nutrition info as a snickers bar! It does not! Being a scientist and a bariatric patient I have to be very careful what I eat and the means to monitor intake properly. So when my surgeon told me I needed to increase my protein I immediately thought of the Tiger Milk Protein Rich Bars that I grew up with. I too was taken back by the claims that these are just candy bars, but don't be fooled by false statements. After doing the research I found that the reviewers who claimed this couldn't be further from the truth.

Snickers Bar: 2oz size: 271 Calories; 14g Fat; 5g Sat. Fat; 7mg Cholesterol; 140mg Sodium; 0mg Potassium; 35g Total Carbs; 1g Fiber; 29g Sugars; 4g Protein; 2% Vit. A; 0% Vit. C; 5% Calcium; 2% Iron

Where as a comparible King Size Tiger Milk Bar; approx. 2oz size: 220 Calories; 8g Fat; 3g Sat. Fat; 0mg Cholesterol; 95mg Sodium; 230mg Potassium; 28g Total Carbs; 2g Fiber; 21g Sugars; 9g Protein; 25% Vit. A; 15% Vit. C; 25% Calcium; 30% Iron.

True that the sugar for these bars is a bit high. However, it is still less than a candy bar and has almost half the fat, twice the fiber, and over twice the protein of the snikers bar. Not to mention it is considerably higher in potassium, vitamins A & C, Calcium, and Iron. HENCE IT IS A NUTRITION BAR. Also please take into account that the King Size version is more than I could or should eat. The actual 1.23oz original size is better formulated for nutrition (140 calories; 5g fat; 2g sat. fat; 60mg sodium; 140mg potassium; 18g carbs; 1g fiber; 14g sugars; 6g protein)which just further proves the point (not to mention that is the actual product we are reviewing here) that it is no where near the sugar and fat intake of a candy bar.

I hope my ranting has better informed those who are looking for a good tasting nutrition bar. Personally, I would recommend this to anyone who needs to get more protein in their diet ... and actually do.

title: The first day I wore my lenses they were fine. After storing them for the recommended time in ...
text:
I had a very scary reaction the the Clear Care with HydraGlyde.I've been using the original formula of Clear Care since 2011. I originally switched to this formula because I having issues and sensitivity to another brands solution. Recently I tired the new version with HydraGlyde because the store I went to was not carrying the original formula. I had and extreme reaction the first (and subsequent times) I used the product.

The first day I wore my lenses they were fine. After storing them for the recommended time in the HydraGlyde formula I experienced a cloud like film. Initially I just thought my vision was a little blurry but within a half hour my visibility was the equivalent of being in a smoke filled room. In addition to that when I was driving at night there were extreme rainbow halos around any light source or reflective surface. Unfortunately I was not able to take them out right away and had to wait several hours. When I did finally remove the contacts stored in HydraGlyde the haziness persisted. I was scared that I would wake up the next morning and my eyesight would still be affected. Thankfully it was not. I did give the solution a couple more trys just to run a little self experiment. Each time was just as bad even when trying it with ta different set of lenses.

When I returned to the original formula and had absolutely no issues. BE EXTREMELY CAREFUL with the product. My eye doctor mentioned that the push is to start storing all their contacts in an equivalent HydraGlyde solution when packaged for consumers. I also worry that the original formula will be phased out of stores and only HydraGlyde will be offered. Alcon Laboratories, please, please do not do this. Many of us use your product specifically because additives have caused us issues in the past.

DO NOT BUY, stick with the original Clear Care.

Some old people (50-70) play tennis all the time even though they are playing with people in their late twenties. Some even beat them.

They get tennis elbow and probably other hurt parts like I do. They play over three days a week. They say people that hit hard strokes on them their arm gets sore so they use elbow straps or bands. Most use thinner straps or bands than this design. I saw at least 3 other designs. They all seemed relatively pleased with their straps. Two said they need theirs all the time I didn't want to spend much but wondered if it would do anything. My arm often hurt after playing for several months constantly for about 3-4 days a week. I decided to buy this. I tried stretching my arm before hand that never worked maybe someone has secret stretches I don't know them tell me. I bought this I couldn't wear it for very long, the old people said to wear it loose without it being too tight so I listened to them seemed to work better. As I wore this item I listed the pros and cons above. I am not a doctor but I think what these bands seem to do is tighten the muscles that run along the lower arm when you move your wrist or grip something this allows sort of a muscle tension that doesn't exist naturally without these straps. I think a thinner one like they had maybe better. I wish this was an elastic type of design. It would probably work better than this one because it doesn't give the strap is like firm unforgiving with a spandex below. So your muscle tenses constantly because of that and the heat of the spandex is not so nice in warm weather. I didn't wear it ever more than one game per each match, it does relieved pain slightly but the negatives exceed the benefits most of the time. I also didn't get instructions on what sort of placement or correct tension to use, If I did I didn't see them. I have other pain as well the top of my arm is also often hurt during several hours of play. The old people said to just get stronger their is no band for that. title: Why you need a different brace, and how to heal faster & prevent re-injury
text:
The BandIt (or one like the BandIt) is a better brace for me and will be for most who need one. Here is a link to it on Amazon: [[ASIN:B000FML7SW BandIT Therapeutic Forearm Band]] It actually compresses the tendon, where the
Bracoo brace provides uniform pressure around the arm. That is better than nothing & does offer a little support to help in healing. But it doesn't support the tendon nearly as well. And to work effectively the Bracoo brace needs to be tight enough to restrict circulation, which obviously won't help it heal.

And for those who prefer to heal faster and solve the problem on a more permanent basis buy a brace & also buy a Thera-Band FlexBar. Here is the Amazon link: [[ASIN:B000KGOMBC Thera-Band Flexbar, Green, Medium]] Depending on how bad your injury is start slow with your hands on the outside of the green (medium) FlexBar (like five reps a day) and work up to ten or fifteen reps with your hands on the inside (where it is harder to use so the muscles get a harder workout). It will take a week to a month (depending on the severity of the damage to the tendon) to see results but it works for almost everyone.

The reason is simple: The tendon is damaged because the muscles on the "other side" of the arm are weak. I'm talking about the small muscles that get big stress only when we do things like play golf/tennis/etc. Using the FlexBar every day will target and slowly but surely strengthen these small weak muscles. This will keep the tendon from continually being stressed too far, allow it to heal much quicker, and in almost all cases prevent re-injury (if the FlexBar is used a couple of times a week to maintain muscle strength).

title: These really work!
text:
I have been using these for several months (and through the hottest summer I can remember). You can actually wear shoes with no socks and these are quite good at keeping odor and wetness away.

I ordered from their website and put them in a pair of well-worn, slighty-stinky shoes. You wipe out the inside of the shoe with a wet cloth to help the rubber backing stick. After the first day, the old odor was gone from the shoes--I was delighted. I put them in all my closed new shoes now, and they keep the insides looking nice and new.

i have not tried them in sandals or clogs (because the clogs have cloth footbeds that the rubber can't stick to). I have also not tried them with socks or stockings--mainly because that would defeat the purpose of using them. But I can say that they keep bare feet dry and odor free in closed shoes with non-porous insoles.

After a while, they do sort of wad up while you are wearing them, but I have noticed that this is about the time they are ready to be changed, so that may just be that they are past effectiveness and my feet are getting sweatier.

I am so happy to see them on Amazon Prime now!

title: These work great!

title: Amazing product, can't live without them now
text:
Before I found Silver Linings, I could never really go sockless. Its such an embarrassing problem, and I am a stickler for anti-bacterial, anti-germs, and cleanliness in general. Every time I bough a cute new pair of ballet flats, they'd inevitably end up in the trash a couple weeks later because the stink would start to get out of control. No amount of daily foot scrubbing with anti-bac soap, powders, etc would keep it at bay, and my feet would slide around from moisture in my shoes after several hours in them. You see, I live in a city where a LOT of walking and being on my feet is done. And ballet flats or sneakers are pretty much my only option - I can't wear open heels for 10 hours a day. This problem really got me down and made me feel icky. I never understood it when I'd see girls sockless in super expensive flats.

I was skeptical when I first tried Silver Linings as I just didn't get how they could ever work. But they do! Like magic! Not only are my feet daisy fresh all day, but they're completely dry too. I finally have the confidence to take my shoes off around others. I think this product is truly a miracle, and has really solved a nuisance problem for me. I've been using these for years now and I'll continue to buy them as long as they're offered and I'm at the point where I don't use anything else.

A few things to be aware of --

- they don't adhere the greatest to shoes that are fabric on the inside. I have to stop and adjust them because they sometimes shift around in my shoes. Though I love that they don't have an adhesive and won't ruin my shoes, I sometimes wish they did just do they'd stay put. This is mentioned in a LOT of other reviews and it's true - with certain types of fabric insoles they will slide around. This is easily remedied with a touch of superglue. Vinyl, Plastic, or Foam insoles? They stick and stay put just fine.

- Also, for those particularly tight and un-breathable shoes, I wish they'd come out with a full foot version. The half is sufficient (at least for me) in most shoes, but I do have a couple that I have to be careful with because the heel isn't protected.
- They're a bit expensive, and you have to replace them every couple weeks. (Or sooner, depending on how frequently you wear the shoes). I think ChuShu may be alienating certain consumers by not offering a product that lasts longer and has a bit of a high price tag. I was so thankful for the 5-pair value pack they were offering.

Reminder that you CANT just stick these into already stinky shoes and hope they eliminate the odor. They work best on clean shoes as a preventative. I've ordered 2 pairs of my favorite ballet flats and the second pair have wayyyy outlasted the first pair with the use of Silver Linings.

Overall, I LOVE this product and know a ton more women would too if they knew about them and had easy accessibility to them. I really think they should be in every walgreens, walmart, and CVS around the block, much more than that Dr. Sholls garbage.

title: 4th month update
text:
(I started taking Toji vitamins a month ago and have noticed less hair fallout. I received a free bottle from the company the day before I was about to finish my first bottle! I am very thankful to them for that!I will continue taking the vitamins, and will be back in five months to offer final reviews. 5th month update: Toji has amazing ingredients that can benefit the heart and the brain along with providing the nutrients needed to grow healthy hair, all of that I loved, but suddenly mid-way during my fourth month my hair started falling out in great numbers again. I do not know why this happened since for the first three months I noticed that I was not leaving hairs everywhere; even my husband had noticed. Regardless of this set back I was intent on continuing, with the idea that when I reached the six month mark I would see the results I was hoping for; but to be honest I cannot continue using the product for now. Another reason I will discontinue the use of the product is the price, I cannot afford it right now. (That and the fact that my hair started falling out in great quantities again are the deal breakers.)
Overall, the product seemed promising during the first months of use but after almost six months the number of new hair growth was not impressive, my hair did not grow any faster and my shedding returned. (I am aware that I did not use the product for six months as recommended, although I did take the pills as indicated.)

title: Long review- giving it a second try
text:
I purchased the 3 bottle set( 90 days). Im one bottle in and things are going ok. I take 4 daily with no stomach irritation or other problems. The pills dont taste that good and start dissolving upon contact with water. I take them with lots of water. So far my shedding as increased and is causing me concern. I haven't seen a change in the condition of my hair or balding areas yet and no uptake in growth rate either.

Of note, I was already taking most of the ingredients listed as contained in Toji in other supplements. So I expected this to kick in quicker since I have the vitamins, herbs and minerals already in my system for the last several (6-8) months. That hasn't happened but I'm Still hopeful , I will update in another 30 days.

Updated_ July 27

Two days away from concluding my second bottle and so far....I have no increase in my hair growth ( i only get 1/8" a month) , no increase in shine ( my hair's still frizzy and unruly) or thickness either( still thinning with bald spots). I have increased shedding and breakage since I started to take these, which is upsetting to me. My fingernails do seems to grow fast but that is all that I have noticed. I am not happy with my experience taking these so far.

Update August 28- added stars to my rating.

Beginning my fourth bottle and I'm finally noticing a betterment in my hair. It still grows slowly but I have noticeably growing hair at my edges. Shedding and breakage has decreased and my hair seems a little thicker. . It looks much better than it did three months
ago or even one month ago.

Update at 4 months: September 25

Still no faster growth and only minor thickening. I've reduced my dosage to half... One in the morning and one in evening and so far no change in the condition of my hair.From my last update. i think ive gotten all I'll get from these. I plan to continue two a day for the time being until I can find something else.

Final review october 2013

I no longer take these. I saw only minor improvement in the condition of my hair after almost 5 months at high dosage, which was four a day. My fingernails grew pretty fast but that's it. I saw no regrowth in bald/thinning areas and no change in growth rate either. I've stopped taking them and so far, nothing happened. No shedding or breaking etc. Seemed they weren't that effective for me. Very pricey fail.

I'm desperate to stop my hair loss so I'm giving these another try. It seems they were effective in slowing my loss and some increase in thickness. title: A bottle of miracles?
text:
I'm very happy to have found this supplement because my medium/thin naturally curly hair needs help!

Pregnancy does many things to your body and my hair has suffered. Before pregnancy, my hair was full, soft and grew quickly to the middle of my back. During pregnancy, my hair continued to grow and was lush/full; then my son was born and my hair literally fell out in clumps (hormonal imbalance) until I had to cut it all off because there were literally bald spots on my head.

Now, finally, my hair has grown to shoulder length and stopped but is medium/thin without falling out anymore. Problem is that it no longer is growing fast or what seems like at all. I don't use chemicals and rarely use heat styling but do occasionally color my hair. It would be nice if my hair would grow long like before and I could get length back again.

These pills are not terribly big (semi small horse pills, if that makes sense) and taste absolutely horrible (smell pretty bad too). I had no trouble swallowing them, even though they are hard pills instead of capsules you can break apart.
I'm taking these as instructed, 2 in the morning with food and 2 again at night with food.
For me, if this supplement works to help my hair, skin, and nails be healthy again the terrible taste is worth it.

What I have noticed from the bottle is that these help support hormonal imbalance, which for me is a major concern after having my son (hope these help) and I have done research on some of the herbs included in this supplement (all good for hormonal balance and the body in general). Like I said, pregnancy does a number on your body and to finally be able to have a supplement that helps restore the hormones is a plus for me.

I will update in a few months with results. I've attached a picture of my hair as it is today and will come back in a few months with an updated picture.

title: LOVE LOVE LOVE!  My absolute favorites!
text: I ordered a few of these diapers from Amazon to try them out on my 2-year-old twins.  These are just as nice or even nicer than my BumGenius, Thirsties, Trend Lab, Diaper Safari, Imagine and several other brands.  I love the minky outer and prints, and so do the twins. They like to pick which diaper they wear (which makes diaper changes fun instead of an argument), and they ALWAYS pick their Alva minky diapers's first!  I only wish these were the first I'd tried instead of the last!  I went and bought 20 more from Alva directly because they have tons of adorable prints both in the minky outers and the plain PUL!  One twin is almost 30 pounds with chunky thighs, and she still has plenty of growing room (so I think it will fit far beyond 33 lbs. whereas some brands say up to 40 and won't even come close...these exceed the size expectations).  The other is only 25 pounds, and these adjust wonderfully to fit both with no leaks or problems at all.  I will say the only negative is that the minky CAN wick if you have an extremely heavy/fast wetter - like my daughter (read that - never ending Niagra Falls wetter all night long!)  Occasionally the leg openings will be slightly damp when she wakes up in the morning, so I usually choose a non-minky Alva for nighttime for her.  During the daytime I have never once had a leak with these at all in several months of use.  They are very comparable to the BumGenius and DiaperSafari pockets with generous sizing, very soft lining and no problems at all with pilling but MUCH cheaper AND I (and the twins) do love the super soft minky!!

text:
Over all a cute product that's super soft. Just unlucky that mine came with red dye problems. The dye stained the white material and this is straight from the box, no washing. I didn't expect this as no one else mentioned it.

I likely would have given this 5 stars if no dye issues and if the design included leg gussets which I have read helps immensely with leaks/blowouts. This all-in-one may work great for your little one. Just maybe try a different pattern as Alva offers many.

UPDATE:
So I was holding this minky diaper just marveling at how soft it is and I was staring at the red "stains". Turns out the stains are actually a very very faint image of the dinosaurs on the reverse side of the minky material. Anyhow, happy to have found this out! text: I'm new to cloth diapering and tried the expensive brands.  Long story short - the expensive ones either leaked or the velcro stuck to everything in the drier.  I love the alva brand so far (been using them for 3 months now).  I haven't had any problems with leaking or blowout.  The key to not having leaks is to adjust the leg gusset snug enough and change the liner inserts often.  I would say I change the liners about every 1.5-2 hours.  These diapers come with 2 liners (and you can buy more if needed) so if the shell isn't wet, just change the liner.  Saves on laundry and the budget since you're washing a bit less and buying less diaper covers. I like that the leg gusset is adjustable so it fits my little guy well.  I would (and have already) recommended these to other parents.

title: Effectiveness justifies the price!
text: Over the past 10 years I have used various products for arthritis in my hands and knees. I have tried Voltaren prescription gel, emu oil, tiger balm, icy hot, capsaicin gel, etc. The only one that reduced my pain was the capsaicin cream. The problem with the capsaicin cream is that, if you cover over it with clothing, it burns your skin off. And it rubs off on anything you touch, and eventually gets into your (Or someone else's) eyes. I really did not expect Cool Azul to work, other than to make my skin feel cool. Was I ever surprised! I could tell within 20 minutes that 50% of my pain was gone, And within another 15 minutes my pain was reduced even more. I have also noticed that if I use it two or three times a day, I can even skip one day and not use it, and my pain remains alleviated until the following day. I make sure to not wash my hands for about 45 minutes after using to give the cream plenty of time to start working. It's not sticky or messy at all, and goes a long way away. It's a little pricey, but its effectiveness justifies its price!

(Try turning it vertical.)  I have tried several other types of support for seats and this is the best.  A good purchase, but the product has some faults.  The check valve in the bulb failed after about a year, so I had to use a binder clip as a clamp on the hose to keep it from deflating.  That worked OK until the rubber hose deteriorated at the connection to the pillow and now it's not fixable.  There are more durable materials than natural rubber for the hose and bulb - it's disappointing that silicone wasn't used instead.  Because it's rubber, avoid getting any oils, greases or lotions on the tubing.  These can cause rapid deterioration.

text:

title: Effective device for lower back pain treatment
text:
Occasionally I have lower back pain. My kinesiologist treats me with a combination of ultrasound and infrared massages which alleviate the pain without recurring to pain killer drugs.
Infrared radiation (IR), sometimes referred to simply as infrared, is a region of the electromagnetic radiation spectrum where wavelengths range from about 700 nanometers (nm) to 1 millimeter (mm).
This device has an array of 63pcs 660nm red lights and 42pcs 850nm invisible infrared lights that can be selected with the controller. Also you can select the intensity (5 levels) of pulse massage.
You can set the timer in 5min increments up to 30 min.
You will experience a pleasant warmth that should alleviate your pain. I am using this with a portable USB power bank as to remain mobile and not be movement restricted by using the enclosed wall power supply.

title: Now this is a great item!
text: It's funny, I hadn't heard anything about red light therapy until about a year ago when I was at a local spa. They encouraged me to try a red light pod machine that they had basically for free. I didn't know anything about it, but after 15 minutes in that space age machine, my chronically painful body felt better, lighter, energized, I don't know...I just felt good. I went back a few more times and actually shed a couple of stubborn pounds that no amount of diet or exercise would help to move. I figured it had to be a fluke. Since those in-spa red light treatments are ridiculously expensive, I didn't continue going, but then decided to try it a couple more times, several months later. The same thing happened, I lost a couple of pounds and felt really relaxed and good after doing it. So, when I saw that there are red light belts and wraps that can be worn at home, I wondered if it is the same basic technology as what they were offering in the spa. I am not completely sure on the science and don't fully understand why this works, but this wrap seems to offer pretty similar benefits to the professional treatment I received. I feel very relaxed and a lot less pain after using this wrap so I am excited to have access to this at home. This belt is so easy to use, just wrap it around your mid-section, your legs or the upper back and chest as well. It feels so relaxing and seems like it might be doing something to get the sluggish lymphatic system to wake up a little bit. I think this would make a fantastic gift for someone because it is so unique and really has a lot to offer in the way of pain relief with the slight possibility of helping someone to lose maybe a pound or two. I know that seems pretty far-fetched, but I don't know, I figure it can't hurt to try if nothing else is working and/or in conjunction with a great diet/exercise regimen, etc...why not give it a try? I think it is working for me and will definitely update if I change my opinion!

title: Helpful pain relief device
text:
I'm an individual who deals with a lot of back pain. I have retrolithesis of L4 and L4, and spinal stenosis. There are days where I'm completely immobile due to lower back pain. I'm always down for something to help my back, especially on days where I am in excruciating pain. I found this awesome red light therapy belt, and thought it could be beneficial to my situation.

So far, my experience is good. I'm using the plug in version, even though you can plug it into a battery pack for portable use. It's very simple to put the belt on, select your options from the control unit, and enjoy the benefits. I really love how the massage and warmth feels on my tender back. There are 3 light modes. You can opt for 660nm, 850nm or both 660nm+850nm together. The days where I'm in severe pain, so I just use the 850nm. There are 5 brightness levels. I believe I'm feeling the warmth from the highest setting. There are also 5 massage levels. I like putting mine on the highest massage intensity. It's like a vibration massage, but it brings relief. Oh, and it has the option to pulsate. I love all the choices with this belt.

Another very nice thing about this belt is its timer. This is nice for me, since I have fallen asleep with it on. The recommended amount of time to use it is 20 minutes per day. The timer gives you the choice of 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, and 30 minutes. I run mine for about 30 minutes. I'm always sad when my session is over. It feels so nice while it's on.

Overall, this is a wonderful therapy belt. It has helped me tremendously and I hope it can do the same for others.

title: Wrap Has A Nice Width
text:

As far as noise levels go, it's not as noisy as some wraps I have tried. There is a noticeable sound, but it's not overly distracting. There is a convenient timer setting that allows you to program the wrap to shut off in as little as five minutes and up to 30 minutes (five minute increments).

title: Their 16oz claim is a lie
text:
I have used collagen for a long time and typically buy 16oz containers for their value. Sadly, I knew something was not right when I picked 5 of these I had ordered out of the box.

I took my handy and reliable kitchen scale and weighed each of the containers along with a new canister of another collagen powder I am finishing up (see pictures).

Using my other brand as a comparison you can clearly see something is up. You can clearly see in the pics that this brand is still sealed and weighing right around 15oz. So not only is it light to start with, but this includes the packaging. Once you take the plastic packaging out of the mix it will be even less. Likely 12 or 13oz for a brand that is advertising 16oz. My other brand weighed 18oz including the weight of the container, so at least they are honest.

Won't be buying these again, as their shady practices inspire ZERO trust in this brand.

title: Sketchy
text:
I ordered this collagen a couple times in the past. At the time, the label said 16 oz. I was quite sure it wasn't a full 16 oz... but it still seemed like a decent deal for the price.

I clicked on the same link to order it again this time. I suppose it's my fault that I didn't notice that the description had changed: where it previously said 16 oz, it now says 10 oz.

* When it arrived, the first thing I noticed was that the canister felt lighter.
* I then noticed that the label said 10 oz instead of 16.
* I then removed the outer plastic seal, to discover that there was no inner seal under the cap. (There had been in the past.)
* And then I discovered that the canister was filled only about 80% of the way. (It had been at least 90% on previous purchases.)

Sketchy.

title: It actually works!  Dried grout on tile.
text: I bought this in a desperate attempt to clean off over-worked grout.  Foolishly I grouted late at night  (base tile) and didn't bother cleaning it off.  Big mistake.  I was left with smeared dried grout on my tile that would not budge.  There were other projects that needed to be done, and I wanted to finish the rest of the tile - so I just left the base tile as is for several weeks, figuring I would get to it when I get to it.  I discovered that cleaning off dried grout is nearly impossible.  I tried an acid based cleaner that did very little, and even the "sugar water" trick.  Surprisingly that did help a bit, but was too much scrubbing work.  THIS product worked like a charm!  I can't believe how well it works.  I wish I had before and after photos to post.  Spray it on, leave it for 20 minutes, then use a scotch brite pad.  I also had to use a plastic scraper in certain heavy areas, but now my tile is clean!  The really bad areas like the corners needed two applications, but it worked.  I don't know how this will perform for other issues, but for dried grout - this is the one!

title: Works wonderfully and is very easy to use / worth the price
text: My 'low priced' concrete guy left me a mess.  Concrete splatter on nearly everything (walls, doors, etc).  Scraping alone will only damage surfaces. I hoped to find an easy and effective chemical solution but not an acid.  Speedy Clean did the job.  It sprays on foamy and needs to sit on the hardened concrete for a full 10 minutes.  I then used a 4 inch scraper to easily remove the splatter.  Anything that didn't want to easily come off (super thick concrete blob) received a second treatment.  It all came off with no damage to underlying surfaces.  Be sure to wash the area well to neutralize the cleaner and lay down a tarp before starting if working on a concrete floor so you don't damage the floor.

title: In control of my sun exposure
text:
Skin cancer runs in my family, but I found out recently that I am Vitamin D deficient. I bought a SunFriend to balance getting some sun but not enough to burn. So far so good. I got the orange and yellow because it looks like the sun. Surprisingly, it looks pretty good with my outfits despite the bright color. People keep asking me about it, which is pretty cool. The panel of lights takes getting used to, kind of like a 1970s digital watch. The SunFriend.com website has more detailed instructions than the package. The first day I set it to Skin Sensitivity 1 (SS-1), and it seemed too low. Now I set it at SS-4, and I still haven't burned. With practice I'm learning to trust that it really is measuring UV. (Apparently, the sensor was designed at NASA) I push the Check UVA+B button throughout the day, and when the LEDs get near 11, I start planning to put on sunscreen or go inside. Voilà! Easy. I feel more in control of my sun exposure, and don't have to slather on as much chalky white SPF 80 sunscreen. Also, the contact points are all silicone or plastic, so no nickel allergy issue.

Cool product for anyone concerned about skin damage and making enough Vitamin D.

title: Very good light...
text:
I generally review 3 kinds of stuff: (1) knocks my socks off, (2) annoys me, or (3)has some feature that hasn't been mentioned but I think should be. This lamp doesn't fit into any of these categories but it's a good lamp. One feature that I like is the 2-light-level switch. I often use the lower level to augment available daylight and the upper level when I'm reading with an overhead light on. I'm not fond of using it as the sole light source. This is partly due to the fact that the light from the lamp looks unusually cold (think of the "white", glary headlights of a modern car). And partly it is due to the smallish "pool" of light given off by the lamp. If you're reading a book or knitting, a small pool of light works well. For a newspaper, however, not very. Would other lamps work better? Probably not.
Bottom line: Am I happy with it? Yes. I like the little platform thing, which I use for a pad and pen. I like the adjustability of the light (the goose-neck feature, which, because it's a floor lamp, I won't change very often). The whole thing seems sturdy and well-made. I like having two light levels. The diffuser that attaches under the bulb to prevent the light from shining directly in your eyes is also a nice touch.
It just didn't knock my socks off.

title: Bad quality control! Buyers be careful!
text:
I ordered this floor lamp from Verilux's website and received it ten days later. I assembled it but found only the low power switch worked. When I switched to high power, the light were off. I disassembled the lamp to check whether I missed some thing. To my surprise, I found the brown wire from the base was out of the connector! I took a photo which you can see here:

http://ecx.images-amazon.com/images/I/51pMExPDRRL.jpg

I contacted their costumer service. The following is part of the conversation:

"""
Me: after i assembled it, i found the high power switch didn't work
Me: but the low power switch did work
Peggy: all right, do you have your order number? It sounds like the ballast, and I would be happy to exchange the lamp for you. I can send you a pre-paid label to return the defective unit to us and send you a new one.
.....
Me: you know what would happen if the wire touch the metal frame ... you put my life into risk just because of your poor quality control
Peggy: No, it would be fine, the wire is not connected to anything and wouldn't make a circuit. Thats why the lamp doesn't work.
Me: my body will be part the the circuit
Peggy: The wire was not connected to a power source.
Me: what if the red one were out?
Peggy: That would be the same thing. Thank you, I'll send the label asap.
"""

I know that they are doing their best to exchange the lamp for me. But personally I don't trust their quality control anymore.

I won't comment more. You can decide whether to buy it or not.

title: Blow Dry Look in Minutes...
text:
I have naturally curly hair. I purchased a professional quality hair straightener years ago. I still love it if I'm looking for the stick straight hair effect. It's generally about a 20 minute process to do it right. If your looking for stick straight hair you'll be better off using a flat iron. Personally, I prefer the look that I get from this straightener brush and haven't used my flat iron ever since I got it. You'll get the kind of straight that you get when you blow dry your hair straight in only a fraction of the time. On me it's more flattering. It straightens out the curls but adds body and shine for a more youthful look. My hair looks healthier using this brush and flows more freely. I use a good Argon Oil conditioner always and also use Argon Oil throughout my hair. I used to use too much until my hair dresser taught me how to do it. You really do only need a few drops. You put some in the palm of your hand and rub your hands together and then finger it throughout avoiding your roots. This is great protection for your hair and adds to the sheen you'll receive in the results. With the flat iron, I had to spray each time I straightened a section out with my protection spray. With this brush, I just spray my head inside and out and then flat brush. It literally takes me 2 minutes to do my hair. It's as if I spent 30 minutes on a blow dry style. As a bonus, this brush comes with some nice accessories. You'll receive 2 hair clips to section your hair with, a heat glove for your other hand and a velvet storage bag. Nice touch.

title: great straightening brush and all you need to straighten your hair quickly and easily
text:
I have very thick hair. It has some wave to it and It is sometimes frizzy. The Apalus Hair Straightening Brush made straightening it quick and easy. I absolutely love using this brush!

It has a nice long cord so I don't feel like I'm tied to the wall when I'm using it. A push of the power button and it powers on and quickly starts heating up. The buttons lock after 5 seconds, so if you miss setting your temperature at first, you can either hold down the power button to shut it off and restart it, or double press it to unclock the keys and adjust the temperature from there. It goes up to 450 degrees and only takes 3 minutes to get to that temperature. I set mine to 400 and it took around 2 minutes to get there. If you prefer to view centigrade temperatures, you can press both temperature control buttons "+" and "-" at the same time.

The brush also came with a couple of plastic to help separate your hair. I also really appreciate that it came with a glove as well to help you from getting burned which gave me peace of mind while I was using the brush knowing that I didn't have to focus on not getting my fingers too close to the bristles, but instead just getting my hair right. There are a good amount of bristles and they are spread over the brush in a manner that is helpful to really get into my hair, but also not put too much tension on my hair and the bristles don't snag my hair.

I like that it is offered in 2 color choices, I chose the black and blue one, but appreciate that others may prefer pink. The LCD screen displays the temperature. The handle stays cool to the touch. If for some reason, you forgot to turn off the brush, it should auto-shutoff after 1 hour. Although, I always unplug mine and let it cool off after I am done using it.

Included in my picture, the left side gives you an idea of what my hair looked like before using this brush, and on the right side is after using it.

I think this brush is a great value and I would highly recommend it to anyone who would use a straightener!!!

title: The great thing is that you can grab the hair and ...
text: You press a button to set the temperature (instructions included).  Wait about 10 seconds.  While waiting, put on the heat-proof glove (included) on your non-dominant hand.  Divide your hair in half along your part and clip (clips included).  Then divide the half you will start with in half top to bottom and clip the top half.  Simply brush through your hair at a slow pace.  I count to 5 to make it through one section of hair and repeat as needed.  My hair is naturally wavy, not curly, so you may need to make multiple passes.  The great thing is that you can grab the hair and hold with the gloved hand immediately and not burn your fingers.  Also, the black tips aren't hot so you don't hit your ear tips or your scalp.  Only the blue part gets hot.  Repeat through the remaining 3 sections of hair.  It takes me about 10 minutes to get hair as straight as with an iron but without the damage and burns to my hands/face/ears.  I immediately bought another one for a family member after using this one.

title: Does the job well, if you can get past the initial feeling of it being behind you.
text:
[[VIDEOID:4906b0eeb97740b6aa8918eb22f9e9d3]] This is my review on the FOMI Lumbar Support. Disclosure: I was offered this product at a reduced price in exchange for my honest and unbiased opinion. When I do a review I always get one or more people to put their opinion in on it, because people have different likes and dislikes and I feel the more perspectives I get on something the better I can review it.

So, my first impression of the FOMI Lumbar Support: Over all I would have to say it was fair. Sadly some of it's value was lost in my use of it has my chair has Lumbar support (and by my chair I mean my husbands that I steal all the time). So when you pile Lumber on Lumbar it gets a little un-comfy. Now if I laid back in his chair it kinda suspended my back similar to how a hammock would and that felt pretty nice and the massage beads were a very nice touch and were not too intrusive to the back. But all-in-all, not for me.

My moms assessment of the FOMI Lumbar Support: She put it in her van and drove around town with it for awhile then gave me her opinion of it. Overall she seemed happy with it but wasn't overly impressed by it. Though it's not necessarily uncomfortable, it could definitely take some getting used to.

I ALWAYS try to find at least one thing that could be improved upon or slight imperfection in every product I review because NO product is completely prefect for everyone.

So the main issues with this product is: 1) It could prove slightly awkward at first and may not use it long enough to get start feeling the long term effect it would have on their back. 2) It presents its self as having adjustable elastic straps, I feel this is slightly misleading. The straps themselves can not be adjusted. Now there are two straps going diagonally and one horizontally. This gives it a sense of flexibility to fit a variety of chairs, but I would not classify it as adjustable.

title: Helps Senior Pet with Improved Mobility
text: I actually got these for my ancient cat, since he weighs as much as a small dog and can benefit just as much from the glucosamine and other ingredients in this treat. When I first offered it to my cat as a whole treat, he was totally uninterested. I broke it up into tiny pieces, but he still wanted nothing to do with it. He goes absolutely nuts over his wet cat food, though, so I have been breaking each treat up into a powder form and stirring it in with his cat food before I give it to him. He's in the habit of gobbling his wet cat food down to the last morsel, and putting this soft chew in his food didn't slow him down one iota. It takes a while for glucosamine to start having an effect in humans, and I figure the same is probably true in animals, but I am starting to see an improvement in his stiffness and his mobility. At one chewy treat per day, and 60 soft chews per package, these will last me for two months. I consider this a good value at $19.99, and I believe my cat does, too.

title: Tasty Beneficial Treat!
text:
[[VIDEOID:9dd81ea89d0293b9bcc0e56aad5ebdef]] This is the first time I’ve given this product to my dogs. They obviously like the taste (see the video) since they both took one without any hesitation. Since they are new to these treats, I do not have enough experience with them to rate their effectiveness as a hip and joint supplement. I can say I like the ingredients and they should be beneficial with these ingredients - glucosamine via shellfish, MSM, Yucca schidigera, Chondroitin Sulfate, Calcium ascorbate (Vit C), Vit. E, Omega-3 (fish and flaxseed oil), Omega-6 (fish and flaxseed oil).

In faint white print on the back of the package, it says to “double the daily amount for the first 3 weeks”. My dogs weigh about 32-33# which means I need to give them 4 chews a day for the first 3 weeks and then 2 chews a day afterward. The package contains 60 chews making a package last only one month with the maintenance dose and for the first 3 weeks lasting only 1/2 month. At $19.99 a package, it is quite expensive.

The packaging list “cautions” which one is giving the treat with food or right after to avoid GI upset. It also lists warnings to keep away from children and animals and if there is an overdose to get medical care immediately.

I like the fact that they are made in the USA but then it list it is manufacted for Kenn & Kit which has a Singapore address. Humm…not sure what to make of that.

I received this product in August, 2021 and the “Best By” date is 5/2024 so they have a nice length of time before expiring.

title: My Dogs Will Take These Healthy Treats!

This treat contains Omega 3 and glucosamine, which lubricates their joints, lowers the chance of inflammation, and makes them feel more comfortable as they age. title: Comparison with greenies hip and joint/ yucca makes me nervous/ serving size
text:
[[VIDEOID:fb3ad9c0a4b5eda2a6a106bf92b18160]] As I compare this with greenie hip and joint, I see that this contains 500 mg of Glucosamine (same as greenies), 400 mg of MSM (none in greenies) and 50 mg of Chondroitin Sulfate Porcine source (greenies has 400mg from chicken source).

I read up on Chondroitin and it’s widely used to help with osteoarthritis which happens when joints degenerate. It’s found in animal tissues rich in cartilage. I like that this is sourced from a pig (porcine) b/c many dogs have allergies to chicken (which is the source used in greenies). This has a lot less Chondroitin, but it’s also priced much more reasonable.

This is also loaded with fish oil, flaxseed, calcium (50 mg) and yucca schidigera (60 mg- controversial, but it seems like the extract helps to clear them out (and makes poops less stinky) so they can absorb more nutrients. I’m not seeing any of these ingredients in greenies.

If you have two medium/large dogs the bag will go fast. I have to give my big dog (60 pounds) 3 chews a day and a my medium dog (35 pounds) 2 chews a day. There are 60 chews in a bag. This means that the bag will only last me 12 days. The directions say to double the daily amount for the first week. I didn’t double the amount b/c it would have gone way too fast if I did. Plus, I wanted to see how my dogs respond to this first. I would have liked if this came in a larger bag of like 90 chews.

I like that this is made in the USA. The packaging is fun and “cool”. The chews however do have a strong, fishy smell. My medium sized dog likes the flavor, but my lab hesitated before trying it out .

Overall, I like the price and quality, I’m just nervous about the yucca and I think I would need to go through the bag way too quickly since I have two dogs.

text:
I ordered this for my 6 year old son who broke his foot and was non- weight bearing for 8 weeks. He did fine with crutches - but this scooter was such a lifesaver! We went camping, went to Disneyland, went to Knotts Berry Farm, shopping, the park and played outside with his scooter. He loved the freedom he had and his ability to keep up with his siblings without having the chore of crutches.

This has a brake which is a little big for his hand, so he had to get used to wrapping his hand around it to get it to stop. It can reach high speeds! I think I said, "slow down" at least 20x a day. When he was outside on it I made him wear a helmet, because he used it like a regular scooter. He used the basket much more than I thought he would. Mostly for his water bottle and snacks, but you just don't think about how much 6 year olds carry around until their hands are busy steering a scooter! He really really loved it. Made our lives so much less complicated.

title: Awkward
text: The toothbrush does an adequate job, but I am unable to find replacement heads for it. I posted the question about availability and no one--not even the seller--responded. I use a AA-battery-powered Colgate toothbrush with a replaceable rotating head that I think does a better job than the oscillating one that comes with this set. The flosser is kind of cool and does have a good bit of pressure. My teeth and gums do feel better after using it. The different spray heads are nice, too. Surprisingly, the flosser requires a proprietary charging cord whereas the toothbrush uses a USB-C charging cable. Both connect to a USB-A jack for power. The flosser is big and bulky in the hand owing to the water tank and requires the user to twist and contort to keep the water pumping. It would have been nice if the manufacturer had provided a bag or case to keep all of the loose ends--i.e., brushes, flossing heads, power cords--together.

title: Comprehensive cleaning
text: If you never had a water flosser before, you will see and feel a difference with the debris that come out when you use one. Indeed it takes a little getting used to if you have sensitive gums, but luckily, the flosser and electric toothbrush both have several modes of intensity. I started with the softer settings on both devices and found myself getting used to it quickly enough that I was able to use normal modes on both less than a week later. The flosser also comes with a few attachments for specialized cleaning and the brush has a few extra heads as well. Both are rechargeable and have a IPX7 Waterproof rating, making them convenient and easy to use even in an environment with lots of water. Both appear to be sturdy and well made, with the only drawback being that the black finish will lead to obvious water stains and spots over time.

title: Great combination

title: Replacement Toothbrush Heads Do Not Appear To Be Available
text:
I've been reviewing quite a few Chinese Water Flossers & Electric Toothbrushes lately.

This one is the most powerful other than my old Philips Sonic Care. 3 brushing speeds.

Toothbrush: Much more powerful than any other Asian brand I've tried. Came 3/4 chraged. Uses a standard USB cable (provided). Really only complaint:
1. The bristles could be a bit softer,

Water Flosser:

Again, the most powerful one I own. Several speed settings. This did include all 4 different syled heads, I tried out the "normal"/standard one. Worked well.

3 issues:

1. As we move into an era of USB powered devices, it is really getting frustrating that there are so many proprietary cords. I often can't find the right cord, and as they all plug into a USB charger there is no reason for this. I had an identical looking cord that didn't fit.

2. On first use, the water had a chemical flavor.

3. The charging port (the unique style, kind of like a razor but barely different sized) has a rubber cover for safety. I could not get it back on the unit after charging, so I am just leaving the charging cable plugged in. At least I won't lose the cable that way!

To sum up, if the chemical flavor goes away, this will be my go to Flosser. I would like to say similar about the tooth brush, I need to watch the impact of harder bristles carefully the first couple weeks. I also can not find replacement brush heads for sale, which if not remedied would cause a fairly short period of the toothbrush being useful.

I will increase the review to 4 stars if I can find replacement toothbrush heads & if they are affordable

text:

The toothbrush uses the same head as sonicare toothbrushes
Toothbrush has the expected power and speed for a brush in this price range
The flosser has 4 modes: normal, soft, pulse, custom (allows you to set the water pressure level)

Cons:
Flosser uses a proprietary charger
It's hard to fully empty and dry the reservoir for the flosser.
The toothbrush and flosser use different charging cables, which is a hassle when traveling.
Neither tool comes with a case

text:
They work as stated. However there are a few issues. First off there doesn't seem to be any temperature regulator in these things. They get uncomfortably warm after about 20 or 30 min. The description says 152 deg, and they are not kidding. The heating unit is a 7 in long by one inch wide strip that inserts in a zipper at the toe. It slips between the insole and out-sole of the slipper. you have to make sure it runs right down the middle or it will only warm one side or the other on your foot. The "Y" cable is kind of short so what ever your connecting it to has to be right next to your feet. and the "Y" itself is very short and limits how you can move your feet.

You can't just use any USB adapter. It draws so much current it got my IPad charger so warm it smelled like burning plastic and was very hot to the touch. They say you can plug it into a computer, but I would be afraid it would burn something out. It would definitely drain your laptop battery,

I will say it will get your feet warm after an evening of shoveling snow. So if you have VERY cold feet, this is what you need. Just don't fall asleep with them on.

title: Works Well and is Well-Constructed
text: I owned a Panasonic ER-GN30 nose hair trimmer for several years, dropped it recently and it stopped working so I replaced it with this.  I immediately noticed the superior construction, despite the lower price, of this model.  It feels heavier and more substantial.  The big problem with my prior Panasonic was that the double-A battery's positive terminal (the metal nub), faced downward, it often shook loose, and the power would cut off.  With this model, the positive terminal properly faces upward/north and the screw-in base provides constant pressure on the battery so the power doesn't cut off.  Long way of saying: this model has superior construction.  I recommend this nose hair trimmer.  It works well, cuts my nose hair quite close without snagging and I imagine it would work equally well for anyone needing ear hair trimming too.  I'm pleased with my purchase.

title: Important Clarification About This Product - Please Read Before You Order!
text:
This is important information you should read before you purchase. This is a bit long, but please take the time to read it all. This will explain why some reviewers think they didn't receive the complete product.

I discovered this Fatigued to Fantastic powder on Enzymatic Therapy's website when I was looking for something else. Enzymatic Therapy is the maker of this product and I know and trust their brand. All of their product lines are shown on their website. This product looked great and I decided I would buy it. It was a canister containing powder and they make two flavors - Berry and Citrus.

However, I always check Amazon to see if they carry products and compare the prices. I found several sellers offering this product here on Amazon, and I was delighted to find that the prices on Amazon are HALF the retail price. I ordered the Citrus flavor on another page from a seller who had both flavors. Please understand that I thought I was ordering the canister of powder which is shown on the manufacturer's website. I even sprung for one day delivery so I'd get it faster.

After I ordered, I received the confirmation email that said I had ordered this "Kit" that contained the powder AND the supplement capsules. I came back to the sales page, enlarged the photo and saw that it was indeed a kit with both products.

I cancelled my order. I was confused. I only wanted the powder.

So I called Enzymatic Therapy and asked them to clarify if this "Kit" was their legitimate product, since it does not appear on their website. Here is what they told me...

They haven't made the "Kit" in the photo and description above for several years. At that time they made a major change. Instead of offering the bottle of vitamins with the powder as the Kit, THEY ADDED THOSE SAME VITAMINS TO THE POWDER ITSELF, so all of the ingredients are now in the one product - the canister containing the powder.

The Kits that are shown on this page and the other sellers' pages NO LONGER EXIST anywhere - no retailer or distributor has them. They have been gone for years.

So the rep told me that all of the pages - like this one - are showing and describing the old product that doesn't exist and that the sellers just haven't updated their pages over the years. At first I found that hard to believe because in all that time, customers would have surely complained if they didn't receive what's shown.

But she was positive that if I placed the order again, I would receive the newer canister (which is what I wanted.) I receive my order the next day (yesterday) and she was right.

So, in summary...

1. The reviewers who said they didn't receive the bottle of vitamin caps with the order as they expected were right.

2. The product "Kit" that's shown and described above is not what you will receive. You'll only receive the powder.

3. BUT you will receive full value of the product because those extra B vitamins are now in the actual powder itself.

Actually, you will receive MORE than full value because Amazon's price is half the retail price plus free shipping.

Oh...one more thing. I read reviews on several pages and I'm glad I didn't order the Berry. I do not like my powders sweet. I ordered the Citrus flavor and it's perfect - definitely not sweet - it's just right. I just added it to spring water and it tasted very good.

I hope this all helps...

UPDATE A FEW DAY AFTER TRYING THE PRODUCT:

I had very high hopes for this product. Good brand, good taste, good reviews. I'm always looking for the most healthful ways to increase energy. I've been a health nut for decades and have always taken lots of vitamins and supplements and nutritional products (greens, etc) and stay current on the latest research.

However, the first couple of days I took the Fatigued to Fantatic powder, I felt abnormally sleepy. Way too relaxed. I skipped a day and bounced back to normal. Took it again and the same thing happened. Instead of giving me energy, it brought my energy way down. I don't know what ingredient caused this. Since I'm used to taking a lot of supplements, I thought maybe it's one of the amino acids. I'm also thinking that perhaps this product is designed more to benefit someone with a condition (CFS,Fibromyalgia, etc). But for those who do not have a condition, perhaps it's overload in some way. I don't know.

I'm returning it and now back to my regular supplements.

I advise you to try it yourself and see how your body reacts. All of the positive reviews can't be wrong.

title: Does what it says but cheapo quality makes it worth no more than $10 - seriously!
text:
Fit and function are great, this knee compression wrap does exactly what they claim. The workmanship (assembled in Taiwan) is pretty good, and in theory, you need this wrap to put the cold therapy just where you need it. Like most of the Active Ice system I bought at the same time, this compression wrap is made using cheapo materials - it is definitely NOT worth $30. I would feel much less ripped off if I'd paid $10 or maybe even $15 - but no more. Someone is making a killing on Polar Products - - top dollar for cheap products.

I'd guess there are about $5 worth of thin foam-backed polyester material, sewn-in velcro hook patches, and three decent elastic bands. Five sewn-in velcro patches attach to the hoop material on the universal chilling bladder that came with your system. The velcro sticks well and the elastic bands look like they will last longer than the cheapo material the body was made from. Overall, the whole thing weighs just a couple of ounces - very light duty. The thin foam/polyester material is exactly the same junk they used in the control box to "insulate" the cold water pipes. (which is still leaking condensation/water through every hole and crack in the control box)

I wore the universal bladder and my new knee compression wrap today for a few hours off and on. I can tell you that if you have fresh staples across your knee, any sensitivity in the knee area, or are easily chafed by rough things against your skin, the stiffness of this compression wrap, bladder, velcro, and elastic will cause you some additional soreness until you're used to it.

Bottom line - I would not buy it again unless they cut the price in half. Yes, it's really that over-priced. Best solution is really just to use the black universal strap with velcro ends to hold your chill bladder in place. If that's not enough, use another Ace bandage. You should be using one under the bladder also, since the bladder can't go against the skin.

title: Fabulous for giving Tramadol to a small dog!!
text: I've always been able to give meds to my animals up to and including cats until my very senior dachshund needed Tramadol.  It seriously must be the most bitter medication in the world. Bless him, he is now deceased (at almost 19 yrs old) but he had teeth from the front all the way to his tail!  He never would bite us but he wouldn't open those jaws to save his live.  I ended up giving it transdermally on his ear until he died.  Now I have his 18 yrs old son requiring the med.  I guess when you live to be that old, you're entitled.  I never thought he'd be an issue as he ate everything.  Ha! Was I ever wrong.  He had the same great teeth as his dad and was just as stubborn.  During my reading on Amazon, I discovered these little jewels and man are they a life saver!!!  I take one of those pills, but it in half length length-wise and then put it in one of these capsules twice a day in a spoonful of canned dog food and zip it gets snarfed up.  He never even thinks about smelling, biting or tasting that pill.  If you have a small dog that is difficult to pill, these are the best thing since slice bread.  I bought a pill popper and haven't had to use it because these work so well.  The pill pockets he bit into so I plan on using these as long as he needs the Tramadol!

title: An answer to our pill problem
text: We have a cat that needs to take a bitter pill every evening and it is always a problem getting her to take it.  If she doesn't swallow it immediately (by using the previous method of wrapping it in a food coating for pills) it makes her foam at the mouth because of the taste.  The pills are larger than she needs so they have to be split into four which then leave the bitter part of the pill exposed to her taste buds if she doesn't swallow it right down.  The quarter of the pill will fit into this size empty gelatin capsules.  Then using a pill popper she swallows the capsule right down.  It used to take both me and my wife to get the pills down the cat - now one person can accomplish the task.  What a better solution and the price is very reasonable!
